docs.title: Production MAWster
docs.text:
The production calendar + contacts app. ClickUp AUTHORS, this app RENDERS.

Next session opens ONE page

[Print-first Runbook] — the print path is fully designed and was entirely unbuilt as of 08-09, and every session since 08-08 built the layer that FEEDS the calendar instead of the calendar. The runbook inverts that order and ends in a PDF. ⚠️ The counts this callout used to quote (36 tables / 0 relationships / 0 layouts) are STALE — the 2026-08-15 DDR reports 37 tables · 15 relationships · 54 layouts · 10 custom functions, and scripts exist. Re-read a DDR before quoting any structural number.

docs.text: Naming conventions for this app. Names lock before any calc queries them by name.

docs.title: Naming
docs.text:
Convention Pattern Example Primary keys PrimaryKey, UUID, never serial ⚠️ Diverges from house pk_ prefix (open governance item) Foreign keys fk<Parent> fkProduction, fkCalendar, fkStandardEvent Dates date_ prefix date_FirstRehearsal, date_NeededLast Booleans bool_ prefix bool_AddPreProWeek, bool_IsScratch Calculations calc_ prefix calc_TotalOutstanding Overrides ovr_ prefix ovr_OutputSize — empty means INHERIT from the parent Integration keys cu prefix, camel, no underscore cuProductionToken, cuProductionID Globals g_ prefix; gLIST_ for value-list globals g_currentProduction, gLIST_PropertyNames Audit fields PrimaryKey, CreationTimestamp, CreatedBy, ModificationTimestamp, ModifiedBy Every table, including a singleton No leading underscores Active core tables only Legacy GLOBAL_, XXval_, old... gets stripped Value list vs table Metadata beyond display value → table Location type = value list until it earns SortOrder; event type (carries skin + report role) = STANDARD_EVENTS

⚠️ date_, bool_, ovr_ and cu were added 2026-08-08 from live practice. This page had documented only calc_, g_ and fk while the build was already using the others — the doc lost to the diff.

docs.title: Why names lock before SQL
docs.text: ExecuteSQL embeds table and field names as text. Rename a table and the calc returns empty, not error.

docs.title: Field-menu conventions (the .tsv side)
docs.text:
• The first column is a confirmation state ({.conf} / {.tbc}), not a sort ordinal. A field menu is a build tracker, not a static list.
  • Columns mirror FileMaker's own field dialog: Field_Name · Type · Options · Notes.
  • Sections are bare singular rows: NORMALIZED FIELDS · INTEGRATION KEYS · RELATIONSHIP · CHILDREN · AUDIT FIELDS, closed by - EOF -.
  • Audit fields are spelled out, not pointed at — you cannot check off a pointer while sitting in the field dialog.
  • TABLE.tsv is uppercase (it is the FMP table name); table.md is lowercase (it is a document).

docs.title: DDR punch list
docs.text:
58 rows from the 2026-08-15 DDR re-audit. Supersedes the 42-row Aug-9 list. Tick them off.

Every finding from the DDR read of Production_MAWnster.fmp12 at 2026-08-15 16:50 — 37 tables, 15 relationships, 52 scripts, 54 layouts, 14 value lists, 10 custom functions.

🔴 This SUPERSEDES the 42-row list of 2026-08-09. That audit ran against a 29-table file with zero relationships and zero scripts, so everything join-side and script-side postdates it entirely. Every one of its 42 rows was re-checked against the live schema; none were dropped silently. See Reconciliation below.

docs.title: The tally — 58 rows
docs.text:
Count Meaning 🔴 26 21 schema/script + 5 repo items carried unverified ⚠️ 28 free now, expensive later ⬜ 4 needs a decision first 58 32 carried from Aug 9 + 26 new

Of the 26 red, SIX corrupt data in flight (rows 1–6). Those six are the ones that write a wrong value into a real record every time they run. Everything else red either blocks something downstream or has two surfaces claiming one fact.

⭐ Read the ratio, not just the count. 58 findings against roughly 543 built objects (398 fields, 52 scripts, 54 layouts, 15 relationships, 14 value lists, 10 custom functions) is about 11%, and only 1% corrupts data. For a file that went from 29 tables and no scripts to this in one week, that is a low defect rate. The build is sound; the defects cluster. Which is the more useful finding — see the pattern below.

🔴 CORRECTED 2026-08-16, same day this list shipped. The first version of this file said "the four defects that corrupt data in flight are 1–6" directly above a section headed "The five that would cost the most" — three different numbers for one set, in adjacent paragraphs. It read as "only 6 flags" and it undercounted the list by an order of magnitude. That is the same species of undocumented arithmetic this list flags in the schema (rows 25, 26, 27, 44), so it is corrected in place and recorded rather than quietly swapped.

docs.title: ⚠️ The source DDR no longer exists
docs.text:
The Aug-15 export was captured into the _ide mirrors and then deleted, per the staging rule. Recovery coordinates and full coverage table: 90-file-imports-temp/DDR_imports/README.md. Last commit containing it: d5745a9.

🔴 The Aug-9 list cited DDR_imports/202608090053.md, which is also gone and has no recovery SHA recorded — it was deleted outside the capture process. That is why the tombstone log now exists. Every finding below is instead traceable to a live _ide mirror, not to a dead path:

Evidence for Lives in Tables + fields, 398 of 398 20-tables/_ide/ · register at observations.md Relationships, 15 of 15 30-RELATIONSHIPS/_ide/ Scripts, 52 of 52 verbatim 70-scripts/_ide/ Value lists, 14 of 14 25-value-lists/_ide/ Custom function signatures 60-custom-functions/_ide/ Layouts, 54 of 54 50-LAYOUTS/_ide/

How to use it

Open the .tsv in a spreadsheet, put anything in Done, save, push. One row is one fix. If a row needs a conversation it is ⬜, not 🔴. Origin reads A9-6 (Aug-9 row 6, still open) or A15 (found in this audit).

docs.title: ⭐ Ordered by dependency, not severity
docs.text:
Unchanged principle. The import pipeline now runs end to end and writes wrong values, so the six data-corrupting defects are rows 1–6 and every cosmetic item is at the bottom. Tier carries severity separately, so sorting by it still works.

Tier Means 🔴 Blocks something downstream, or two surfaces claim one fact, or it silently writes a wrong value ⚠️ Free right now, expensive after more records exist ⬜ Needs a decision before it can be a task

docs.title: The six that corrupt data in flight — rows 1–6
docs.text:
• import \| merge Event reads four wrong JSON keys (row 1). The payload emits Name, dateTime_Start, dateTime_End, fkStyle; the merge branch asks for EventName, dateTime_start, dateTime_end, StyleKey. Two differ by letter case only. ParamGetText returns the fallback on a missing key, so merge writes "err" into the name and both dates. import \| net new Event reads all nine correctly — so net-new works and merge is broken, which is exactly the split that looks like "merge is flaky" rather than "merge is wrong."
  • hash_history failure INVERTED (row 2). Aug 9 it was fkProduction & "." & fkStandardEvent — byte-identical every run, so nothing ever looked changed. It is now cu_TaskID & "." & fkUtilityReport. fkUtilityReport is new on every run, so the hash now differs every time and everything looks changed. The formula moved; the defect swapped ends.
  • EVENTS::hash_current copies it (row 3), so change detection is dead end to end in whichever direction row 2 currently fails.
  • calc_ResolvedEnd still reads dateTime_Start (row 4). This was row 6 on the Aug-9 list. It is one week old. Both resolved calcs read Start, so every emphasis span resolves to zero length. Same bug species as the legacy RGB ( $R ; $G ; $R ). CALENDAR_HIGHLIGHTS has 0 records, which is the only reason nobody has seen it.
  • Both calc_Resolved* are typed Calculated, Number (row 5) while holding dates, so a Number result on a date calc returns the serial.
  • THEME_COLORS::calc_Hex is view_THEME_COLORS::R alone (row 6). G and B are not in the expression.

docs.title: 🔴 The pattern, which is worth more than any single row
docs.text:
Three separate fields build a multi-argument value out of one argument: legacy RGB ( $R ; $G ; $R ), calc_ResolvedEnd reading Start, and calc_Hex reading only R. Three instances is a pattern, not three slips. All three are silent — they return a plausible value of the right type, so nothing errors and nothing looks wrong until someone compares output to intent.

And the second pattern, which only became visible once scripts existed: writers and readers disagreeing. A script setting "New" into a field whose own comment names three other values. A script setting the string "0" into a Number field commented Get(LastError). Three counters no script increments. A timestamp nothing stamps. A field name that does not exist. Nine of the 26 new rows are this shape, and none of them are schema-shape problems — the schema is fine, the contract between the two halves is not.

If only two things get fixed this week: row 1 (merge writes "err" into live records now) and row 18 (the rename wave broke every @table-* doc id).

docs.title: Reconciliation — all 42 Aug-9 rows accounted for
docs.text:
Outcome Count Rows ✅ Closed 4 11, 12, 19, 20 🔄 Partially fixed, re-scoped 6 8, 17, 18, 33, 34, 37 🔴 Still open, verified in the live schema 27 1–7, 9, 10, 13–16, 21–32, 35, 36 ⚠️ Carried, NOT re-verified 5 38–42

Closed: fkImportSssion and fkImportSesseion (11, 12) both vanished when the import tables moved to the UTILITY_* model — fixed by rename, not by correction. g_pkDefault_PRINT_SET (19) was deleted outright, and the lesson landed: the two new globals in VALUE_LISTS carry proper Storage: Global. ROLES::fkPerson (20) is gone.

🔴 Rows 38–42 are repo, renderer and GitHub-token items. A DDR says nothing about repo trees, so they could not be re-verified from this audit and are carried forward unchanged. They are marked A9-38…A9-42 with tier intact. Do not read their presence as confirmation they are still broken, or their silence as confirmation they are fixed. They need a separate pass.

docs.title: 🔴 A rename wave happened between the two audits, and it invalidates doc ids
docs.text:
The Aug-9 list is written in the old vocabulary. Six tables were renamed:

Aug 9 Aug 15 PRODUCTION_CALENDARS CALENDARS CALENDAR_HIGHLIGHT CALENDAR_HIGHLIGHTS EVENTS_WORKDAYS EVENTS_X_WORKDAYS PRINT_SETS EXPORT_SETS PRINT_PRESETS EXPORT_PRESETS PRINT_SET_ITEMS EXPORT_SET_ITEMS IMPORT_SESSIONS UTILITY_SESSIONS

⚠️ That table lists SEVEN renames under a heading that says six. Counted from the DDR: seven rows, seven renames. The heading is the error, kept visible for one revision because this file just shipped with three contradictory counts in it and silently fixing the next one would teach the wrong lesson. Seven.

This is why row 18 (doc name vs build name) is now the highest-leverage cleanup on the list, not a tidy-up. Every @table-* id in the doc tree is wired to the left column. The rename also left three PRINT ghosts in the schema: EXPORT_PRESETS's only occurrence is view_PRINT_PRESETS, and both EXPORT_SET_ITEMS::fkPrintSet and EXPORT_SESSIONS::fkPrintSet still say PrintSet while pointing at EXPORT_SETS.

docs.title: ⚠️ Two Aug-9 rows need re-deciding, not just re-doing
docs.text:
• Row 4/5 (stored date-only fields on EVENTS) were written when spans were to be compared directly. The architecture changed: button | generate events x workdays now projects one EVENTS_X_WORKDAYS row per day, and the join is Date = Date on that table. The original fix may be the wrong fix now. Kept as A9-4 at 🔴 because EVENTS::dateTime_Start/_End are still Indexing: None while both partners on that join are All, but read it as a question.
  • Row 30 (CALENDAR_HIGHLIGHT → CALENDAR_EMPHASIS) drifted the wrong way — it pluralized to CALENDAR_HIGHLIGHTS instead. But emphasis is now a live STYLES::vl_Domain value, and CALENDAR_HIGHLIGHTS::fkStyle is commented "STYLES row, domain emphasis." The word is taken by a different concept now, so the Aug-9 ruling deserves a second look before anyone renames a table to collide with it. Now ⬜, not ⚠️.

docs.title: What this audit found that Aug 9 could not
docs.text:
The Aug-9 file had no scripts and no relationships, so nothing below was observable then. 26 new rows.

  • Nothing writes UTILITY_SESSIONS::countRows_File / _Imported / _Flagged (row 12). All three sit on the Import New Events layout, permanently blank. This is the second half of Aug-9 row 28: the token cannot land and the counter has no writer.
  • Nothing writes APP_SESSIONS::ClosedTimestamp (row 20), and the only script that writes StartTimestamp is trigger_App_Open, which has no caller — File Options binds OnFirstWindowOpen to on App Open instead. The live session token lives in a global and never touches the table. It holds 2 records.
  • new \| Utility Log writes "open" into a field that does not exist (row 7). Set Field [ view_UTILITY_LOGS::<Field Missing>; "open" ] is a live step. UTILITY_LOGS has 13 fields and none holds state. The open | close value list exists and is bound to nothing. 4,939 rows have been written through this script with that step failing.
  • UTILITY_LOGS::ErrorCode is set to the string "0" on every call and by nothing else (row 33), into a Normal, Number field. Its comment says Get(LastError) from the failing step. No failing step's error can reach it.
  • UTILITY_REPORTS::vl_Status is set to "New" (row 34) — not one of the three values its own comment names (complete | partial | failed).
  • EXPORT_SET_ITEMS has ten of fifteen fields on no layout and zero relationships (row 47). Fully specified in fields and comments, entirely unwired.
  • Four layout names are each used twice (row 39), and every Go to Layout resolves by name only. Worst case: table | EVENTS exists twice — one instance has zero objects, the other has 12 fields and a button bar.

✅ Three Aug-14 script defects were fixed by Aug 15 and are recorded here only so nobody re-files them: import | pass to workspace had an unassigned $result and read Get(ScriptParameter) where it wanted Get(ScriptResult); it tested "new new" against a returned "net new"; and lookup | calendar for production had an empty Set Field. All three now read correctly. import | net new Event also went from a two-line stub to fully written.

docs.title: Not in here
docs.text:
• Open questions and rulings live in the Decision Log, not on a punch list.
  • ⭐ What landed right is still not itemised, same reason as before: a punch list that also lists wins stops being a punch list. The ratio in the tally above is the one exception — a defect count with no denominator reads as a verdict on the build, which would be wrong. The counter-examples themselves are recorded where they belong, in 20-tables/_ide/observations.md: IMPORT_EVENTS's six-field date/time calc family IS correctly wired, and UTILITY_REPORTS::bool_Pass is the one boolean whose comment and options agree.
  • Layout object geometry. Not captured from the Aug-15 DDR by ruling ("dont need the loayout objects yet"), so no row here concerns field placement. Print geometry is not auditable from the mirrors.

docs.title: ⚠️ One structural note on this file
docs.text:
The .tsv gained an Origin column. Six columns, not five. It is the only way a row can say "this was found a week ago and is still here" without that fact living in prose nobody re-reads. If the renderer is column-count sensitive, that is the change to look at.

docs.title: Device Handoff
docs.text: MAW Prose · Fall 2026

docs.title: Device handoff — the open-log
docs.text:
One file, three devices. The file is never open twice — it just never SAYS which copy is current. A display problem, not a sync problem.

🔒 SINGLE-FILE LOCKED 2026-08-08 (Michael): "kinda want to keep it all in one… I've not really had issues with the transferring up to this point and I design MOSTLY for interaction on my iPad — it's slick."

That ruling shrank this doc's job to one sentence: the file never says which copy is current. Not a sync problem, not a version-control problem. A display problem. Everything below either serves that or is marked speculative.

Ruling Effect One file, no UI/DATA split separation → [revisit block], not queued Transfer has not been painful Tiers 1–3 DEMOTED to speculative iPad is the PRIMARY interaction surface mobile read-only is dead; layouts target iPad

docs.title: The existing workflow is already a checkout protocol
docs.text:
Habit Protocol equivalent download the file onto the device checkout share-sheet it back off the device check-in never open it in two places the lease iCloud between work laptop and home laptop, sequential the transfer — and it works

It runs in Michael's head, and it runs fine. The only thing memory genuinely cannot do is "it's not clear what's open elsewhere." That is the entire build.

docs.title: ⬜ THE BUILD — Tier 0 + the landing page
0a · File-level stamp — three fields, one trigger, no relationships
docs.text:
On 00_APP (the single-record app-state row):

Field Type Written by LastOpenedAt Timestamp OnFirstWindowOpen LastOpenedDevice Text OnFirstWindowOpen LastOpenedPlatform Text OnFirstWindowOpen 
Set Field [ 00_APP::LastOpenedAt       ; Get ( CurrentTimeStamp ) ]
Set Field [ 00_APP::LastOpenedDevice   ; Get ( SystemNVLTargetName ) ]
Set Field [ 00_APP::LastOpenedPlatform ; Get ( Device ) ]

Open any copy on any device and it tells you where that copy last lived. A copy on the work laptop last opened on the iPad two hours ago is visibly the stale one.

Rule Failure mode if broken Stamp on OPEN, not on close A crash or force-quit never writes a close. Open always fires. Never treat the stamp as a LOCK It is a sign, not a gate. It reports; it does not prevent. Verify Get ( Device ) return values against current docs Return integers get quoted from memory constantly, and are wrong about as often.

⚠️ Get ( SystemNVLTargetName ) is unverified on FileMaker Go. Fallback: a one-time manual device picker written to a global on first open per device.

docs.title: 0b · Record-level state — a FOLD-IN, plus exactly one new field
docs.text:
Four of these already exist as a fleet convention (see Departments, Fiscal_Years and others in URITP Global Setup). Formalize them on every canonical table, and add the fifth:

Field Auto-enter Native? CreationTimestamp Creation → Timestamp ✅ built in CreatedBy Creation → Account Name ✅ built in ModificationTimestamp Modification → Timestamp ✅ built in ModifiedBy Modification → Account Name ✅ built in ModifiedOnDevice Calculated value, "do not replace" UNCHECKED 🆕 the only new one

FileMaker has no native "which device modified this," so ModifiedOnDevice is an auto-enter calculated value with do not replace existing value left unchecked, so it re-stamps on every edit. Feed it the same value 0a resolves, ideally through one global set at open so both agree.

docs.title: ⭐ Why this is the highest-value field in the build
docs.text:
It automates the audit Michael already does by hand. His words: "reopen it on my Mac and audit it." With ModifiedOnDevice on every table, that audit becomes a query — show me every record touched on the iPad since this file was last opened on a laptop. The manual read-through stops being necessary.

It also degrades gracefully: even if the landing page is never built, the fields alone make the question answerable from a Find.

docs.title: 0c · The landing page
docs.text: One home layout, iPad-first, showing: the file-level stamp, counts of recently-touched records per table, and anything flagged for review.

docs.title: 🔴 The rule that decides whether this layout is fast or unusable
docs.text:
No live unstored aggregate calcs and no summary fields on this layout. They recalculate on record load, throw the Summarizing… progress dialog, and are a documented cause of catastrophic open times — including a case of a file taking 15 minutes to open on a one-record layout, diagnosed to aggregate calcs and summary fields (thread).

Instead, CACHE: a script writes plain number fields on 00_APP at open, the layout displays those, and a visible counts as of <timestamp> line plus a manual Refresh button keeps it honest (caching pattern). A stale-but-labelled number beats a live number that costs 15 seconds a tap.

docs.title: iPad-first, because that is the primary surface
docs.text:
Michael designs on desktop (Go cannot edit layouts) but lives on iPad. So:

  • build and measure at iPad dimensions, not desktop-then-shrink
  • no hover states — they do not exist on touch
  • popovers and Card windows over dialogs — dialogs are hostile on touch
  • generous touch targets; buttons sized for a thumb, not a cursor
  • test on the device, because the design surface and the use surface are different machines

⚠️ Layout geometry and the print seam are their own subject: [Print & iPad Geometry]. Pure look-and-feel belongs in [UX]. This doc owns only the STATE the landing page displays.

docs.title: ⬜ Open — what "database state" means
docs.text:
Michael said "tagging of records or database state" and those are two different builds. Not guessing:

  1. File-level mode — one field on 00_APP (clean / working / needs-audit), set manually or by script. Answers "is this copy trustworthy."
  2. Record-level lifecycle — a status field per record (draft / confirmed / needs-review), which is domain state and belongs with each table's own design.

0b above delivers neither; it delivers provenance (who, when, where), which is the prerequisite for both.

docs.title: 💤 Speculative — Tiers 1–3 (demoted 2026-08-08)
docs.text:
These solved a problem Michael does not have. Kept because the reasoning is sound and the constraints are real, not because they are queued.

Tier Idea Why it is parked 1 Mobile leg to Dropbox; iCloud stays for laptop↔laptop Dropbox is the only leg with an HTTP API Insert from URL can call, so it is the precondition for ANY pull automation. But the transfer has not hurt. 2 MAW_Launch.fmp12 per device — build stamps + a Pull newest button Blocked on an untested device claim (below). Nice, not needed. 3 APPS · APP_BUILDS · APP_CHECKOUTS · DEVICES · SYNC_EVENTS Tier 0 answers most of what it would report. APPS also duplicates VERSIONS.md + the URITP fmp Solutions list.

Constraints that stay true regardless:

  • 🚫 Push is never scriptable. FileMaker Go cannot export to FMP12 at all, so moving a file off an iPad is an iOS share-sheet operation FileMaker cannot see or trigger.
  • ⚠️ Validate any download. Insert from URL succeeds at storing whatever came back — a 404 page and a wrong MIME type both land in a container looking fine. GetContainerAttribute ( … ; "fileSize" ) and "MD5" make the check two lines.
  • ⚠️ Untested: the launch token (fmp://~/ vs fmp://$/) on current Go, and whether Export Field Contents can write where Go actually browses (a 2024 report has AirDropped .fmp12 files landing in an iOS Downloads folder Go cannot see).
  • A registry can never live inside the app it tracks, or you must open the stale copy to learn it is stale.
  • Open-state should be a relationship, not a stored flag — constant calc cOutFlag = "out" matched against APP_CHECKOUTS::State on a second TO, then not IsEmpty ( … ) unstored. Derived state cannot go stale, same law as the [Projection Law].

docs.title: 🚫 Never on the table
docs.text: Not doing Why Merge / conflict resolution .fmp12 is opaque binary. No diff, no merge, not ever. Two edited copies = pick one, retype the other. A pull-request UI It would be a merge surface that can never merge. Hosting / serving Out of scope by ruling. Automated push from mobile Platform impossibility. Mobile read-only privilege set ⛔ Killed 2026-08-08 — the iPad is the primary interaction surface.

docs.title: 🪦 If we ever revisit separation
docs.text:
Rejected 2026-08-08 (Q10 → no). Splitting into a records-free UI file + a DATA file makes version push idempotent, because a file with no records cannot lose work when overwritten. It was rejected for a good reason, kept for a better one: the reasoning is what stops it being re-proposed cold.

Why it lost: the payoff is desktop-shaped and the risk is mobile-shaped, and mobile is where Michael works. A local separated pair on FileMaker Go is the least-proven deployment of the pattern — separation normally pairs with hosting. Documented breakage: a local pair working on Go 18.0.3.325 and the data file silently failing to open on 19.5.2.200 (thread); same-folder auto-open breaking on FM19 desktop (thread); Go returning error 100 on a file:-prefixed path and possibly being case-sensitive on filenames (thread).

Architectural principle worth keeping even though the pattern lost: Open URL [ "fmp://…" ] is loose coupling — launch and walk away. An external data source reference is a hard runtime dependency re-resolved on every open. On Go, prefer loose.

The four things that would bite, if it is ever reconsidered:

  1. Keep table-occurrence names identical. Everything addresses fields as TOName::fieldName, so same-named external TOs mean most references survive untouched. Renaming during the split means re-touching the whole solution.
  2. Accounts must exist in both files with matching name + password, or every open prompts. Read-only would have to be enforced in DATA — UI privileges cannot stop an edit on records that are not there.
  3. Get ( FileName ) / Get ( FilePath ) start describing the UI file, silently breaking any script that builds a path or an fmp:// link from them.
  4. Filename stability becomes load-bearing — and iOS appends 2 to duplicates, which breaks the reference instantly.

Also: keep ALL scripts in one file (cross-file Perform Script on Go fails with error 100 until the target has been opened manually once), and the UI file must hold zero records forever — the sneaky violation is a value-list source or preferences table, and it silently destroys the entire payoff.

docs.title: Document Templates
docs.text: MAW Prose · Fall 2026

docs.title: Document Templates
docs.text:
Documents are templates. Each one declares which roles and events canonically belong on it.

Grain

One STANDARD_DOCS row per document TYPE. One DOC_ROLES row per (document × role).

Michael, 2026-08-09: "the whole point of this endeavor is that our documents become templates. Standard docs will be templatized so that every event and every document lists which roles or events canonically belong there. For instance, an info sheet will specify that it typically includes the director, stage manager, and designer running tech, while a crew call calendar will look much different."

That is the app's purpose, and it is what STANDARD_DOCS is for. It is also what EXPORT_SET_ITEMS::fkDocument has been pointing at since the table was written — the comment "back to the canonical DOC index. Decides WHICH overrides apply" had no referent until this was stated.

docs.title: The join already exists, fused onto ROLES
docs.text:
🔴 ROLES::Contact Sheet HEADER (in ClickUp) is named for the document it serves. Creatives · Program · CAST · Shop Staffs · STAGE MANAGERS is not a property of a role. It is which section of ONE SPECIFIC DOCUMENT that role prints under.

It works today because there is one document. It breaks at document two, because a crew call's sections are not a contact sheet's sections and the field can only hold one answer.

⭐ Third instance of this shape found in a single day, alongside STYLES (already a theme, the default one, unnamed) and ROLES::CALLS (already an event join, stored as text). In all three the tell was the same: a field named after the only instance that existed.

docs.title: The tables
docs.text:
STANDARD_DOCS ......... one row per DOCUMENT TYPE
  Name .............. "Info Sheet" · "Crew Call Calendar" · "Contact Sheet"
  Sort · Description
  fkLayout .......... ⬜ hypothesis: → auto_LAYOUTS. see below

DOC_ROLES ............. one row per (DOC × ROLE)
  fkDoc · fkRole .... both indexed
  SectionHeader ..... where Contact Sheet HEADER goes
  Sort .............. empty = inherit ROLES::Sort
  bool_Required ..... expected, vs merely permitted
  bool_Seeded ....... machine-proposed?
  bool_Reviewed ..... has a human blessed it?

Sort belongs on the JOIN, not the role. A crew call sorts run crew to the top; a program sorts artistic staff first. One-per-(doc × role) — the same grain test that settles every placement argument in this app. ROLES::Sort stays as the global default and the join overrides it; empty means inherit, per the house pattern.

docs.title: AUTHORED, with the query as a seeding tool
docs.text: Ruled by Michael, 2026-08-09. DOC_ROLES rows are real records a human owns. The query proposes; it never governs.

docs.title: 🔴 The seeder runs ONCE per (doc × role), ever
docs.text:
It is a create-if-absent pass, never an update pass. It proposes rows that do not exist and never revisits one that does. The moment "re-seed" comes to mean "re-derive," every hand edit is gone and AUTHORED stopped being true.

⭐ And the deletion is worse than the edit. A hand-added Video Designer has no rule behind it — that is exactly why a human added it. A re-derive removes it as not matching, which reads as the system being clever and is the system discarding the only information it did not already have.

State Meaning Machine may touch? Seeded, unreviewed proposed by the query ✅ yes — re-derive or drop Authored a human made or blessed it 🚫 never Diverged seeded, then hand-edited 🚫 never — authored from that moment

docs.title: What the seeder reads
docs.text:
For a contact sheet: every role carrying a Contact Sheet HEADER, section pre-filled. For a crew call: every role whose CALLS contains that event type.

⭐ The multi-value fields are perfectly good SEED SOURCES even though they are bad JOIN KEYS. A seed source is read once by a script; a join key is read on every render. Only the second has to be clean — which retires most of the pressure to unfuse CALLS into an EVENT_ROLES table right now.

docs.title: A template is an EXPECTATION, not a filter
docs.text:
What prints is the intersection of what the template declares and what the production actually assigned. The difference between those two sets is the most useful report in the app.

It fails in three ways and only the first is visible:

  1. Declared but unassigned — the info sheet expects an LD, this show has none. A blank line on the page.
  2. 🔴 Assigned but undeclared — the show HAS a Video Designer, no template lists one, so they are silently absent from the paperwork. No blank, no error, nothing to notice.
  3. 🔴 A role in NO template at all — added in ClickUp, declared nowhere, will never print. This one is created by the authored ruling (the seeder does not revisit), and it is the honest price of not letting a rule overwrite judgement.

All three belong in the completeness report. ⭐ Same shape as the EXPECTED_ASSIGNMENTS vs COMPLETIONS model already ruled for URITP Safety Programs — expected rows generated, actual rows imported, the mismatch is the product. Second app, arrived at independently.

docs.title: Consequence for the first build
docs.text: A brand-new template starts EMPTY, and that is correct. Seed, review, edit. The template is trustworthy only because a human signed it — a query-governed doc set looks identical on day one and drifts apart by October.

docs.title: ⬜ Open
docs.text:
• STANDARD_DOCS::fkLayout → auto_LAYOUTS — hypothesis, not a finding. A document template must know which layout renders it, and this would make the layout registry load-bearing rather than decorative. If true, the upsert-never-rebuild rule on auto_LAYOUTS gains a real dependency: deleting and recreating those rows would orphan every template.
  • EVENT_ROLES — the event half of the same unfuse. Not forced yet; DOC_ROLES is, because of the Contact Sheet HEADER collision. They are one pattern and must not get solved two different ways.
  • Multi-value sections — Contact Sheet HEADER already holds "STAGE MANAGERS, Run Crew" on the PSM. Under DOC_ROLES that is two rows, which resolves it cleanly. Confirm no document needs one role printing twice within itself.

docs.title: Sources
docs.text:
Canonical role data: URITP CRM ▸ CONTACT SHEETS ▸ SHOW ROLES, fully populated, nine custom fields per role. Rulings: Production MAWster FMP — Decision Log J10 and J11.

docs.title: ClickUp Integration
docs.text: MAW Prose · Fall 2026

docs.title: ClickUp Integration
docs.text: ClickUp AUTHORS. This app RENDERS. The list is the work; the PDF is the byproduct.

docs.title: The pipe
docs.text:
• CSV first, API second. Same fields serve both — no migration.
  • The VIEW is the contract. A saved ClickUp view is a stable, human-editable integration surface: change what gets published without touching a script.
  • One session = one production (see [import_SESSIONS]).

docs.title: Views are per-LIST
docs.text:
• A view lives on one list and carries its own filter. So "Big Love events" is a saved view built once.
  • Cost: one saved view per production. Manual upkeep at 7+ shows, and a new show means a new view before the first import.

docs.title: ⬜ TO-DO — one view, production passed as a PARAMETER at pull time
docs.text:
Wanted. Replaces N per-production views with ONE view plus a runtime filter argument.

  • API only. A CSV export is a static file; there is no parameter to pass.
  • So the per-production views are the CSV-era stopgap, and this is what retires them.
  • Blocks nothing today: cuProductionID is already on [PRODUCTIONS] waiting for it.

docs.title: Join keys
docs.text:
Key Transport Note cuProductionToken CSV + API Exact label string. A rename in ClickUp breaks it SILENTLY cuProductionID API only Rename-proof. Empty until the pull exists
  • Operator declares the production at import. Non-resolving rows get flagged, never silently filed.

docs.title: ⬜ Open
docs.text:
• ⬜ Multi-label exposure. URITP Productions is multi-select, so one event task can carry two shows. Handled by per-production views + a compound upsert key — verify against a live CSV.
  • ⬜ Do CSV multi-value labels come back comma-separated inside one quoted cell, and do any show titles contain commas?
  • ⬜ Event classification: a CU-side canonical-type dropdown was declined, so a crosswalk (raw name → fkStandardEvent) with an unmatched queue carries it. Learns instead of guessing.
  • ⬜ ClickUp does not emit a LOCATION on an event task today. Ruled 2026-08-08: not going there yet, but [LOCATIONS] is built so it can.
  • ⬜ Crew calls — third document, or a view of the calendar? A call carries person, role, call time, report location.

docs.title: Print-first Runbook
docs.text: MAW Prose · Fall 2026

docs.title: MAWster Print-first Runbook
docs.text:
The only page to open next session. Four stages, two PDFs, and a list of everything you are not allowed to touch until a page prints.

Read this paragraph or the runbook does not work

36 tables, 0 relationships, 0 layouts (DDR 202608091643). The print path is fully designed and entirely unbuilt. Every session since 08-08 went into the layer that FEEDS the calendar instead of the calendar. This page inverts that order and it only works if the Do-Not-Touch list is obeyed. If a session touches anything on that list before a page prints, it has repeated the mistake this runbook exists to fix.

Target: two PDFs. An ugly vertical date list at the end of Stage 2, and the week grid at the end of Stage 4. Everything here is already specced elsewhere — [Print & iPad Geometry] holds the geometry and the build checklist, [Relationships] holds the graph plan, 50-LAYOUTS/LAYOUTS.tsv names the layouts. Read, do not redesign.

docs.title: Stage 0 · Decided, do not re-litigate (5 min)
docs.text: Two forks that would otherwise eat the first twenty minutes. Both are Fiona's calls, 2026-08-13.

docs.title: 0.1 · The calendar-scope predicate Confirmed
docs.text:
A relationship matches two occurrences only, so the parent side needs a field holding the current calendar. Resolution: the global is reached from the ANCHOR as an unstored calc — not stored on WORKDAYS, not a portal filter.

  1. Cartesian (×) buoy from the grid anchor to GLOBAL_USE.
  2. Unstored calculation Calculation on the anchor returning GLOBAL_USE::g_pkCurrentCalendar Global.
  3. Use that calc as the parent-side match field. Parent-side match fields may be unstored; only the child side (EVENTS::fkCalendar) needs an index.

Verify this resolves before building on it

Five minutes in the file. If FileMaker refuses the unstored calc as a match field through a Cartesian buoy, fall back to a plain global field on the anchor and write that down.

Never the portal filter

It filters DISPLAY only, so found sets and reports lie.

Apply the same answer to STYLES_ACTIVE and STYLES_HOUSE. The relationships index says decide once for all three. This is the once.

docs.title: 0.2 · WEEKS is the print anchor To be confirmed
docs.text:
J8 parked WEEKS "with no known job"; J19 killed fkWeek fkCal. For an old VALUE rather than an old name, use was.">Former name "until a report that groups BY week." The month grid IS that report. print-geometry requires seven day-portals side by side in one week row with also resize enclosing part, so the layout body part must be one record per week. That is WEEKS.

This is a proposal against a parked ruling

It needs Michael's yes before fields are added to WEEKS — but it is the only shape that satisfies the print spec, so treat "WEEKS is dead" as retired and do not re-park it.

docs.title: Stage 1 · Import — get 115 rows into EVENTS (~20 min)
docs.text:
The landed set is already there: 117 records, 115 real events, 5/1 → 10/18/2026 in import_EVENTS.

  1. EVENTS::fkProduction — add the index. Its own field comment claims "Indexed" and it is not. Sixth flag, and it is a match field in Stage 2, so it stops being a nuisance and starts being a blocker here.
  2. Move the rows into EVENTS by hand — internal import, import_EVENTS → EVENTS, mapping by name.
  3. Skip the two junk rows (blank record #1, header-as-record #2) and keep the three dateless rows — Paper Tech, LX Hang prep, SET Risers are the legacy UNSCHEDULED bucket, not garbage.
  4. Stamp fkCalendar on all of them. One calendar exists; set it once by Replace Field Contents.

Do NOT wait for BUILD · Upsert Events to be written

The chain does not have to be finished for the data to be in the table, and this is the single decision that unblocks the whole page.

Stop condition: EVENTS shows ~115 records with dates and a calendar key. Nothing else about EVENTS matters yet.

docs.title: Stage 2 · WORKDAYS — the ugly PDF (~40 min, ends in output)
docs.text:
Not the grid. A vertical date list. Real output a stage manager could use tomorrow, and it proves the graph works before any geometry is at stake.

  1. Generate WORKDAYS. Loop script Script, ~10 lines, one record per real date across the season range. Canonical-per-date per J19 — Date is Unique + Not empty, and there is no bool_HideFromCalendar and no ovr_ManualDate.
  2. Build WORKDAYS_EVENTS Relationship — WORKDAYS::Date = EVENTS::Date, plus the calendar predicate from 0.1. This is the first relationship in the file.
  3. Build the WORKDAYS working form per LAYOUTS.tsv: anchor WORKDAYS, one portal Portal on WORKDAYS_EVENTS. Fields: date, then event name and times in the portal row. Ugly is the point.
  4. Preview mode. Not Browse. Browse never shows sliding and will lie to you all night.
  5. Save/Send Records as PDF.

Stop condition — PDF #1 exists. A page of dates with their events on it. If this does not happen, nothing in Stage 3 is worth starting.

docs.title: 3.1 · Run the empty-portal PDF test FIRST Verify on site
docs.text:
Before building all seven columns

An empty sliding portal is documented as corrupting Save/Send Records as PDF: with slide + resize enclosing part, a record whose portal is empty produces a PDF where the object below the portal does not render at all. This app has empty days by design and PRINT_SESSIONS exists to log Save/Send output, so this is the intended path, not an edge case.

Test: one week row, ONE day portal, containing a fully empty day, then Save/Send as PDF and confirm nothing below it vanishes. If it reproduces, a hidden single space in the day cell keeps the portal from ever being truly empty. Ten minutes here saves rebuilding seven columns.

docs.title: 3.2 · Build it
docs.text:
1. WEEKS fields: one record per week, plus the seven dates of that week (calc Calculation off the week-start date, or seven stored dates set by the generator — either is fine, the calc is cheaper).
  2. Seven buoys: WEEK_EVENTS_MON through WEEK_EVENTS_SUN Relationship, each predicated on that day's date on WEEKS against EVENTS::Date, plus the calendar predicate.
  3. Seven portals Portal side by side in the body part. Draw the slot count for TECH WEEK, not for an average week — a portal never grows, and busy weeks cost nothing extra while quiet weeks give the space back by sliding.
  4. Run print-geometry's build checklist literally. All seven portals slide up + also resize enclosing part (six out of seven pins the row open), and every object below them slides too.
  5. Chrome hides, space slides. Navigation and buttons get hide when printing; anything that leaves a hole has to slide or the collapse is blocked.

No rectangle as the day-cell border

Non-field objects slide but never shrink, so a box drawn for 10 rows keeps its height on a collapsed week and breaks the grid. Use the portal's own row borders, alternating fill, or a bottom rule set to slide.

Stop condition: in Preview, a light week is visibly shorter than tech week. If every week is the same height, something in step 4 is missing — it is almost always one portal or one footer object.

docs.title: Stage 4 · PDF test — acceptance (~15 min)
docs.text:
1. Save/Send Records as PDF across a range that contains: a tech week, a light week, an empty day, and a multi-day span (both Costume Fittings, Meliora Weekend and Fall Break are the four legitimate spans in the landed data).
  2. Check, in this order: nothing vanished below a portal, week rows differ in height, the multi-day spans read correctly, and a displaced event past the last slot carries its own date in its label (Decision Log J17).
  3. Open it on the iPad. Letter fit to the 13-inch screen renders at ~92% of physical size, so this is close to 1:1 and worth seeing on the real surface.

Done = PDF #2. A month grid that self-sizes per week, from real Big Love data, with zero scripting in the print path.

docs.title: Do-Not-Touch until a page prints
docs.text:
All real, all logged, none of it between you and a page

  • the import chain spec and the IMPORT · script pages
  • the logging spine defaults (Run End defaulting vl_Status to "ok")
  • the APP_SESSIONS vs UTILITY_LOGS fork (Q2)
  • the two goto_view_UTILITY_LOGS twins, and exit w/ errors
  • import_Style_Key Not recorded, STYLES, THEMES, CALENDAR_EMPHASIS, conditional formatting
  • the rest of the DDR punch list beyond the one index in Stage 1
  • the two colliding Decision Logs

One exception, already folded in: the fkProduction index, because Stage 1 needs it.

docs.title: If it stalls
docs.text: Symptom Cause, in order of likelihood Portal shows nothing calendar predicate — the unstored calc did not resolve (0.1); check the child-side index Every week the same height one portal missing also resize enclosing part, or an object below that does not slide Objects missing from the PDF the empty-portal defect (3.1). Put a hidden space in the day cell Grid looks right in Browse, wrong on paper you checked Browse. Sliding is Preview-only, anchoring is Browse-only Day cell keeps its height when empty a drawn rectangle as the border. Delete it

docs.title: The fallback, and it is not a failure
docs.text:
Running Big Love on the legacy file this fall costs nothing durable. ClickUp AUTHORS → FileMaker RENDERS → git ARCHIVES is locked, and a renderer is disposable. The season data lives in ClickUp; legacy handles one production at a time and Big Love is one production. Nothing done in legacy is lost work, because the data was never in FileMaker — MAWster re-imports whenever it is ready. The choice is which renderer to use this fall, not whether to finish the build.

The cost, stated honestly

Swapping globals per show by hand, and any hand-edit inside legacy is uncaptured, because FMP renders and does not author.

docs.title: Print & iPad Geometry
docs.text: MAW Prose · Fall 2026

docs.title: Print & iPad geometry
docs.text:
Design at letter geometry, because the iPad IS roughly a piece of paper. One layout serves screen and print — until it hits a portal.

The PDF is the product. PRINT_PRESETS · PRINT_SESSIONS · PRINT_SETS · PRINT_SET_ITEMS are in the schema before a single layout exists, and the whole [Projection Law] layer is generated in order to be rendered. So print is not a feature bolted on at the end; it is the output the app exists to produce.

Michael, 2026-08-08: "design it well for an ipad the size of a piece of paper." That instinct is dimensionally correct, and it is checkable.

docs.title: The measurement
docs.text:
13-inch iPad Pro display is 2752 × 2064 px at 264 ppi (Apple spec) → 10.42″ × 7.82″ in portrait.

US Letter 13″ iPad screen ratio width 8.5″ 7.82″ 92% height 11″ 10.42″ 95% aspect (w/h) 0.773 0.750 letter is slightly wider

A letter page fit to that screen's width renders at ~92% of physical size and clears the height with room to spare. Accurate to within 8%. Designing at letter geometry is therefore not a compromise for the screen — on the primary surface it is close to 1:1.

docs.title: One layout CAN serve both — two first-party mechanisms
docs.text:
1. Hide when printing. Inspector → Position tab → Sliding & Visibility → Object visibility. Non-printing objects are visible in Browse and Layout modes but not in Preview or when printed (Preventing objects from printing). Navigation, buttons and on-screen hints can live on the printed layout and evaporate on output.

2. Get ( WindowMode ) for a conditional Hide: 0 Browse · 1 Find · 2 Preview · 3 printing in progress · 4 Data Viewer while in Layout mode (first-party).

🪤 The gotcha that bites everyone once: a Hide condition of bare Get ( WindowMode ) is inverted, because Browse returns 0 and 0 is false — so it hides the object in every mode except Browse. Write Get ( WindowMode ) = 0, or not Get ( WindowMode ).

docs.title: Two mechanisms, two surfaces — do not confuse them
docs.text:
Both change an object's height, which is why they feel like one feature. They are not.

Anchoring (auto-resize) Sliding Responds to the window size the content Works in Browse — the iPad Preview / print / PDF only Direction grows and shrinks shrinks only

Vertical anchoring does nothing on paper: a page has no window to grow into, and Claris notes only the horizontal auto-resize settings apply in Preview and printing (auto-resize options).

Anchoring is the screen tool. Sliding is the paper tool.

docs.title: 🚫 Where "one layout for both" stops being true
docs.text:
1. Hiding an object leaves its hole. Claris's own note: to close the blank space you must set sliding on that object and every object below it. Print output is not screen output minus chrome; it is screen output compressed, and compression is a separate pass of work.

2. Sliding applies only in Preview and print, never in Browse — and it is vertical-only. So the iPad view is genuinely NOT what prints. Design at page geometry, then check Preview mode as a distinct step; it is the only honest proof.

3. A portal never grows. Whatever row count you draw is the permanent ceiling — a 6-row portal over 40 events prints 6. Draw for tech week, not for an average week: busy weeks cost nothing extra, quiet weeks give the space back.

docs.title: ⭐ The self-sizing week grid (Michael, 2026-08-08)
docs.text:
🔧 Correction, logged because the wrong version was briefly written here. "A field inside a portal row cannot shrink" is TRUE — row height is fixed. "A portal cannot shrink" is FALSE. Claris: "You can slide any object, including fields, portals, other objects, and even layout parts" (Removing blank spaces in printouts).

So the calendar day cell can be a portal, and the design is:

Draw ~10 slots per day. Turn sliding on. Each week row collapses to its busiest day.

Also resize enclosing part shrinks a part to its tallest remaining object, and seven day-portals sit side by side in one week row — so the row's printed height is set by the heaviest day that week. A week topping out at 3 events collapses hard; tech week prints at full depth. One layout, self-sizing per week, no scripting.

docs.title: ✅ Build checklist — the failure mode is forgetting one of these
docs.text:
• All seven day portals set to slide up + also resize enclosing part. Six out of seven pins the row open.
  • Every object below the portals slides too — rules, labels, footers. Anything that does not slide blocks the collapse.
  • 🚫 No rectangle as the day-cell border. Non-field objects slide but never shrink, so a box drawn for 10 rows keeps its height on a collapsed week and breaks the grid. Use the portal's own row borders or alternating fill, or a bottom rule set to slide.
  • Draw the slot count for tech week.
  • Overflow past the last slot uses the displaced-event treatment: visible, marked, and carrying its own date in its label (see the Decision Log, J17).
  • Check it in Preview, not Browse. Browse will never show the collapse.

docs.title: 🔴 Test this BEFORE building all seven columns
docs.text:
An empty sliding portal is documented as corrupting Save/Send Records as PDF — with slide + resize enclosing part, a record whose portal is empty produces a PDF where the object below the portal does not render at all. Print-to-PDF is reportedly unaffected; only Save/Send (thread).

This app has empty days by design (dark Mondays, hidden days per the emphasis rules), and PRINT_SESSIONS exists to log PDF output, so Save/Send is the intended path rather than an edge case.

Test: one week containing a fully empty day → export → confirm nothing vanishes. If it reproduces, a hidden single space in the day cell keeps the portal from ever being truly empty.

docs.title: The rule
docs.text:
Design at letter geometry. Hub layouts are dual-purpose, with chrome set to hide when printing. A portal is fine on paper as long as sliding is on and the drawn row count is the real ceiling.

Screen-only chrome hides; screen-only space has to slide.

⚠️ A list that must print every record regardless of count still wants a body part per record rather than a portal — that constraint has not changed, it just does not apply to a fixed-slot calendar cell.

docs.title: ⬜ To verify
docs.text:
• Portal + Hide when printing. An FMP13-era report has Hide when printing being ignored inside portal rows in Preview (thread). Old, possibly long fixed — but worth one test in FMP 26 given how portal-heavy this app is.
  • Whether the screen layout keeps 6 slots or matches print's 10. Screen has no sliding, so 10 fixed rows on a light week is dead space on the iPad; different counts on the two layouts is legitimate because they are different layouts.
  • Whether any of this generalizes into the FileMaker Canonical Object Library as a fleet-wide pattern rather than a MAWster one. Likely yes; that is Fiona's call, not this doc's.

docs.title: Projection Law
docs.text: MAW Prose · Fall 2026

docs.title: Projection law
docs.text:
LOCKED 2026-08-08 — there are NO manual edits to the projection layer, ever. The engine covers it.

"let's just not plan to do ManualEdits and have a formatting engine that is robust enough to get what I need done." — Michael, 2026-08-08

docs.title: The rule
docs.text:
[WEEKS] · [WORKDAYS] · [EVENTS_workday]To be confirmed are 100% derived. Delete-and-rebuild, always, on any trigger. No flags, no preservation pass, no reconciliation, no verify-before-commit step. Nothing is ever lost because nothing is ever authored there.

The ManualEdit flag is killed before it shipped — and killing it removes the whole machine it needed: a preservation pass on rebuild, a divergence report, an accept/discard decision per row. That machinery existed only to protect edits that now cannot happen.

⭐ Why this is the right call and not just the simpler one: a disposable table with edits in it is not disposable, it is a second source of truth wearing a temporary costume. Same species as the autoGenerated flag killed on the legacy duplicates, the convenience-copy dates, and the second-claimant highlight fields. Fourth instance in one session.

docs.title: What this OBLIGATES the engine to do
docs.text:
The pressure that creates spot-edits is real. Refusing the edits means the engine has to cover the cases, so they are named here rather than discovered under deadline:

Pressure Must be solved by "this one event needs different styling on this one page" a [STYLES] row or a [CALENDAR_EMPHASIS] row — a rule, not a keystroke "this week needs a page break here" PAGE_BREAK is generated; the RULE that sets it belongs on the preset "this day is too crowded to fit" overflow behaviour in the layout, not a hand-trimmed cell "the name is too long for the cell" UseShortTitle + a length-aware display calc "drop this event from this one printout" a [PRINT_PRESETS] FILTER (the legacy agenda already did exactly this to hide rehearsals) "a typo in an event name" fix it in ClickUp, reimport. ClickUp authors.

🔴 The last row is the load-bearing one. Every "just let me fix it on the page" is really a request to author data in the render layer, which is the architecture locked on 2026-08-07: ClickUp authors, FileMaker renders.

docs.title: Consequences, stated plainly
docs.text:
• ✅ Rebuild is dumb and safe: delete in scope, regenerate. No branching.
  • ✅ Reprinting an old [PRINT_SESSIONS] row is honest: it renders today's truth, and the paper was never authoritative.
  • ✅ No verify-before-commit pass to build or maintain.
  • ⚠️ A formatting need with no rule behind it becomes a BUILD task, not a workaround. That is the trade: slower on the one-off, and the app never accumulates untracked hand-fixes.
  • ⚠️ If a genuinely unrulable one-off ever appears, the answer is export the PDF and edit the PDF — outside the system, where it cannot pretend to be data.

docs.title: Theme Build Order
docs.text: MAW Prose · Fall 2026

docs.title: Theme build order
docs.text:
Every remaining step to get styled month headers and styled events onto one printed page. Nine steps, dependency-ordered, with what to verify after each.

The design is settled ([Theme Selection] · [Theme Resolution]) and the data is entered ([Theme State]). This page is the remaining WORK, in the order it has to happen, with the verification step that proves each one before the next depends on it.

⚠️ Written 2026-08-16 while the build was moving hourly. Check [Theme State] before trusting any ⬜ here.

docs.title: ✅ Already built — do not rebuild
docs.text:
STYLES::calc_Key            = vl_Domain &">"& vl_Label       auto-enter text, stored, indexed
WORKDAYS::StyleJoin_auto    = "monthLabel>"& Lower(MonthName(Date))
THEMES_x_STYLES::calc_ThemeStyleKey = fkTheme &">"& fkStyle  stored, UUID>UUID
PRODUCERS::fkTheme          →THEMES, nullable
GLOBAL_USE::g_pkCurrentTheme / g_pkDefaultTheme / g_pkCurrentOrg / g_pkCurrentProduction
ORGANIZATIONS::fkProducer / fkDefaultTheme
PRODUCTIONS::fkProducer
WORKDAYS → STYLES_for_WORKDAYS   (StyleJoin_auto = calc_Key)
EVENTS → STYLES_for_EVENTS → THEMES_X_STYLES_for_EVENTS → COLORS / TYPOGRAPHY
DATA: 19 STYLES · 23 THEME_COLORS · 4 THEME_TYPOGRAPHY · 3 THEMES · 22 THEMES_x_STYLES

docs.title: 🔴 STEP 0 · Settle the two claimants on the incoming status token
docs.text:
Nothing else in the import path can be built until this is decided, because it decides which field the lookup reads.

import_EVENTS already carries TWO fields for the same fact:

Field Its own note Status import_Style_Key "just get the data in and safe" {.conf} — treated as built CU_StatusToken "Raw label text, unmapped" {.tbc} — to be confirmed

⭐ These are one field wearing two names, and the naming tells you which survives. Every sibling in that block is import_* (import_Name, import_dateSTART, import_dateEND, import_raw_payload) — the prefix means raw, as it arrived, not yet trusted. CU_StatusToken sits in an INTEGRATION block beside cu_TaskID and uses a different casing convention.

Recommendation: keep import_Style_Key, retire CU_StatusToken. It matches its neighbours, it is already {.conf} rather than {.tbc}, and the import parser writing all the other import_* fields writes this one in the same pass. 🔴 Two claimants on one value is the defect this file has been caught on repeatedly — and this one is worse than most, because a parser that fills the other one leaves the lookup permanently empty and every event imports unstyled, silently.

⚠️ Verify against a DDR which one the import script actually populates today before deleting either. Archive → repoint → delete, never delete first.

⚠️ EVENTS::fkStyle's note says "STYLES row, domain event-status" and the file's domain is calendar. Stale note, from before the rename. Fix it in the same pass.

docs.title: 🔴 STEP 1 · The import-side lookup (2 fields, 1 TO)
docs.text:
This is the part I skimmed. Written out fully:

A.  import_EVENTS::calc_StyleLookup
       type ....... Text, auto-enter calculated value
       formula .... "calendar>" & import_Style_Key
       storage .... stored is fine (same-record)
       ⚠️ leave "Do not replace existing value" UNCHECKED
       ⚠️ BACKFILL if any import rows already exist

B.  New TO:  STYLES_for_IMPORT
       import_EVENTS::calc_StyleLookup  =  STYLES::calc_Key
       Allow creation ...... NO
       ⚠️ its own occurrence — anchor–buoy, do not reuse STYLES_for_EVENTS

C.  import_EVENTS::calc_StyleMatch   (optional but recommended)
       type ....... Calculation, UNSTORED, returns Text
       formula .... STYLES_for_IMPORT::PrimaryKey
       ⭐ this is what the import script reads. Empty = no match = report it.

⭐ Why C is worth the field: without it the script has to navigate the relationship inline, and an unmatched token looks identical to a matched-but-empty one. A named field makes "did this row find a style?" answerable in a table view, which is the only debugging surface an import gets.

VERIFY: put calc_StyleLookup and calc_StyleMatch side by side in the import_EVENTS table view. Every row should show a UUID in the second column. Any blank is a token with no STYLES row.

docs.title: 🔴 STEP 2 · Stamp the FK during import (script)
docs.text:
In the existing upsert loop, where each import_EVENTS row becomes or updates an EVENTS row:

Set Variable [ $styleFK ; import_EVENTS::calc_StyleMatch ]

If [ IsEmpty ( $styleFK ) ]
    #  do NOT abort the import. Log and continue.
    Set Variable [ $unmatched ; $unmatched & import_EVENTS::import_Style_Key & ¶ ]
End If

Set Field [ EVENTS::fkStyle ; $styleFK ]

Then after the loop:

If [ not IsEmpty ( $unmatched ) ]
    #  one UTILITY_LOGS row listing every distinct unmatched token
End If

🔴 The unmatched report is the ONLY defence on this whole path, and it is why the step exists. A UUID FK makes renames safe for already-imported events — rename DEADLINE → Deadline and existing rows keep their styling. But the NEXT import finds no row, writes an empty fkStyle, and those events render with no styling at all. ⚠️ That is not magenta. Magenta means a style was found and its appearance did not resolve; an empty FK means no style was ever found, the relationship is simply empty, and nothing is flagged. The two failures look nothing alike and only one of them is self-announcing.

⚠️ Never abort the import on an unmatched token. Partial styling is recoverable; a refused import loses the whole batch.

⚠️ STYLES rows must exist BEFORE the first import, or every event lands unstyled. The legacy file hardcoded status→RGB in a calc, so there was nothing to seed and this failure mode did not exist there.

VERIFY: run an import, then check EVENTS::fkStyle is populated. Confirm the log row appears when you deliberately misspell a token.

docs.title: 🔴 STEP 3 · The two theme-key calcs on STYLES (2 fields, serves everything)
docs.text:
STYLES::calc_ActiveThemeKey
    type ...... Calculation, UNSTORED, Text
    formula ... GLOBAL_USE::g_pkCurrentTheme & ">" & PrimaryKey

STYLES::calc_DefaultThemeKey
    type ...... Calculation, UNSTORED, Text
    formula ... GLOBAL_USE::g_pkDefaultTheme & ">" & PrimaryKey

🔴 UNSTORED is mandatory, not a preference. A calc referencing a global cannot be stored or indexed — FileMaker will refuse. ✅ And that is fine, because these are always the LEFT side of a relationship, and the left side needs no index. Only the right side (calc_ThemeStyleKey, already stored) does.

⭐ These are the highest-leverage two fields in the build. They live on the STYLES base table, so every occurrence inherits them — STYLES_for_WORKDAYS, STYLES_for_EVENTS, STYLES_for_IMPORT, and anything added later. Both branches on both chains, from two fields.

⚠️ No relationship to GLOBAL_USE is required. A global is readable from any context in a calculation; that is what global storage means. (This is the fork that blocked three relationships in the relationships doc until 08-16.)

VERIFY: in the Data Viewer, evaluate STYLES::calc_ActiveThemeKey on a month row. It should read <URITP-uuid>>january-uuid and change the moment you edit g_pkCurrentTheme. If it does not change, the global is not truly global.

docs.title: 🔴 STEP 4 · The WORKDAYS appearance branches (6 TOs)
docs.text:
The WORKDAYS chain currently reaches STYLES and stops. Both branches:

WORKDAYS (anchor)
  └─ STYLES_for_WORKDAYS                     ✅ exists
       ├─ TXS_ACTIVE_for_WORKDAYS            ⬜ calc_ActiveThemeKey = calc_ThemeStyleKey
       │    ├─ COLOR_ACTIVE_for_WORKDAYS     ⬜ fkColor_Text = THEME_COLORS::PrimaryKey
       │    └─ TYPE_ACTIVE_for_WORKDAYS      ⬜ fkTypography = THEME_TYPOGRAPHY::PrimaryKey
       └─ TXS_DEFAULT_for_WORKDAYS           ⬜ calc_DefaultThemeKey = calc_ThemeStyleKey
            ├─ COLOR_DEFAULT_for_WORKDAYS    ⬜ fkColor_Text = THEME_COLORS::PrimaryKey
            └─ TYPE_DEFAULT_for_WORKDAYS     ⬜ fkTypography = THEME_TYPOGRAPHY::PrimaryKey

⚠️ All six Allow creation = NO. ⚠️ Write the six rows into RELATIONSHIPS.tsv BEFORE building them — that file is the design step, and written afterwards it is transcription that gets skipped.

⚠️ Six occurrences for two vectors looks heavy and is correct: colour and typography are different tables (×2), active and default are different rows (×2), plus the two parents. Anchor–buoy forbids sharing them with the EVENTS chain; that duplication is the pattern working.

VERIFY: on a WORKDAYS layout, drop COLOR_ACTIVE_for_WORKDAYS::Name and COLOR_DEFAULT_for_WORKDAYS::Name as plain fields on the layout temporarily. For an August row under theme URITP you should see pure-blue and august. Two different values is the cascade proving itself.

docs.title: 🔴 STEP 5 · Mirror it on the EVENTS chain (1 repoint + 3 TOs)
docs.text:
REPOINT  THEMES_X_STYLES_for_EVENTS
    from ... fkStyle = STYLES::PrimaryKey
    to ..... STYLES::calc_ActiveThemeKey = calc_ThemeStyleKey

ADD      TXS_DEFAULT_for_EVENTS         calc_DefaultThemeKey = calc_ThemeStyleKey
           ├─ COLOR_DEFAULT_for_EVENTS
           └─ TYPE_DEFAULT_for_EVENTS

🔴 THE FLIP-ORDER TRAP. g_pkCurrentTheme is URITP, which covers only 4 of 19 tokens. The instant you repoint, the other 15 event styles go blank, because the default branch does not exist yet to catch them. ⚠️ It reads as "I broke the relationship" when it is actually the first honest answer — the old fkStyle-only match was ignoring the theme entirely and could return the wrong theme's row by found order.

✅ Safe orders: set g_pkCurrentTheme to default first, then repoint, then add the default branch · or build all three TOs and the resolve calc in one sitting, then flip the global back to URITP. 🚫 Never repoint and then go build the default branch afterwards — that leaves the file visibly broken between two edits, which is exactly when a session gets interrupted.

docs.title: 🔴 STEP 6 · The resolve calc
docs.text:
One per consumer. The WORKDAYS one:

WORKDAYS::calc_MonthLabel_Styled       Calculation, UNSTORED, Text result

Let ( [
    rgb  = If ( not IsEmpty ( COLOR_ACTIVE_for_WORKDAYS::PrimaryKey ) ;
                RGB ( COLOR_ACTIVE_for_WORKDAYS::R ;
                      COLOR_ACTIVE_for_WORKDAYS::G ;
                      COLOR_ACTIVE_for_WORKDAYS::B ) ;
            If ( not IsEmpty ( COLOR_DEFAULT_for_WORKDAYS::PrimaryKey ) ;
                RGB ( COLOR_DEFAULT_for_WORKDAYS::R ;
                      COLOR_DEFAULT_for_WORKDAYS::G ;
                      COLOR_DEFAULT_for_WORKDAYS::B ) ;
                RGB ( 255 ; 0 ; 255 ) ) ) ;

    fnt  = Case ( not IsEmpty ( TYPE_ACTIVE_for_WORKDAYS::Font ) ;
                      TYPE_ACTIVE_for_WORKDAYS::Font ;
                  not IsEmpty ( TYPE_DEFAULT_for_WORKDAYS::Font ) ;
                      TYPE_DEFAULT_for_WORKDAYS::Font ;
                  "Menlo" ) ;

    siz  = Case ( TYPE_ACTIVE_for_WORKDAYS::Size  > 0 ; TYPE_ACTIVE_for_WORKDAYS::Size ;
                  TYPE_DEFAULT_for_WORKDAYS::Size > 0 ; TYPE_DEFAULT_for_WORKDAYS::Size ;
                  9 ) ;

    cse  = Case ( not IsEmpty ( TYPE_ACTIVE_for_WORKDAYS::vl_Case ) ;
                      TYPE_ACTIVE_for_WORKDAYS::vl_Case ;
                  TYPE_DEFAULT_for_WORKDAYS::vl_Case ) ;

    lbl  = STYLES_for_WORKDAYS::vl_Label ;
    lbl  = Case ( cse = "UpperCase" ; Upper ( lbl ) ;
                  cse = "LowerCase" ; Lower ( lbl ) ;
                  cse = "TitleCase" ; Proper ( lbl ) ;
                  lbl )
] ;
    TextColor ( TextFont ( TextSize ( lbl ; siz ) ; fnt ) ; rgb )
)

🔴 Test emptiness on PrimaryKey, never on the value. IsEmpty ( ::R ) is TRUE when R is legitimately 0 — which is january's red channel (0000C5) and every pure colour in the table. Testing the value would make black and pure-blue fall through to magenta. This is the single easiest way to get this calc wrong.

🔴 Four independent coalesces, one per property. Never one row-level If — the URITP DEADLINE row overrides colour and typography while the month rows override colour only, so a row-level test loses the inherited half.

⚠️ Case is applied here, not by conditional formatting — CF provably cannot set case. ⚠️ SmallCaps has no FileMaker text function, so the display row's value silently does nothing on this path; it needs a real font variant. Untested.

⚠️ The literal fallbacks ("Menlo", 9) are a judgement call. They only fire if the default theme is incomplete, which should be impossible — so arguably they should be conspicuous garbage instead. Left readable deliberately: a print that comes out ugly-but-legible beats one that comes out unreadable, and magenta already covers the colour vector loudly.

✅ The EVENTS twin is identical with EVENTS::Name in place of vl_Label and the *_for_EVENTS occurrences.

VERIFY: Data Viewer, on an August WORKDAYS row, theme URITP. Expect pure-blue Menlo 9 bold uppercase. Then set g_pkCurrentTheme to default — the same field should go dark blue.

docs.title: 🔴 STEP 7 · Put it on the layout
docs.text:
1. On print | Calendar, the month header object currently displays a date field or a literal. Swap it to calc_MonthLabel_Styled.
  2. ⚠️ Turn OFF any local formatting on that object. A font or colour set on the object itself wins over TextColor ( ) in some render paths — the object must be visually neutral so the data does all the work.
  3. ⚠️ The object must be big enough for the largest theme's type, or a 22pt override clips silently in print with no error.
  4. Same for the event name object with the EVENTS resolve calc.

VERIFY: Preview mode, not Browse. 🔴 Then actually make a PDF — print rendering and screen rendering are different code paths, and this whole model exists to produce paper.

docs.title: 🔴 STEP 8 · The startup script
docs.text:
00App_onFirstWindowOpen  (or a SET · Theme From Context subscript it calls)

  1. g_pkCurrentOrg      ← stored preference, else the only ORGANIZATIONS record
  2. g_pkDefaultTheme    ← ORGANIZATIONS::fkDefaultTheme        ⭐ FLOOR FIRST
  3. g_pkCurrentProduction ← last used, or the user picks
  4. g_pkCurrentTheme    ← PRODUCTIONS::fkProducer → PRODUCERS::fkTheme
                            if empty → g_pkDefaultTheme
  5. GUARD: either theme global still empty → dialog + halt

🔴 Step 5 is not optional. A global holds nothing until something sets it, so an empty g_pkDefaultTheme prints the entire file magenta. That is the one real advantage the record-based design had: a stored fact cannot be unset by opening the file. The floor is now a startup obligation and needs a guard, not trust.

⚠️ A production switch IS a theme switch. Step 4 must be its own subscript, called from open AND from the production picker. 🚫 Never duplicate the walk.

⚠️ Until this exists, the globals are hand-set, and that is fine for testing. After it exists, hand-setting g_pkCurrentTheme is a debugging action, not configuration.

docs.title: 🔴 STEP 9 · Leave one row genuinely EMPTY
docs.text:
Three of the four URITP rows set fkTypography = body rather than leaving it blank. ⭐ A restated default is indistinguishable from an override, so those rows will never exercise the inherit path — the coalesce could be completely broken and they would still look right.

Blank fkTypography on at least one URITP row and confirm it still renders in the default's typography. That is the only test that proves inheritance rather than coincidence.

docs.title: Dependency order, one line
docs.text:
0 claimant → 1 lookup → 2 stamp → 3 theme calcs → 4 WORKDAYS TOs
  → 5 EVENTS TOs → 6 resolve calc → 7 layout → PDF → 8 script → 9 inherit test

⭐ Steps 3 + 4 + 6 + 7 alone get a styled month header onto paper. 0–2 are the event half; 8–9 are correctness. If the goal today is one printed page, do 3, 4, 6, 7 and stop.
