docs.title: Event Styling
docs.text: MAW Prose · Fall 2026

docs.title: Event styling
docs.text:
How an EVENT gets its style. ONE path— the ClickUp token arrives, a domain prefix is added, the string finds the STYLES row. The calendar vocabulary is a contract with ClickUp.

How a canonical EVENTS row gets its style token.

Mechanism: [Theme Resolution] · selection: [Theme Selection] · observed state: [Theme State] · remaining work: [Theme Build Order].

docs.title: 🔴 CORRECTION 2026-08-16 — read this before anything else on this page
docs.text:
An earlier revision of this page (PR #140) described EVENTS::fkStyle and EVENTS::autoKey_StyleLookup as two mechanisms: a UUID foreign key acting as a human OVERRIDE, and a derived string acting as the AUTO path, with a resolve order between them, two relationships, and a coalesce branch in the resolve calc.

🚫 All of that was invented. There is no override layer. Retracted in full.

What is actually true:

EVENTS::fkStyle              holds the RAW ClickUp token:  "DEADLINE"  "Production"
EVENTS::autoKey_StyleLookup  =  "calendar>" & fkStyle

They are the same fact, one step apart. fkStyle is the token; autoKey_StyleLookup is that token with its domain prefix. ✅ The relationship to STYLES keys on autoKey_StyleLookup, and that is the only path. One route, no override, no second relationship, no coalesce.

docs.title: Why the error happened, because the cause is still in the schema
docs.text:
🔴 Two different fields in two different tables are both named fkStyle, and they hold different KINDS of value.

Field Holds THEMES_x_STYLES::fkStyle a UUID — a real foreign key to STYLES::PrimaryKey EVENTS::fkStyle the raw token text — "DEADLINE"

A screenshot of THEMES_x_STYLES::calc_ThemeStyleKey rendering as UUID>UUID was read as proof that fkStyle stores a UUID — and then that conclusion was carried one table over to EVENTS, where the same field name means something else entirely. The evidence was real and the inference crossed a table boundary.

⭐ The lesson, and it is worth more than the correction: fk is a TYPE CLAIM. In this file the prefix means this holds a key to another table's PrimaryKey. On EVENTS it holds display text from another system. A field whose prefix lies will be reasoned about wrongly by everyone who reads it — including its author's collaborators — and no DDR flags it, because a Text field holding text is perfectly valid. This is the third EVENTS::fkStyle finding in the app's history and all three trace to the name.

docs.title: 🔴 Rename it, and ovr_ is ALSO wrong
docs.text:
Fix-queue item 11 currently says "EVENTS::fkStyle → rename ovr_fkStyle". 🚫 That is wrong too, for the same reason — it keeps the false fk claim and adds a false override claim on top of it.

The field holds an imported vocabulary token, so name it that:

EVENTS::styleToken           <-- preferred. says what it holds.
EVENTS::import_StyleToken    <-- if provenance matters more than brevity

⚠️ Then autoKey_StyleLookup reads correctly as what it is: the token with its domain prefix, built for one job — finding the row. ⚠️ Renaming breaks nothing (relationships and calcs follow field IDs, not names), but the autoKey_StyleLookup formula text will need re-reading once.

⚠️ EVENTS::fkStyle's own field note says "STYLES row, domain event-status." Both halves are now wrong: it is not a STYLES row, and the live domain is calendar, not event-status. Fix in the same pass.

docs.title: ✅ Placement, ruled 2026-08-16 (Michael)
docs.text:
"The style applies to the canonical event in the database — which is EVENTS — and the stylekey gets updated on the canonical EVENT via import_. So the autoKey and relationship to style should be on the canonical EVENT, because that's where the workday print version comes from."

The key lives on EVENTS, not import_EVENTS. This corrects an earlier draft that put the lookup on the import table.

⭐ The reasoning generalizes into a rule: a resolution key belongs on the table the RENDER reads, not the table the VALUE arrived through. print | Calendar is anchored on WORKDAYS and reaches events via EVENTS_X_WORKDAYS → EVENTS. It never touches import_EVENTS. A key on the import table would have forced the render to walk back through the archive to style a row, coupling the print path to the intake path.

✅ Consequence: import_EVENTS stays purely ARCHIVAL. It holds what arrived, verbatim, and nothing downstream reads it at render time.

docs.title: The one path
docs.text:
ClickUp status token                         "DEADLINE"
      |
      v
import_EVENTS::import_Style_Key              raw, archival, never read at render
      |
      |  import script writes it forward to the canonical row
      v
EVENTS::fkStyle   (→ styleToken)             "DEADLINE"
      |
      |  auto-enter:  "calendar>" & fkStyle
      v
EVENTS::autoKey_StyleLookup                  "calendar>DEADLINE"
      |
      |  = STYLES_for_EVENTS::calc_Key
      v
STYLES row  →  THEMES_X_STYLES  →  THEME_COLORS / THEME_TYPOGRAPHY

✅ Keeping the bare token on EVENTS rather than only the prefixed key is right, for two reasons worth stating: it is the provenance of the style decision (what ClickUp actually said, on the canonical row, without reopening the archive), and it keeps the prefix in exactly one place instead of being baked into stored data.

⚠️ Auto-enter does not backfill. Any existing EVENTS rows created before autoKey_StyleLookup existed have it empty. Replace Field Contents with calculated result, then eyeball the column.

docs.title: 🔴 The calendar vocabulary is a CONTRACT with ClickUp
docs.text:
The join is on a string, so the two vocabularies must agree character for character. That is not a flaw — it is what the calendar domain IS: the mapping table from ClickUp's status names to our appearance. STYLES.md says exactly that: "STYLES maps token → colour."

🔴 But the two domains have OPPOSITE ownership, and that has to be written down:

Domain Who owns the label text Renaming a vl_Label calendar ClickUp. Mirrors of status names. 🚫 Never rename to taste. It must match ClickUp exactly or the join dies. monthLabel Us. Derived by Lower ( MonthName ( ) ). ⚠️ Only alongside the calc that produces it.

⚠️ Renaming a status in ClickUp is a two-system change. The next import writes the new token, finds no STYLES row, and those events land unstyled.

🔴 Unstyled is NOT magenta, and the difference is the whole reason the report matters. Magenta means a style was found and its appearance did not resolve — loud, on the page. An unmatched token means no style was ever found: the relationship is simply empty, nothing resolves, nothing is flagged. One failure announces itself and the other does not.

✅ So the unmatched-token report is the single defence on this path. One UTILITY_LOGS row per import listing every distinct token that matched no STYLES row. ⚠️ Never abort the import — partial styling is recoverable, a refused batch is not. ⚠️ STYLES rows must exist BEFORE the first import or everything lands unstyled; the legacy file hardcoded status→RGB in a calc, so it had nothing to seed and this failure mode did not exist there.

⭐ A note on key types, since this got argued in both directions today. A UUID key is rename-safe because it is opaque — and opacity is precisely what you do NOT want on the ClickUp seam, whose entire job is to notice when two vocabularies stop agreeing. The string key makes drift detectable; a UUID would have hidden it and gone on applying yesterday's mapping. ⚠️ Detectable is not detected: the report does that work, not the key type.

docs.title: Naming · unify on autoKey_
docs.text:
Three conventions currently name one job:

STYLES::calc_Key                    the shared right side
WORKDAYS::StyleJoin_auto            month header, left side
EVENTS::autoKey_StyleLookup         event, left side

⭐ autoKey_ is the best of the three — auto-entered AND key in two front-loaded tokens, so it sorts with its siblings in a field list. Rename WORKDAYS::StyleJoin_auto → autoKey_StyleLookup so both consumer halves match exactly. Do it before a third consumer exists.

⚠️ STYLES::calc_Key keeps calc_ — it is the field on the other side of every join, and the different prefix marks that asymmetry usefully.

docs.title: ⚠️ The domain prefix is a typed string, in two calcs
docs.text:
"calendar>" and "monthLabel>" are literals inside auto-enter calculations — which the file's own pre-build discipline warns against (no domain strings typed into calcs; a misspelling is FALSE forever, silently).

✅ Accepted as-is, and the reason is worth recording so it is a decision rather than an oversight: it is one literal per consumer table, sitting immediately beside the join it feeds, and the failure is total rather than partial — misspell it and every row on that table fails at once, which is loud on the first test. Contrast a typo in a vl_Domain data value, which breaks exactly one token and hides.

⚠️ Revisit if a third or fourth consumer appears. At that point the domain names want to be a value list feeding both the data and a single derivation, not four literals in four calcs.

docs.title: Open items on this path
docs.text:
• ⬜ Rename EVENTS::fkStyle → styleToken. 🚫 Fix-queue item 11's ovr_fkStyle is withdrawn — wrong on both halves.
  • ⬜ Its field note says "STYLES row, domain event-status" — wrong twice over.
  • ⬜ The unmatched-token report does not exist. Only defence on this path.
  • ⬜ Backfill autoKey_StyleLookup on any pre-existing EVENTS rows.
  • ⬜ Two claimants on the raw token in import_EVENTS: import_Style_Key ({.conf}) and CU_StatusToken ({.tbc}). One field wearing two names. 🔴 If the parser fills the unused one, fkStyle is never written, autoKey_StyleLookup is "calendar>" with nothing after it, and every event imports unstyled, silently.
  • ⬜ THEMES_X_STYLES_for_EVENTS still has no theme predicate. ⚠️ Flip-order trap: g_pkCurrentTheme is URITP, covering 4 of 19 tokens — repointing before TXS_DEFAULT_for_EVENTS exists blanks the other 15, and it reads as a broken relationship when it is the first honest answer.
  • ⬜ Is there a canonical style on STANDARD_EVENTS? An 08-09 note claims so. If yes, that is where a real specific-else-general question lives — but it is about tokens, not about an FK on EVENTS, and it is not yet verified.

docs.title: Theme Resolution
docs.text: MAW Prose · Fall 2026

docs.title: Theme resolution
docs.text:
How a layout object finds its appearance. SELECTION picks the theme once at startup; RESOLUTION reads it per object. Two layers, not two rival designs.

How any styled object on any layout gets its appearance, using the month day label as the worked example because it is the first token family built out.

🔴 For what is actually IN the tables and the graph right now, read [Theme State] first. This page is the mechanism; that page is the evidence, and it is newer.

docs.title: ⭐ TWO LAYERS, and conflating them cost half a session
docs.text:
SELECTION  ....  WHICH theme is in force?     runs ONCE, at startup
                    a cascade -> two globals

   RESOLUTION ....  what does THIS object look like?   runs per object, per render
                    globals -> token -> vectors -> values

🔴 The ORGANIZATIONS → PRODUCERS cascade and the two globals are NOT rival designs, and they never were. The 08-09 design and the 08-16 build were mistaken for competing answers because both were described as "the cascade." They are different layers:

  • The cascade SELECTS. Producer's theme, else the organization's default — a question about whose paperwork is this.
  • The globals CARRY the answer. g_pkCurrentTheme + g_pkDefaultTheme, read by every resolve calc.

✅ So nothing was lost, and the better mechanism composes with the built one. The cascade is what a startup script RUNS to set the globals. Neither replaces the other.

🚫 The cascade must NOT be moved INSIDE the resolve chain, and this is the load-bearing reason the split matters:

  1. Cost per cell. A resolve calc runs on every styled object on every row. A 42-cell month grid × several tokens per cell would walk producer → organization lookups thousands of times per print. Resolving once into a global is the whole point of a global.
  2. It pushes magenta further away. The per-vector coalesce is active → default → MAGENTA. Add producer and organization as rungs and it becomes four-deep × three vectors, and the bug detector stops being adjacent to the bug.
  3. Two answers to one question. If the resolve calc can re-derive the theme, the global is no longer authoritative and nothing keeps them equal. ⭐ One question, one answering surface.

docs.title: 🔴 What the SELECTION layer needs (mostly already there)
docs.text:
✅ ORGANIZATIONS already carries both pointers: fkProducer and fkDefaultTheme, both relationship-typed. The 08-09 design's data half exists.

⚠️ PRODUCERS has NO fkTheme in its table doc, though an 08-09 note claimed it landed. Either the doc is stale or the field was never built. Verify against a DDR before building the cascade — without it there is no producer rung and the cascade is one hop.

⚠️ The table is ORGANIZATIONS (plural). Docs and session notes have called it ORGANIZATION throughout. One of them is wrong and it is about to appear in a script.

🔴 ORGANIZATIONS.tsv's field NOTES are copied from an export table — fkProducer is annotated "what it's called in this set" and fkDefaultTheme "the final per-file export path choice". Neither describes a theme. The comments-are-the-spec defect, again: treat every field comment as a claim.

⚠️ Which organization record is "us" is unresolved. Tenancy was phased 08-09 to multi-record-by-design with g_pkCurrentOrg selecting one. The selection script needs that global set before it can read a default theme — so the cascade is really g_pkCurrentOrg → organization → producer → theme, and the first hop is itself a startup choice.

docs.title: The script, in order
docs.text:
OnFirstWindowOpen
  |
  1. set g_pkCurrentOrg        (which organization is this copy)
  2. set g_pkDefaultTheme  <-  ORGANIZATIONS::fkDefaultTheme     THE FLOOR
  3. set g_pkCurrentTheme  <-  PRODUCERS::fkTheme  if not empty
                               else g_pkDefaultTheme
  4. HALT + report if either theme global is empty

🔴 Step 4 is not optional. A global is volatile — it holds nothing until something sets it, so an empty g_pkDefaultTheme prints the entire file magenta. That is the one real advantage the record-based design had: a stored fact cannot be unset by opening the file. The floor is now a startup obligation, and it needs an explicit guard rather than trust.

⭐ Why the cascade does NOT block the print, and why deferring it is cheap this time: it lives in a script. The 08-09 reasoning — add a level to a cascade now, because converting a single lookup into a cascade later means touching every resolve calc — was true of the resolve chain. In a startup script, adding a rung is one step in one place. Build the resolve chain, get a page out, then deepen selection whenever. Choosing the layer is what made it cheap.

docs.title: RESOLUTION — the chain
docs.text:
LAYOUT: month-view part / portal row
=====================================================================

    [ TEXT OBJECT: the month day label ]
                |
                |  displays a CALC, not a plain date field
                v
    [ calc_DateLabel_Styled ]   unstored, on the object's base TO
                |
                |   TextColor( TextFont( TextSize( label ; size ) ; font ) ; rgb )
                |                  ^           ^                   ^
                |            text colour   font family           size
                |                  |           |                   |
                +------------------+-----------+-------------------+
                                   |
=================================  |  ==============================
 HOP 1     DATE ------> JOIN KEY   |
                                   |
    [ WORKDAYS::Date ]             |
            |                      |
            |  "monthLabel>" & Lower ( MonthName ( Date ) )
            v
    [ WORKDAYS::StyleJoin_auto ]   auto-enter TEXT, stored
            |
 HOP 2      |   JOIN KEY ------> TOKEN
            v
        ||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||
        ||  TO: STYLES_for_WORKDAYS            ||
        ||     StyleJoin_auto = calc_Key       ||
        ||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||
            |
            v
        [ STYLES ]  ---- IDENTITY ONLY. 12 month rows.
        [   PrimaryKey                          ]
        [   vl_Domain = "monthLabel"            ]
        [   vl_Label  = "january"               ]
        [   calc_Key  = vl_Domain &">"& vl_Label ]  <-- STORED, indexed
        [   LegendText   printed string, NOT a key ]
        [   Sort = 70.01   PRESENTATION ONLY    ]
        [   no colour  no font  no theme key    ]
            |
 HOP 3 + 4   TOKEN ------> APPEARANCE      TWO parallel TOs
            |
        +---+-----------------------------+
        v                                 v
 [ TXS_ACTIVE_for_WORKDAYS ]      [ TXS_DEFAULT_for_WORKDAYS ]
 [  calc_ActiveThemeKey     ]     [  calc_DefaultThemeKey     ]
 [    = calc_ThemeStyleKey  ]     [    = calc_ThemeStyleKey   ]
        |                                 |
        |  fkColor_Text                   |  fkColor_Text
        |  fkTypography                   |  fkTypography
        +---------------+-----------------+
                        |
        PER-VECTOR coalesce -- twice, INDEPENDENTLY.
        Never one row-level If.  Empty = inherit, per vector.
                        |
   text = active.fkColor_Text or default.fkColor_Text or MAGENTA
   type = active.fkTypography or default.fkTypography or MAGENTA
                        |
 HOP 5     VECTOR ------> VALUE
        +---------------+-----------------+
        v                                 v
 [ THEME_COLORS ]                 [ THEME_TYPOGRAPHY ]
 [  R / G / B --> RGB( r;g;b )  <-- layout eats THIS ]
 [  Hex       --> export / HTML only                ]

⭐ The two key calcs live on the STYLES BASE TABLE, so every occurrence inherits them free — STYLES_for_WORKDAYS, STYLES_for_EVENTS, any future consumer. Fields are shared across occurrences; TOs are not. Extending to a second anchor costs predicates and buoys, never fields.

docs.title: ✅ The join key is a COMPOSITE (Michael's design, adopted 08-16)
docs.text:
STYLES            calc_Key            = vl_Domain & ">" & vl_Label       stored, indexed
WORKDAYS          StyleJoin_auto      = "monthLabel>" & Lower(MonthName(Date))
THEMES_x_STYLES   calc_ThemeStyleKey  = fkTheme & ">" & fkStyle          stored, indexed
STYLES            calc_ActiveThemeKey = g_pkCurrentTheme & ">" & PrimaryKey   unstored
STYLES            calc_DefaultThemeKey= g_pkDefaultTheme & ">" & PrimaryKey   unstored

⭐ Why a composite beats two predicates: two predicates need two match fields per side. One composite needs one. Multiply by token families and it halves the field count on every consumer.

🔴 The reuse is asymmetric. calc_Key on STYLES is ONE field serving N relationships. A consumer's join field holds one domain's value at a time, so it is one field PER DOMAIN — StyleJoin_Month, StyleJoin_Emphasis. Suffix from row one; an unsuffixed first field forces the second into a worse name and the pair reads as though one is authoritative (the fkStyle / ovr_fkStyle defect).

⚠️ Right sides MUST be stored and indexed. An unstored right side makes a relationship non-functional, not slow. ✅ Left sides may be unstored, which is what lets them read globals.

⚠️ Auto-enter does NOT backfill. Any new key field is empty on every pre-existing row until Replace Field Contents runs. ⚠️ calc_ThemeStyleKey needs it across all 18 rows.

⚠️ Verify what fkTheme and fkStyle STORE before building calc_ThemeStyleKey. The table view displays default and monthLabel>january — either the stored value or a value-list rendering of a UUID. A composite built from a display label is not a key.

⚠️ The delimiter is >. Chosen over . because . already means decimal in Sort (70.01) in the same table, and vl_Label holds human strings. > has no second job. One character wrong on either side fails as no related record.

⚠️ Call it a KEY, never a hash. Readable composites survive the Data Viewer, which is the only debugging surface a calculation has.

docs.title: 🔴 Sort IS NOT A JOIN KEY
docs.text:
Sort for the month family is 70.01–70.12 — a block-prefixed presentation ordering, not identity.

  1. ⭐ Positional values get renumbered. Resequencing a legend is a routine presentation edit; key a relationship on it and a legend reorder silently restyles the calendar, with the symptom nowhere near the edit.
  2. Matching it needs 70 + Month ( Date ) / 100 — a domain constant typed into a calc.
  3. Sort is globally unique, so any domain predicate beside it becomes decorative. A predicate that cannot fail is not a predicate.

✅ It is typed Number. It is the wrong key for reasons unrelated to its type.

docs.title: Hop 1 — what is in the calc
docs.text:
🔴 A predicate cannot hold an expression — FileMaker matches field to field, so a field on the consumer is required either way. 🔴 And a calculation cannot call a SCRIPT (nor can conditional formatting, a merge field, or web viewer content) — anything a script returns but does not DO is a custom function, and on a boundary it MUST be. ⚠️ Debug it in the Data Viewer; custom functions have no step-through.

✅ As built: Lower ( MonthName ( Date ) ). ⚠️ Lower ( ) is load-bearing — MonthName returns January, the token is january. Remove it and all twelve fail silently.

⚠️ MonthName ( ) reads the file's language setting, so the key's correctness now depends on a locale. Failure mode is no related record → magenta, which reads as a theme bug. ⚠️ Reasoned, not observed in this file.

✅ It is also the ONLY place the twelve strings are derived — no Choose ( ), no typed literals. So the MonthLabel ( ) custom-function proposal is now OPTIONAL rather than required: a native function plus Lower ( ) already gives one origin. Promote it only if the locale risk is confirmed real.

🚫 A numeric MatchKey field on STYLES was REFUSED — it duplicates what vl_Label already is, a convenience copy, the defect caught three times in this file.

docs.title: 🌐 Value lists: YES for domains, NO for months
docs.text:
Domains — back it with a value list. vl_Domain is half of a join key; a typo orphans a token permanently and prints magenta. Typing is the only failure mode; a picker removes it.

🔴 Months — no, structurally. vl_Label is polymorphic: month names on month rows, calendar names on calendar rows. One field whose legal values depend on another field cannot be backed by one flat list, and a conditional list would need a source of legal (domain, label) pairs — which is STYLES itself. Circular.

⭐ The real problem it was reaching for: the twelve strings must not exist twice. ✅ Solved by Lower ( MonthName ( ) ) being the sole derivation. If rows are ever re-seeded, seed them BY SCRIPT from the same expression, never by typing.

docs.title: 🔴 FILL is DEMOTED, not missing (ruled 08-16)
docs.text:
The capability list says CF can set fill and text colour. True — and it never distinguishes STATIC from CALCULATED, which is the whole question.

  • CF picks a colour from a swatch picker, per condition. The condition is a formula; the colour is not. So CF cannot read THEME_COLORS, and a CF-driven fill means one hardcoded condition per token per theme — the exact defect the model prevents.
  • ✅ TextColor ( ) · TextFont ( ) · TextSize ( ) in a calc DO take data, PROVEN IN THIS FILE: THEME_COLORS::Hex_autoCalc renders each hex string in its own colour from stored R/G/B. Text and typography are deliverable.
  • 🔴 There is no Fill ( ) function. Fill is not calculable by any route.

⭐ Fill is a CELL concern; colour and typography are a TEXT concern. A month label is text inside a cell. The one token that genuinely wants a fill (BLACK) wants a whole-cell treatment via the emphasis path and a real layout object — the vector had no delivery mechanism because it was aimed at the wrong layer.

Consequences: ✅ the default theme is COMPLETE at two vectors, so magenta is unreachable and meaningful again · 🚫 keep fkColor_Fill, but exclude it from the completeness test or that test reports false failures forever · 🔴 the CF capability test is OFF the critical path — it was load-bearing only for fill · ⚠️ revive when a real cell background is needed AND CF is shown to take data.

⚠️ Case is data too (vl_Case) and CF cannot set case — apply Upper ( ) in the calc. 🔴 FileMaker has no SmallCaps text function, so SmallCaps is undeliverable by the calc path and needs a real font variant. Untested.

docs.title: 🔴 MAGENTA is a CALC LITERAL, never a record
docs.text:
RGB ( 255 ; 0 ; 255 ) inline in the resolve calc. Stored nowhere, and it must not be.

Why: magenta exists to prove a lookup failed. A fallback stored as a record can itself be renamed, deleted or fail to resolve — the exact failure it detects. A detector that shares the failure mode of the thing it detects is not a detector. It must also not be themeable, or a theme could hide its own gaps. It is deliberately ugly: an unresolved join renders as ordinary black and prints silently, which is the whole problem.

docs.title: Currency at the boundary
docs.text: ✅ THEME_COLORS stores R / G / B, so the layout path needs no conversion at all — RGB ( R ; G ; B ) reads straight off the vector. Hex serves export and HTML only, which makes the canonical color/ custom-function family an export concern, never a rendering blocker.

docs.title: Known open items
docs.text:
• ✅ The default-theme floor EXISTS as g_pkDefaultTheme (true Global storage), not ORGANIZATIONS.fkDefaultTheme. The 08-09 open item is satisfied differently than written — every doc calling the floor missing is stale. ⚠️ But it is volatile: OnFirstWindowOpen must set it, with a guard.
  • 🔴 THEMES_X_STYLES_for_EVENTS matches on fkStyle alone — no theme predicate. Works only while default is the sole populated theme. ⚠️ FLIP-ORDER TRAP: g_pkCurrentTheme is URITP, which has zero rows, so repointing before the default branch exists blanks every event style — and it reads as a broken relationship when it is actually the first honest answer. Set the global to default first, or build both branches in one sitting.
  • ⬜ PRODUCERS::fkTheme — claimed built 08-09, absent from the table doc. Verify.
  • ⬜ ORGANIZATIONS vs ORGANIZATION — plural in the table doc, singular everywhere else.
  • ⬜ g_pkCurrentOrg must be set before the cascade can read a default theme.
  • ⬜ calc_ThemeStyleKey not built, and needs backfilling on all 18 rows.
  • ⬜ The WORKDAYS chain stops at STYLES — no appearance buoys yet.
  • ⬜ BLACK has a token, no appearance row, no LegendText.
  • ⚠️ STYLES.md describes a superseded design — specs a nonexistent MonthNum, puts Hex + RGB on STYLES against the identity-only model, and lists domains (month, event-status) the file does not use. Reconcile before building from it.

Related: [Theme State] · [Relationships] · [Projection Law] — a formatting need with no rule behind it becomes a build task, never a hand-edit. A month that needs its own look is a STYLES row.

docs.title: Theme selection
docs.text:
WHICH theme is in force. A startup script walks records and lands the answer in two globals. Carries the MASTER DIAGRAM of the whole theme system, fields through to printed page.

The SELECTION half of the theme system. [Theme Resolution] is the other half.

   SELECTION  ....  WHICH theme is in force?          ONCE, at startup
                    records -> script -> two globals

   RESOLUTION ....  what does THIS object look like?  per object, per render
                    globals -> token -> vectors -> values

⭐ The app and every print reference only a CURRENT and a DEFAULT theme. A script sets those from records. That is the whole idea: the cascade is expensive and situational, so it runs once; the resolve chain is hot, so it reads two globals and nothing else.

docs.title: ⭐ THE MASTER DIAGRAM — fields to printed page
docs.text:
Read this one first

Captured verbatim 2026-08-16 at Michael's request. If you only read one thing about theming in this app, read this. Every claim below it is elaboration.

FIELDS
=========================================================================

ORGANIZATIONS ....... who OWNS this copy       ✅ built
  Name                Text
  fkProducer          →PRODUCERS    which producer row is US (brand/logo)
  fkDefaultTheme      →THEMES       ⭐ THE FLOOR
  + audit ×5

PRODUCERS ........... the producing entities   ✅ built
  Name / NameShort / NameDisplay
  media_LogoWide / media_LogoSquare
  fkTheme             →THEMES       ✅ built. nullable = inherit floor
  + audit ×5

PRODUCTIONS ......... a show                   ✅ built
  fkProducer          →PRODUCERS    ⭐ who produces THIS show
  Title / dates / cuProductionToken / fkVenue / fkCourse

GLOBAL_USE .......... session state, all true Global
  g_pkCurrentTheme        ⭐ the ACTIVE side of every resolve
  g_pkDefaultTheme        ⭐ the FLOOR
  g_pkCurrentProduction      reaches the show's producer
  g_pkCurrentAppSession / g_pkCurrentUtilitySession
  g_AppTitle / g_AppTitleShort
  g_pkCurrentOrg          ✅ built

THEMES .............. default(90) · URITP(20) · database(80)


SELECTION  ──  runs ONCE at startup
=========================================================================

  OnFirstWindowOpen
     │
     1. resolve the ORGANIZATION record
     │
     2. g_pkDefaultTheme  ←  ORGANIZATIONS::fkDefaultTheme
     │                       the floor, set FIRST
     3. g_pkCurrentProduction  ←  last used / user picks
     │
     4. walk to the SHOW's producer:
     │      PRODUCTIONS::fkProducer → PRODUCERS::fkTheme
     │         has value?  → g_pkCurrentTheme = it
     │         empty?      → g_pkCurrentTheme = g_pkDefaultTheme
     │
     5. GUARD: either global empty → HALT + report
     ▼
   two globals hold the answer. nothing else re-derives it.


RESOLUTION  ──  runs per object, reads only the globals
=========================================================================

  ClickUp authors
     │  CU_StatusToken  ("Rehearsal", "DEADLINE"...)
     ▼
  import_EVENTS ──"calendar>"& token──→ STYLES::calc_Key
     │
     ▼
  EVENTS::fkStyle   ← stamped at import, or a user picks it on the portal
     │                ✅ stamping a token FK is IDENTITY, allowed
     │                🚫 stamping a resolved COLOUR is not
     │
  ═══ projection: WORKDAYS + EVENTS_X_WORKDAYS (generated) ═══
     │
     ▼
  print | Calendar        anchor = WORKDAYS
     │
     ├─ MONTH HEADER                    ├─ EVENT ROW
     │   StyleJoin_auto                 │   EVENTS::fkStyle
     │   = STYLES::calc_Key             │   = STYLES::PrimaryKey
     │        ▼                         │        ▼
     │   STYLES_for_WORKDAYS            │   STYLES_for_EVENTS
     │     ├─ ACTIVE  → COLOR / TYPE    │     ├─ ACTIVE  → COLOR / TYPE
     │     └─ DEFAULT → COLOR / TYPE    │     └─ DEFAULT → COLOR / TYPE
     │        ▼                         │        ▼
     │   coalesce per vector            │   coalesce per vector
     │   active → default → MAGENTA     │   active → default → MAGENTA
     │        ▼                         │        ▼
     │   TextColor(TextFont(TextSize(   │   TextColor(TextFont(TextSize(
     │      Upper( "JANUARY" ))))       │      "First Rehearsal" )))
     └──────────────┬──────────────────┘
                    ▼
              🖨️  ONE PDF PAGE

✅ PRODUCERS::fkTheme and GLOBAL_USE::g_pkCurrentOrg were both built 2026-08-16, minutes after being flagged missing. Every field the selection layer needs now exists. What is left is the script that walks them.

docs.title: 🔴 fkProducer means TWO DIFFERENT THINGS, and only one of them should drive a theme
docs.text:
Field Question it answers ORGANIZATIONS::fkProducer which producer row is US — house identity, logos, brand PRODUCTIONS::fkProducer who produces THIS show — URITP vs One Acts vs ROC

⭐ A print's theme must follow the SHOW's producer, not the house's. The whole point of the 08-09 design was One Acts could print differently from the main season — and One Acts is a value of PRODUCTIONS::fkProducer, never of ORGANIZATIONS::fkProducer.

🔴 So the cascade path is g_pkCurrentProduction → PRODUCTIONS::fkProducer → PRODUCERS::fkTheme, NOT through ORGANIZATIONS. The 08-09 write-up drew it as organization → producer, which reads correctly and resolves to the wrong producer for every show the house does not produce itself. ORGANIZATIONS contributes exactly ONE thing to selection: the floor.

⚠️ Same word, two grains, one already-built field each. Neither is wrong; using the wrong one is silent.

docs.title: The startup script, in detail
docs.text:
🔴 Step 5 is not optional. A global holds nothing until something sets it, so an empty g_pkDefaultTheme prints the entire file magenta. This is the one real advantage the record-based design had — a stored fact cannot be unset by opening the file. The floor is now a startup obligation and needs an explicit guard, not trust.

⚠️ Changing production mid-session re-runs step 4. A production switch is a theme switch, so the same subscript is called from wherever g_pkCurrentProduction changes. 🚫 Never duplicate the walk — one SET · Theme From Context subscript, called from open and from the production picker.

⚠️ g_pkCurrentTheme is currently set to URITP by hand, and URITP has zero appearance rows. Once step 4 exists, it is derived, and hand-setting it becomes a debugging action rather than configuration.

⚠️ Step 1 depends on how many ORGANIZATIONS records there are. g_pkCurrentOrg now exists, which supports the multi-record reading; the competing 08-09 ruling was "a second company is a second FILE, so the tenant IS the file." ⭐ With the global built, the script should read it and fall back to the only record when it is empty — that works under either answer and needs no decision today. 🔴 If it stays one record, create by script and never via a layout, or the day there are two the script silently reads whichever comes first.

⚠️ The table is ORGANIZATIONS (plural); every doc and session note says ORGANIZATION. About to appear in a script.

🔴 ORGANIZATIONS.tsv's field notes are pasted from an export table — fkProducer reads "what it's called in this set" and fkDefaultTheme "the final per-file export path choice." Neither describes a theme. Comments-are-the-spec, again: treat every field comment as a claim to verify.

docs.title: Notes on the end-to-end path
docs.text:
✅ Both print chains use the SAME calc_ActiveThemeKey / calc_DefaultThemeKey fields, because those live on the STYLES base table and every occurrence inherits them. ⚠️ The occurrences must still be separate per anchor — anchor–buoy — and that duplication is the pattern working, not a cost of it.

🔴 The two chains differ at ONE hop and it matters: the month header joins on a derived key (StyleJoin_auto, computed from the date), the event joins on a stored FK (fkStyle, set at import or picked by a human). Derived keys self-heal; stored FKs rot when the thing they point at is renamed or deleted. So events need referential care that month labels never will.

⚠️ EVENTS::fkStyle should be ovr_fkStyle — STANDARD_EVENTS holds the canonical style and this field is the per-event OVERRIDE. Unprefixed, it reads as authoritative. Already on the fix queue.

🔴 cuProductionToken and CU_StatusToken are EXACT ClickUp strings, and a rename in ClickUp breaks the join SILENTLY. The styling chain inherits that fragility at its very first hop: a renamed ClickUp status produces calendar>SomethingNew, which matches no STYLES row, and the event lands unstyled. ⭐ STYLES rows must exist BEFORE the first import, and an unmatched token is worth a report line rather than silence.

docs.text:
• ✅ PRODUCERS::fkTheme BUILT 2026-08-16.
  • ✅ g_pkCurrentOrg BUILT 2026-08-16.
  • ⬜ The startup script does not exist. 00App_onFirstWindowOpen is present but was never read or specced.
  • ⬜ THEMES_x_STYLES::calc_ThemeStyleKey not built; needs backfilling on all 18 rows.
  • ⬜ The WORKDAYS chain stops at STYLES — no appearance buoys yet.
  • ⬜ THEMES_X_STYLES_for_EVENTS has no theme predicate. ⚠️ Flip-order trap: repointing it while g_pkCurrentTheme is URITP blanks every event style, and it reads as a broken relationship when it is actually the first honest answer.
  • ⬜ URITP has zero appearance rows, so the cascade is untestable until a few exist.
  • ⬜ ORGANIZATIONS singular/plural — settle before the script names it.

docs.text:
The colour chain RESOLVES END TO END and renders on the print layout. What is built, what the remaining work is, and the two bugs that cost the afternoon.

🔴 EVIDENCE, not plan. Read off the running file. Mechanism → [Theme Resolution]; this page is record- and schema-level truth and where they disagree, this one is newer.

⚠️ A SNAPSHOT. It went stale three times inside one hour on 08-16. Re-read before acting.

docs.title: ✅ THE COLOUR CHAIN WORKS — 14:00 ET, 2026-08-16
docs.text:
Month-token colour resolves end to end and renders on print | Calendar. Date headers print in their month's colour, from data, with no hardcoding on the layout. First proof that the whole model delivers.

Every hop verified by eye in a table view:

WORKDAYS::Date               8/8/2026
  → StyleJoin_auto          "monthLabel>august"          ✅
  → STYLES_for_WORKDAYS     the august token row         ✅
  → calc_ActiveThemeKey     "8B833BAF…>007629BE…"        ✅
  → TXS_for_curr_WORKDAYS   ::fkColor_Text = 3E37CF9C…   ✅
  → THEME_COLORS_for_curr   ::Name = "august"            ✅
  → TextColor( … RGB(R;G;B) )   renders on the page      ✅

docs.title: 🔴 The two bugs that cost the afternoon — both silent, both invisible to a DDR
1. Delimiter mismatch: . vs >
docs.text:
calc_ActiveThemeKey   =  g_pkCurrentTheme & "." & PrimaryKey    ← built from a stale doc
calc_ThemeStyleKey    =  fkTheme & ">" & fkStyle                ← the file's real delimiter

Never matched. Symptom: every date header printed BLACK, because RGB ( 0 ; 0 ; 0 ) is what an empty relationship yields. 🔴 That is the exact silent-black failure magenta was designed to catch, and magenta could not catch it — the fallback lives inside the calc, so a join that returns nothing never reaches it. ⭐ A bug detector downstream of the break cannot see the break.

⚠️ Cause was a stale doc: an early revision of theme-resolution.md specced "." before the file's ">" was observed. The doc was corrected; the field built from it was not. Correcting a document does not correct what was already built from it.

docs.title: 2. Globals held NAMES, not keys
docs.text:
g_pkCurrentTheme held "default" while fkTheme holds a UUID, so the composite could never match. 🔴 Third instance in one day of a prefix making a false type claim (g_pk… promising a key, EVENTS::fkStyle promising an FK). ✅ Fixed: globals now hold UUIDs, with a pop-up display override so they stay human-readable on screen.

⭐ The debugging method that actually found both: put each hop's raw value on a layout as a plain field, side by side, and read across. The first blank column is the broken hop. Two blank columns plus one populated key column localised it in one pass.

docs.title: ⭐ Size is layout, everything else is data (ruled 14:20)
docs.text:
Full reasoning → [Vector Grain]. Colour, font, bold, italic and case stay DATA. Only SIZE moves to the layout object. Omit TextSize ( ) and the object's own point size governs while TextFont / TextStyleAdd still apply, so ONE calculation field serves every surface.

🪦 The surface domain is withdrawn (PR #145's model). 🪦 So is a global surface — impossible, since print | Calendar renders two typography roles at once.

⚠️ THEME_TYPOGRAPHY::Size becomes spec, not render — keep the field, comment it, do not delete it.

docs.title: 🔴 Object calcs are a HACK — use real fields
docs.text:
The styled text was prototyped as button-bar calculations (Action: Do Nothing), which is the only native way to put an expression on a layout without a field.

🚫 Not shippable. A button bar is a click target, it is invisible to the DDR so it cannot be audited or documented, no script or export can read it, and it cannot be reused on a second layout. ✅ The resolve calc references only related data from WORKDAYS context, so a real unstored calculation field behaves identically and is placeable. Result must be Text or formatting is stripped.

docs.title: The tables
docs.text:
STYLES               19 rows   ✅  calendar ×7 · monthLabel ×12
THEME_COLORS         23 rows   ✅  11 semantic + 12 month
THEME_TYPOGRAPHY      4 rows   ✅  display · cal-month-portal-header · body · meta
THEMES                3 rows   ✅  default(90) · URITP(20) · database(80)
THEMES_x_STYLES      22 rows   ✅  18 default + 4 URITP (sparse, by design)

✅ Keys and graph, all confirmed live:

STYLES::calc_Key              = vl_Domain &">"& vl_Label        stored, indexed
STYLES::calc_ActiveThemeKey   = g_pkCurrentTheme &">"& PrimaryKey   Calculation, unstored
STYLES::calc_DefaultThemeKey  = g_pkDefaultTheme &">"& PrimaryKey   Calculation, unstored
WORKDAYS::StyleJoin_auto      = "monthLabel>" & Lower(MonthName(Date))
THEMES_x_STYLES::calc_ThemeStyleKey = fkTheme &">"& fkStyle    Calculation, INDEXED
EVENTS::autoKey_StyleLookup   = "calendar>" & <the imported token>

✅ An UNSTORED calculation IS usable as a relationship's left side — verified live. Only the right side needs storage and an index. calc_ThemeStyleKey is indexed and correct.

✅ LineWeight deleted · the nameless fifth THEME_TYPOGRAPHY record deleted · month LegendText populated (JAN…DEC) · BLACK given --.

⚠️ fkColor_Fill is empty on all 22 rows and fill is DEMOTED, not missing. Fill is a CELL concern and text colour is a TEXT concern; the one token that wants a real fill (BLACK) needs a whole-cell treatment via the emphasis path. Exclude it from any completeness test or that test reports false failures forever. 🔴 Consequently the CF capability test is OFF the critical path — it was load-bearing only for fill, and text/typography are now proven by a rendered page rather than by a pending test.

docs.title: 🔴 The domains in the FILE are calendar and monthLabel
docs.text:
STYLES.md says month · event-status · watermark · emphasis — stale. watermark, emphasis and base do not exist; event-status was renamed calendar with no doc following.

⭐ THE GOVERNING LESSON: the DATA is the truth and the table doc is a CLAIM. On 08-16 an agent read STYLES.md, found month, and corrected Michael away from monthLabel — the string actually in his file. A domain string is half of a join predicate, so acting on the stale doc would have produced twelve tokens resolving to nothing.

🔴 STYLES.md also specs a MonthNum field that does not exist and describes STYLES as a colour table holding Hex + R/G/B, contradicting the identity-only model. It documents a superseded design.

docs.title: Remaining work
docs.text:
• ⬜ Typography still reads _for_EVENTS in the date calc, so the month header apes the top portal event's font. Repoint to THEME_TYPOGRAPHY_for_curr_WORKDAYS.
  • ⬜ ~italic / ~bold / ~underline are declared in the Let and never used in the output — so cal-month-portal-header's bold is computed and thrown away.
  • ⬜ Convert the button-bar calcs to real calculation fields.
  • ⬜ The DEFAULT branch is not built on WORKDAYS — only _for_curr_*. Until it exists there is no inherit path and a sparse theme renders nothing. 🔴 Build it before adding more URITP rows.
  • ⬜ THEMES_X_STYLES_for_EVENTS has no theme predicate, so two rows qualify and found order picks. ⚠️ Flip-order trap: repointing while g_pkCurrentTheme covers only 4 of 19 tokens blanks the rest.
  • ⬜ Rename EVENTS::fkStyle → styleToken — it holds raw token text, not a key. 🚫 Fix-queue item 11's ovr_fkStyle is withdrawn: wrong on both halves.
  • ⬜ Two claimants on the raw token in import_EVENTS: import_Style_Key and CU_StatusToken.
  • ⬜ The unmatched-token report — the only defence against a ClickUp status rename landing events unstyled. 🔴 Unstyled ≠ magenta: an empty FK is silent.
  • ⬜ The startup script to set the two theme globals, with a guard.
  • ⬜ Leave one URITP row's fkTypography genuinely EMPTY — three of four restate body, and a restated default never exercises the inherit path.
  • ⬜ ORGANIZATIONS singular/plural — settle before a script names it.

docs.title: Styled Objects Template (build spec)
docs.text: MAW Prose · Fall 2026

docs.title: template | STYLED OBJECTS — build spec
docs.text:
Build spec for template | STYLED OBJECTS — one layout holding one instance of every styled role. It is the token inventory, the theme test bench, and the source you copy production objects from.

Michael, 2026-08-16: "we can define in a template page the exact OBJECTS that we need/want on every page and use that to drive which styles we define?" — yes, and it is the FMP-native twin of the F1 theme object templates already in FileMaker Home.

docs.title: Why this layout exists — three jobs, not one
docs.text:
1. ⭐ It IS the inventory. The objects on this page are the definitive list of styled roles. Not on the template → not a token. A layout needing something the template lacks is the moment to decide new role, or reuse an existing one — the object library's approval test, enforced by a place instead of a document.
  2. ⭐ It is the theme test bench. Flip g_pkCurrentTheme and every token that resolves wrong is visible on ONE page, instead of hunting four print layouts.
  3. ✅ It is the copy source. FileMaker Home already rules: production layouts should be copied from the object library, not styled ad hoc. This gives that rule a home inside the file.

docs.title: 🔴 The three rules that keep it useful
docs.text:
• 🚫 Tokens, not layouts. Do NOT mock up the calendar grid here. It is a swatch page — one instance per role even if five layouts use it. Geometry lives on the real layouts; this page carries appearance only.
  • 🚫 Never in the layout menu. Same rule as util_* layouts. It is a workbench, not a destination.
  • ⚠️ Every object gets an OBJECT NAME matching its token (Inspector ▸ Position ▸ Name). That is what makes it findable, scriptable, and greppable in a DDR — without names this page is just a pretty picture.

docs.title: Layout setup
docs.text:
name .......... template | STYLED OBJECTS
show in menu .. NO
base table .... WORKDAYS      ← chosen deliberately, see note
parts ......... Header (chrome roles)
                Body   (record-driven roles)
                Footer (chrome roles)

⚠️ Base table WORKDAYS, and the reason matters: the date roles are the only ones already proven end to end, and WORKDAYS is a projection table so its records are disposable. 🔴 A styled field only renders on a layout whose context can reach its relationships — so the EVENT roles need either a portal to EVENTS_X_WORKDAYS or a second template layout anchored on EVENTS. Start with a portal; split to template | STYLED OBJECTS · EVENTS only if the graph fights you.

docs.title: ✅ BUILD NOW — the calendar roles
docs.text:
These are live or one step away. Each row is one object.

Object name Displays Size Status tok_date_short calc_DateLabel_Short 9 ⬜ field not built tok_date_colloquial calc_DateLabel_Colloquial 11 ⬜ tok_date_display calc_DateLabel_Display 14 ⬜ tok_event_name EVENTS::calc_EventName_Styled 9 ⬜ needs a portal tok_emphasis_label the holiday / blackout label 9 ⬜ token exists (BLACK), no appearance row

⚠️ All five are the SAME formula with one line different (~text = …). Build one, verify it, duplicate.

⚠️ Set each object's point size in the Inspector, per the size-only ruling in [Vector Grain] — size is layout, everything else is data. 🔴 Size the object taller than the text needs. A font swap changes width and a bigger theme clips silently in print with no error.

docs.title: Chrome roles — defer the decision, not the objects
docs.text:
Place these as plain text objects for now, styled with the FMP theme:

chr_page_title        the production title
chr_subtitle          calendar name / date range
chr_footer            "printed <date>" + page number
chr_column_header     day-of-week strip
chr_legend_entry      one legend row

⭐ Why plain, not tokenised: chrome has NO record grain, so there is nothing to join to. A footer looks the same on every page of every production. ⚠️ Tokenise a chrome role only when a THEME needs to restyle it — that is a real requirement, and it is not today's. Placing them now means the page shows the whole visual language even where the mechanism is still native.

docs.title: 📇 PRELIM · CONTACT SHEET roles
docs.text:
Drawn now so the vocabulary exists before the layout does. 🔴 Do NOT build the fields yet — there is no PEOPLE table (fix-queue item 16: ROLES::fkPerson pointed at nothing and was removed). These are named holes, not tasks.

Object name Displays Data-driven? tok_person_name full name ⚠️ probably NOT — see below tok_person_role "Stage Manager" ✅ likely — department could carry colour tok_person_dept department / section label ✅ likely — the strongest candidate chr_contact_detail phone / email 🚫 chrome. no meaning in its appearance chr_contact_group_header "PRODUCTION TEAM" 🚫 chrome tok_person_status active / released / TBD ✅ likely — condition, like calendar

⭐ The useful prediction, and it is the whole reason to write this early: a contact sheet is mostly CHROME. A person's name does not mean anything different in blue. Department and status are the only real token candidates — department is a kind (same shape as monthLabel) and status is a condition (same shape as calendar).

⚠️ So the contact sheet will want a department domain and possibly a personStatus domain — domains, never tables. STYLES.md: "Add a domain, not a table."

🔴 And the open vocabulary gap already logged in the object library applies exactly here: document-type labels express KIND, badge_status_* expresses CONDITION, and forcing one into the other is how a family drifts. department is kind; personStatus is condition. Two domains, not one.

docs.title: Build order
docs.text:
1. The three dateFormat_* calcs on WORKDAYS (Text result, stored).
  2. calc_DateLabel_Short — one styled field, the full colour + font + case body. Verify it renders before duplicating.
  3. Duplicate it twice for Colloquial and Display, changing only ~text.
  4. Cut the layout, place the three date objects, name each one.
  5. Add the chrome text objects. Plain, FMP-theme styled.
  6. Flip g_pkCurrentTheme to URITP and look. August and October should change colour; nothing else should move. 🔴 That is the first real cascade test.
  7. Only then add the EVENTS portal and tok_event_name.
  8. report-contact-sheet objects: not yet. Revisit when a PEOPLE table exists.

docs.title: ⚠️ Two things this page cannot do
docs.text:
• It does not test GEOMETRY. A token that looks perfect here can still clip in a 0.9-inch grid cell. Print the real layout too.
  • It cannot show the DEFAULT branch working, because the default branch is not built on WORKDAYS yet — only _for_curr_*. 🔴 Until it exists, a sparse theme renders nothing rather than inheriting, and this page will show that as blank text rather than as an obvious error.

docs.title: Vector Grain (what is data, what is layout)
docs.text: MAW Prose · Fall 2026

docs.title: Vector grain
docs.text:
SIZE is the only typography property that varies by surface. Strip it to the layout object; colour, font, bold, italic and case all stay data. One placeable field serves every surface.

Michael, 2026-08-16: "an agenda view workday header would be a very different font size than the calendar view day-portal view — how do we handle both?" → then, after three worse answers: "what if SIZE was stripped down to per layout but the rest of typography applied regardless of surface?"

docs.title: ⭐ THE RULING · SIZE is the only property that belongs to the surface
docs.text:
DATA  (themeable, in-app editable, joins from STYLES)
   colour ....... varies by month / status / theme
   font family .. semantic. a month header is Menlo everywhere
   bold ......... semantic
   italic ....... semantic
   case ......... semantic

LAYOUT  (the object's own formatting)
   SIZE ......... the ONLY one that changes because of WHERE it is printed

⭐ Everything except size is semantic — it describes what the thing IS. A month header is uppercase Menlo bold in the grid, on the agenda, and on a wall poster. It is only bigger on the agenda. Size is the one axis that is genuinely about the surface, and it is the one that was forcing every other property to be duplicated per surface.

✅ And FileMaker cooperates: omit TextSize ( ) and the layout object's own point size governs, while TextFont ( ) and TextStyleAdd ( ) still apply from data. They are independent formatting runs on the same text.

TextColor (
   TextFont ( TextStyleAdd ( ~text ; ~case ) ; ~font ) ;
   RGB ( ~r ; ~g ; ~b )
)

⭐ Result: ONE calculation field, placeable on every layout. The grid object is set to 9pt, the agenda object to 22pt, and both render Menlo bold uppercase in august blue. Typography stays user-editable per theme.

docs.title: 🪦 SUPERSEDED · the surface domain
docs.text:
An earlier revision of this page (PR #145) ruled that typography resolves from a second token — surface>cal-day-header, surface>agenda-day-header — as a fourth vl_Domain.

🚫 Withdrawn. Do not build the surface domain. It solved the right problem (a token matrix of 12 months × N surfaces) at the wrong layer, and it still cost one resolve calc field per surface plus a STYLES row and a THEMES_x_STYLES row per surface per theme.

⭐ The size-only split gets the same outcome for nothing: no new domain, no new tokens, no per-surface fields, no per-surface rows. It is strictly cheaper and it is strictly simpler, and the reason is that it cut along the axis where the variation actually was.

🪦 Also dead, recorded so they are not re-proposed:

  • A global surface. 🔴 Provably impossible: print | Calendar renders two surfaces at once — the month header and the event names inside the portal are different typography roles on the same page in the same pass. One global cannot be two values. (Michael reached this himself mid-riff.)
  • A token per month per surface. 12 × 4 = 48 rows per theme with 36 duplicated colours; recolouring August becomes a four-row edit that can drift. The exact failure the object library exists to prevent.
  • Moving typography entirely into FileMaker theme styles. Native and clean, but it takes typography out of the data, so a theme could recolour and never restyle. Rejected because Michael wanted it in-app editable — correctly, since that is what makes it a THEME rather than a palette.

docs.title: What THEME_TYPOGRAPHY::Size becomes
docs.text:
⚠️ SPEC, not render. The number a human reads while sizing a layout object — the same role hex plays for colour (hex is for export and human eyes, R/G/B is what the layout eats).

🔴 DO NOT DELETE THE FIELD. It is populated, it is genuinely useful, and it is the only written record of what size a role is supposed to be. ⚠️ But an unused field that looks used is exactly the defect this app keeps getting bitten by (LineWeight, fkColor_Fill, enter_Hex) — so it must SAY it is spec, in its own field comment, or someone wires TextSize ( ) back in and re-breaks the surface split.

✅ The LineWeight precedent does not apply: that rule is never build a container nothing can fill, and Size is filled with real values that do real work. The test is whether the field has content and purpose, not whether the RENDER reads it.

docs.title: ⚠️ The cost, stated plainly
docs.text:
A font swap changes width at a fixed size. Georgia 9pt is wider than Menlo 9pt, so a theme change can overflow a cell that a font change never used to touch. ✅ Accepted by Michael. Mitigation is generous object sizing, not a mechanism.

⚠️ A theme cannot change scale. URITP can make the agenda serif and italic; it cannot make it 30% larger. If that ever becomes a real requirement, the answer is a per-surface resolve field on that one surface — which is now an additive, local change rather than an architecture.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
Manual first, import skins on top.

ClickUp is the editing surface. It holds canonical Task IDs for each canonical item. Whatever you can get away with in ClickUp with a single task ID is what we can expect to be able to import with. The path from "plan" to "page" is:

  • Tasks are devised in CU and stored as EVENTS (typically TaskType::Event, but not a requirement).

    • These are necessarily homed in a list in CU, but may be added to other list

  • Those created Event TASKS are either repitions of known 'standard' events, or are on-one requirements. This distinction is far more important to plans for the fmp build, than with CU use.

docs.title: Related ClickUp Lists
docs.text: Production Events (canonical) for the distinct, repeating event types: First Rehearsal, DR, LX Focus. Finding this grain can be challenging.

docs.title: URITP Production Folders
docs.text:
Each working Production gets a ClickUp view which serves as the export surface of that Productions Events or fkCalendar Events?

Think of these views as that Production's individual Production Google Calendar - that these are passive chunks of that larger calendar, but some events may overlap - notable breaks that exist at the beginning and ends of processes. More and more productions are overlapping now, so it would be prudent to be able to print a productions calendar, and it be aware of events associated with that production vs associated with other producitons - or UR Events.

Calendar Color should no longer include: UR Events > that is essentially it's own "Production" as viewed from the mainstage schedule's awareness.

If the same event needs to appear on multiple calendars.

The actual EVENT exists once in CU, and has a unique ClickUp ID. This Event, however, could be shared into multiple ClickUp view Calendars.

docs.title: For the Production Calendars
docs.text:
[PRODUCTION_CALENDARS] - One calendar per production (usually - exceptions might be the same production in two different time blocks). - Joining entity to output.

[CALENDAR_EMPHASIS] - N typed callouts per calendar. range mode = typed dates; event mode = anchored to a STANDARD_EVENT so it survives a reschedule. - Priority-resolved. Replaced the fixed highlight/lowlight pairs. - ⬜ Michael's note: use this for HIDE as well. Not done — HIDE is currently a range pair on the calendar because hide is EXISTENCE (stamped, changes the found set) while emphasis is STYLING (resolved live). Folding it in means deciding which verb wins.

[WEEKS] - Parent is the CALENDAR, not the production. [WORKDAYS] - The printed grid cell. Generated, never typed.

[STANDARD_EVENTS]To be confirmed - For defining custom events. Nothing in the app should break if there are no standard events. That is to say that all imported events are handled elegantly regardless of its existence in STANDARD_EVENTS. But STANDARD_EVENTS should automatically be linked during import and might SKIN additionally or help us export specialized reports or create workflow notes from canonical definitions. - ⭐ Also the anchor for event-mode emphasis.

[EVENTS] - What gets printed. UPSERT on TaskID + fkProduction, never TaskID alone. [import_SESSIONS] - One pull. The session IS the snapshot. - see also {#import-events}

docs.title: Exporting — the print hub
docs.text:
⚠️ PRINT or EXPORT — the vocabulary is split and this section is where it shows

Every label below says PRINT_. Every file in 20-tables/ says EXPORT_. The @ids mostly kept the PRINT spelling through that rename, so the links work and the words disagree.

✅ @table-print-presets was DEAD and is fixed (2026-09-30) — EXPORT_PRESETS.md carries id: table-export-presets, the one id that drifted on both sides at once. 🚫 The four visible labels are deliberately NOT renamed: renaming one of five leaves the section half-converted, which is the state that produced this defect. One decision, one pass, or leave it.

[PRINT_PRESETS] - HOW to output. Reusable across productions. [PRINT_SETS] - WHAT to output, batched. One reserved SCRATCH set resets from a template set on entry. [PRINT_SET_ITEMS] - One produced document. Overrides live here; empty means inherit from the preset. [PRINT_SESSIONS] - WHAT HAPPENED. One row per PDF. Carries fkPreset.

[EDITIONS]To be confirmed - Prelim | For Bid Only | Final. A PRINT is a VERSION of an edition. [VERSIONS]To be confirmed - Parts of an edition.

docs.title: HIDE is real, and it stays
docs.text:
HIDE_Start / HIDE_End grey a range out entirely — the flag stamps onto WORKDAYS and those days do not print. Legacy evidence: Secretary INFO sets 3/7/27 → 3/13/27, which is spring break.

Hide is existence, not styling: it changes which records are in the found set. CALENDAR_EMPHASIS only styles records already there.

⚠️ Superseded in part, 2026-08-09: bool_HideFromCalendar on WORKDAYS was ruled illegal on a canonical date table — hiding is ONE calendar's decision about a date, so left there, one show hides a week for every show sharing it. The hide row moves to CALENDAR_HIGHLIGHT. 🔴 And it must BLANK THE CELL, never remove the record: a flowed found set shifts every subsequent day one column left.

docs.title: 🔴 The grid moved to the PRINT layer (2026-08-08, Michael)
docs.text:
Week start is a PRINT spec, not a calendar fact. date_CalendarStart and bool_StartOnMonday are gone from this table.

  • WeekStartDay (1–7) lives on the export preset, snapshotted onto the export session.
  • 🪦 The boolean is dead. It cannot express Tuesday, which is the actual answer — a theatre week runs Tue→Mon because Monday is the dark day. Sunday-or-Monday was never the real domain, and the legacy startOnMon (a TEXT field compared against = 1) was wrong twice over.
  • date_CalendarStart is derived: the WeekStartDay falling on or before PRODUCTIONS::DateFirstRehearsal.

⚠️ The consequence is structural: WEEKS and WORKDAYS are DISPOSABLE. The same calendar rendered Tue-start vs Sun-start produces different week rows, so the grid cannot be generated once and reused. It is rebuilt per print, exactly like EVENTS_workday.

🔒 The projection is never hand-edited — see projection-law.md. Rebuild is therefore a dumb delete-and-regenerate with no preservation pass.

docs.title: The three-layer table is NOT here
docs.text:
It lives on the app index. This page carried its own copy until 2026-08-10 and the copy had gone stale — it listed PRINT_SESSIONS under Archive with no export preset beside it, and omitted STYLES from Canonical entirely.

⭐ Two surfaces stating one model is the dueling-canonical defect, and the duplicate is always the one that rots — this repo has retired three manifests over exactly that shape. A table page is the wrong home for a whole-app classification: it is read when someone wants THIS table, so nobody re-checks the part that is about the other fifteen.

16 rows · EVENTS.tsv

  • Built by UPSERT from the newest import session. Never deleted and re-created.
  • 🔴 Upsert key = TaskID + fkProduction. A CU event task can carry two shows; each calendar prints its own copy.
  • fkStandardEvent is the reporting spine: per-production churn on TaskID, season-wide "we never move these" on the standard event.
  • Unscheduled (no date) events collect at the top of week one, legacy parity.

docs.title: 🔴 SPANS STAY WHOLE (ruled by Fiona, 2026-08-08)
docs.text:
The legacy file DUPLICATED a multi-day event into one record per day (CREATE_multipleDays, flagged autoGenerated = 1) so that a day-portal could find it. That is killed.

Why it cannot survive:

  1. It breaks the upsert key. Three rows with an identical TaskID + fkProduction means the second import cannot tell an update from a duplicate. Either the key grows a date and stops being an identity, or re-import returns to delete-and-replace — and the whole history model goes with it.
  2. It destroys the change count. A span moving Mon–Wed → Tue–Thu is ONE change. Duplicated, it reads as three deletions and three creations, so WatchHash counts noise on exactly the events that move most.
  3. ⭐ autoGenerated is the tell. A flag meaning this row is not real is the schema saying the row should not exist. Same species as a convenience-copy date or a second-claimant field.
  4. The agenda gets correct for free. A span appears ONCE with a date range. Under duplication it could not — hence the autoGenerated descending sort buried in Events Agenda View SORT.

docs.title: How a day-portal finds a span
docs.text:
Not an equality on a stamped key. A multi-predicate RANGE relationship:

WORKDAYS::DATE      >=  EVENTS|span::Start_DATE
WORKDAYS::DATE      <=  EVENTS|span::End_DATE
WORKDAYS::fkCalendar =   EVENTS|span::fkCalendar

Every day inside the span sees the event, from ONE stored row. Same pattern as CALENDAR_EMPHASIS — one range-resolution mechanism used twice, not two different tricks.

  • 🔴 End_DATE must never be empty. A single-day event needs End_DATE = Start_DATE; empty means DATE <= "" and the event vanishes from every portal. Auto-enter it.
  • ⚠️ Inequality predicates cannot use a stored index like equality can, so a span portal is slower. On a 68-day grid with ~120 events this is a non-issue.
  • 🚪 Escape hatch, NOT built: if performance ever bites, generate an EVENT_DAYS join (one row per event-day, rebuilt at import, never edited, never the source of truth). That buys duplication's SPEED without its IDENTITY problem. Named here so nobody re-invents autoGenerated under pressure.

docs.title: Open, from Beckett
docs.text:
• ⬜ A span crossing a HIDDEN day renders on both sides of a gap and reads as continuous. Duplication handled this by accident (no row was made for a hidden day). Range joins have no opinion. Decide what the page should show.
  • ⬜ A span running past the calendar bounds truncates silently — the page understates duration with no marker.
  • ⬜ Visual continuation. A five-day load-in prints its name in five cells with no "continues" affordance. Legacy had the same problem, so not a regression, but nobody has specified it.

docs.text: MAW Prose · Fall 2026

docs.title: EVENTS_workday
docs.text:
One row per event per day. A projection, rebuilt at import, never edited.

Grain

One event on one workday. A five-day load-in is five rows.

Unresolved data file: EVENTS_WORKDAY.tsv

docs.title: Why it exists — and it is NOT a performance hedge
docs.text:
It was first offered as an escape hatch in case the range join proved slow. Michael found the real reason: a list view repeats per RECORD, so a one-row span cannot produce three agenda lines, and a WORKDAYS portal is fixed-height. The agenda REQUIRES this table.

The split that keeps it safe:

Table Holds Layer [EVENTS] IDENTITY — the upsert key, history, change counts canonical EVENTS_workday a PROJECTION for reports disposable

Both agenda shapes then come free: base a report HERE for one line per day, base it on EVENTS for one line with a date range.

docs.title: When it is built
docs.text:
At import, as the LAST step. Never at print.

  • Printing must not be a write. A read-only report that mutates data cannot run on a locked file, cannot run twice safely, and turns "reprint that PDF" into a schema operation.
  • Rebuild triggers: an import lands · the grid regenerates (page bounds or WeekStartDay moved) · on demand.
  • Full delete-and-rebuild for the calendar in scope. Safe precisely because it holds no identity, nothing points at it, and nothing is lost. See [Projection Law].

docs.title: ⭐ It SKIPS hidden days
docs.text:
A span crossing a hidden range (spring break) gets no rows for those days. Two things fall out of that:

  • Beckett's continuous-span problem solves itself on the agenda — the gap is real because the rows are absent, rather than a span silently reading as unbroken.
  • DayIndex / DayCount count working days, so "day 2 of 3" reads the way a person would say it.

docs.title: Where it sits in the print hub
docs.text:
Table Is Lifetime PRINT_PRESETS HOW to output reused forever [PRINT_SETS] WHAT to output, batched reused; one is scratch [PRINT_SET_ITEMS] one output + its overrides per line [PRINT_SESSIONS] WHAT HAPPENED one per produced PDF

docs.title: DocumentType (added 2026-08-08)
docs.text: A preset is scoped to a KIND of document. A calendar preset has no ShowVacancies; a contact-sheet preset has no WeekStartDay. Without this field, one flat option list serves every document and the table becomes legacy SETUP again.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
• Presets are reusable across productions. fkCalendar is NULLABLE: null = a house preset ("11x17 Full Company"), set = a one-off saved for this calendar.
  • This is what makes department filtering (the legacy next-step: "only light lab tasks") a preset row rather than a code change.
  • Legacy parity: the two PRINT_SET...Rlandscape scripts and exportORprint are what this table replaces as DATA.
  • ⬜ Department filtering needs a department field on EVENTS that does not exist yet — Corey's Production Note labels field is the candidate, unresolved (see [ClickUp Integration]).

  • Michael's rule: import sessions are inherently the snapshot; an edition is a published artifact plus live awareness of where we are in the process. That is the export side.
  • Consequence: watermark stops being a field you flip on the calendar and becomes a value on the run. FIRST / REVISED / UPDATED styled via STYLES, domain watermark.
  • Gives print-to-print diffing two stable endpoints, so "what moved since last print" no longer depends on a ClickUp automation firing.
  • Reissue is ROUTINE, not rare — zOLD/ holds 9 dated versions for Thought Crime, 8 for The Christians. Each reissue is a staffing milestone, not a formatting pass.

Michael's rule, and it is the important one: every imported event is handled elegantly whether or not it matches a standard event. fkStandardEvent is nullable on both [EVENTS] and [import_EVENTS]. An unmatched event still prints.

docs.title: Workdays
docs.text: MAW Prose · Fall 2026

docs.title: Workdays
docs.text:
One canonical row per real date. Calendar-agnostic.

🔴 READ THIS BEFORE YOU READ A FIELD — the grain CHANGED on 2026-08-12

WORKDAYS is CANONICAL-PER-DATE. One row per real calendar date, for the whole file. It is CALENDAR-AGNOSTIC and PRODUCTION-AGNOSTIC. Ruled by Michael 2026-08-12 (J19).

One date inside one calendar's week. The printed cell. WEEKS x 7. was the grain until this ruling, and it is the single most misleading sentence a cold agent can inherit here, because every remaining field on this table was designed under it.

The consequence, stated once and applied everywhere below: a workday row is SHARED. Sept 8 is ONE record that Big Love, the One Acts and a spring show all read. So any field expressing what ONE production or ONE calendar thinks about a date is ILLEGAL HERE — set it for one show and you have set it for every show that shares the date. That is not a style preference, it is silent cross-production data corruption, and it is the test to run against any field anyone proposes adding.

docs.title: Grain
docs.text:
Grain

One real date. Canonical. One row per date in the whole file. Not one row per date per calendar, and not one row per date per production.

18 rows · WORKDAYS.tsv

  • Generated, never typed.
  • Date is the identity. Unique + Not empty is a CONSTRAINT, not a convention — "one canonical workday per real date" is unenforceable without it, and duplicate rows for one date split every relationship that reads through it. Not recorded
  • Month colour resolves through MONTHS on a numeric month key, then through STYLES — never a 3-letter name. The legacy file joined on a display abbreviation. See J8.
  • ⚠️ Legacy table was Prodution WORKDAYS — misspelled, with a space. Do not inherit either.

docs.title: 🔴 What the ruling EVICTS from this table
docs.text:
Each of these is a per-calendar or per-production opinion sitting on a shared row. They are fix-queue items, not open questions.

Field Why it cannot live here Where it goes Title / TitleShort Thanksgiving is canonical; First Rehearsal is ONE production's name for a date. One field holds both kinds, so the table cannot tell them apart. The production-specific half becomes a Label on CALENDAR_EMPHASIS. A genuinely canonical day name belongs to a canonical holiday source, not to the grid cell. bool_HideFromCalendar Hiding is one calendar's decision about a date. Left here, one show hides a week for every show sharing it. A hide row on CALENDAR_EMPHASIS. 🔴 And it must BLANK THE CELL, never remove the record — a flowed found set shifts every subsequent day one column left. Manual_Override / ovr_ManualDate An override date on a table whose identity IS the date. Nowhere. Delete. Sort ⚠️ Unresolved under the new grain. To be confirmed A stamped print order is calendar-relative — two calendars covering the same dates can legitimately want different orders. Either it is per-calendar (so it moves to the projection) or it is a pure date sort (so it is derivable and should not be stored). Decide before the generator is written. fkWeek Points at WEEKS, which J8 PARKED with no known job. A relationship to a table with no purpose is not a path to a calendar. ⬜ Dead until J8's revive trigger fires: a report that needs to group BY week.

⭐ The pattern worth carrying out of this ruling: a field named for the only instance that existed. Title works today because one production is loaded. It breaks at production two, exactly like Contact Sheet HEADER (J10) and the unnamed default theme (J3). Third instance of the same tell.

docs.title: Where a production's opinion about a day DOES live
docs.text:
CALENDAR_EMPHASIS, keyed to the CALENDAR. It already carries every part of the need: AnchorMode = event matching through fkStandardEvent, a Label field whose documented job is what makes a printed legend possible, fkStyle, PadBefore/PadAfter, and a priority ladder.

🔴 The key is fkCalendar, NEVER fkProduction. EVENTS::fkCalendar exists precisely because "a production can have two calendars — stops a spring event printing on a fall grid." A day label keyed to the production prints on both of them.

docs.title: Per-vector resolution (added by J19)
docs.text:
Emphasis resolves ONE winner per day, so "Tech, Day 1" would compete with academic greying and one would lose. Resolve PER VECTOR instead, exactly as THEMES_x_STYLES does: Label from the highest-priority row that carries a label, fkStyle from the highest-priority row that carries a style, empty = no claim on that vector. A greyed Fall Break day can then still read "Load-in." Second instance of the mechanism, not a new one.

🚫 Ordinals are DERIVED, never stored. "Tech, Day 1 / 2 / 3" is position within the matched span, so the label is a template resolved unstored at render. Hand-numbering them means inserting one day makes every later number wrong with nothing flagging it — the same class of failure as stamping a resolved colour onto a record (J3).

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• EVENTS|span — a range relationship, not an equality. DATE >= Start_DATE, DATE <= End_DATE, fkCalendar =. One stored event row is seen by every day it covers, which is what lets a span stay whole. ⚠️ fkCalendar in that predicate is what keeps a canonical workday from showing every show's events at once — it was doing the scoping work all along, which is corroboration for this ruling rather than a change forced by it.
  • CALENDAR_EMPHASIS — RANGE, sorted Priority then span. Resolved live, never a stamped flag — stamping would mean regenerating every workday record to change one colour.
  • MONTHS — indexed equality on the numeric month, for colour. See J8.
  • fkWeek — see the eviction table.

docs.title: 🔴 Live contradiction — NOT resolved by this ruling
docs.text:
CALENDAR_EMPHASIS states plainly that HIDE deliberately did NOT move there and "hide stays a stamped flag on WORKDAYS driven by a range pair on the calendar," on the reasoning that hide changes which records EXIST in a found set while emphasis only styles records already there — a genuinely different verb. The 2026-08-09 11:49 ruling and this page say the opposite.

Both instructions are live in this doc set right now, and one of them is a fix-queue item about to be run. Verify on site The verb argument is real and is not answered by the grain ruling: emphasis-as-hide needs a resolver that can subtract a record, not just colour it. Michael's call, and it must be settled before either is built. 🚫 Do not implement one and quietly leave the other page contradicting it.

docs.title: Calculations
docs.text:
This section is the register, and that is deliberate

FileMaker has no screen that lists every calculation in a file. Manage > Database > Fields shows one table at a time and buries the formula behind a button. So this page is not a description of the calcs — it is where they are written down, and the build report collects every one across the whole doc set into a single grouped list.

One ### per calculation, each carrying an explicit {#calc-name} anchor. That anchor is a contract: any page can reach this one with @calc:table-workdays#calc-<name>. It is written by hand rather than left to the automatic heading slug because an automatic one is derived from the heading TEXT and lowercased — so retitling the heading would break every inbound link while both ends still looked perfectly fine.

⚠️ Both calcs below are typed Number in the file and cannot return what they are for. Verify on site Fix-queue item 6.

  • Unstored on purpose. It is display only; nothing joins on it and nothing sorts by it.
  • ⚠️ Never join on this. The legacy file matched a month colour against a 3-letter abbreviation and broke the first time a display string changed.
  • ⭐ Once MONTHS exists this can read MONTHS::NameShort through the relationship instead of hardcoding month names in a calc (J8).

docs.text:

  Right ( "0" & Month ( d ) ; 2 ) & "/" & Right ( "0" & Day ( d ) ; 2 )

  • Same rule: display only.
  • The numeric month is what STYLES resolves colour against, never this string.

Stored because it references only its own record's field, which keeps it indexable — and it must be indexed, because it is the join key into MONTHS.
