docs.title: Two anchor modes
docs.text:
AnchorMode Range comes from Use range typed DateStart / DateEnd spring break, a residency, dark days event matched EVENTS rows via fkStandardEvent Designer Run, Q2Q, load-in

⭐ event mode is the one that survives a reschedule. "Highlight Designer Run" resolves through EVENTS at render time, so when the run moves, the emphasis moves. A typed range would silently point at the old date.

  • event mode matches every event of that type in the production, so "all designer runs" is ONE row, not one per instance. This is the honest answer to recurrence: it works when the recurrence is a real event type, not when it is "every Monday."
  • Cost, stated plainly: two resolution predicates, one priority ladder. range resolves date-between; event resolves through the workday's events. Same sort, same winner rule, two relationships.
  • PadBefore / PadAfter extend an anchored emphasis outward in days (tech week = Q2Q anchored, padded back 3).

docs.title: Resolution rule (the load-bearing part)
docs.text:
Overlap is the NORMAL state, not an edge case — tech week sits inside the rehearsal block, opening weekend sits inside tech.

  1. Highest Priority wins.
  2. Tie → narrowest range wins. The specific thing is almost always the thing you meant to call out.
  3. Resolved LIVE through a sorted relationship from WORKDAYS (sorted Priority, then span). Not stamped: stamping would mean regenerating 68+ workday records to change one colour.

Convention that makes Priority easy: the academic calendar always loses to the production calendar visually. Spring break greyed under tech week red, never the reverse. Set academic rows low (10) and stop thinking about it. Increment by 10.

⚠️ A day with two claims prints ONE colour. MatchCount exists so the layout can mark a contested day instead of silently dropping the loser.

docs.title: Not supported in v1
docs.text:
• Half-day emphasis. Grain is the day. Ruled out by Michael.
  • Calendar-shape recurrence ("every Monday is dark"). Hand-enter the rows; accept that a one-week shift invalidates all of them. event mode covers the cases that are really event types.
  • Derived cross-production emphasis (greying another show's load-in on a shared stage). Type the range for now. This is the most likely v2 ask.

docs.title: Guards
docs.text:
• DateEnd ≥ DateStart. An inverted row matches nothing and reads as a broken feature.
  • Range must fall inside the calendar's bounds (Calendar_START → last week's end). Wrong-year entry is the boring failure that costs twenty minutes.

docs.title: Seams
docs.text:
• fkStyle → STYLES, domain emphasis. Emphasis never hardcodes a colour.
  • Label is not decoration: it is what makes a printed legend possible. The legacy file had no legend, so every colour on the 11x17 was tribal knowledge.
  • HIDE deliberately did NOT move here. Hide changes which records EXIST in the found set; emphasis only styles records that are already there. Different verb, so hide stays a stamped flag on WORKDAYS driven by a range pair on the calendar. ⚠️ The names "hide" and "lowlight" sound like one idea at two strengths and are built differently on purpose.
  • ⚠️ Lineage tradeoff: live resolution means reprinting an old PRINT_SESSIONS row renders with TODAY's emphasis rows, not the ones in effect at print time. Accepted; the paper was never authoritative.
  • 🪦 Legacy scripts checkHIGHlight / checkLOWlight are replaced by this relationship. checkHideWorkday survives.

docs.title: Append-only
docs.text: Nothing in the app edits or deletes a row here. This table IS the revision history — order by session and the timeline reads itself. That is why there is no separate EVENT_TRACKING / revisions table.

docs.title: 🔴 Upsert key = TaskID + fkProduction, never TaskID alone
docs.text:
URITP Productions in ClickUp is a labels (multi-select) field, so one event task can legitimately carry two shows. Each production's calendar prints its own copy, so the same TaskID must be able to exist twice — once per show.

Keying the upsert into EVENTS on TaskID alone means show two silently overwrites show one. Compound the key.

Mitigation on the ClickUp side: make the export view per-production, so one import session = one show. A cross-listed event then arrives in both sessions, which is correct.

docs.title: WatchHash
docs.text:
Auto-enter calculation, "Do not replace existing value" CHECKED. A plain calculation field recomputes, which rewrites history the first time the formula is touched.

Let ( ~d = "|" ;
  GetAsText ( Start_TIMESTAMP ) & ~d &
  GetAsText ( End_TIMESTAMP )   & ~d &
  Event_Name
)

The delimiter is load-bearing: without it "12" & "3" and "1" & "23" collide.

Watched set: start/end timestamps + event name. NOT modification stamps, style, or row order — otherwise "Q2Q moved 12 times" really means "you reimported 12 times." Same hash as the prior session for that TaskID = no real change. Counting distinct hashes = counting real changes.

docs.title: Timestamps are STORED, not unstored
docs.text: An unstored calculation re-evaluates on read, so fixing the parse formula later silently rewrites every historical row and moves every change count.

docs.title: Raw_Payload
docs.text: The whole original row/JSON, kept verbatim. An unmapped ClickUp field that turns out to matter in six months is already in the table instead of needing a re-import that can no longer be reproduced.

date_FirstRehearsal + date_Opening. Both are contractual facts about the show — negotiated with a director, true whether or not anyone ever prints a calendar. Both are typed by hand and can never be derived.

The hard line: a third production-level date is an EVENT, not a field. Designer deadline, build start, photo call — those move, repeat, or are one of many. Events already have a table, an import pipe, and a canonical type layer.

A date that can move, repeat, or be one of many is an EVENT. A date that is a defining property of the entity is a field.

21 rows · UTILITY_LOGS.tsv

Specced 2026-08-09. ⬜ Not built in the file. The script template has depended on this table since it was written, and INDEX.tsv has carried it as a gap the whole time.

docs.title: Why one table and not two
docs.text:
A file session and a script execution look like different things and they are not. Both start, both end, both either succeed or do not, and both want the same nine columns. Splitting them would duplicate every field to gain one distinction that a single indexed value already makes, and it would turn the most useful question in the table — what happened during this session — into a join instead of a sort.

SessionToken is what holds it together. The open row mints it, every script run inside that session carries it, and the close row ends it. Sort by token and you are reading one person's afternoon in order.

docs.title: The unfinished row is the point
docs.text:
A row with ts_Start and no ts_End is not a defect in this table. It is the only crash log the file will ever have.

FileMaker fires no close trigger on a crash, a force quit, a lost server connection or a killed process. So the close row is best-effort by nature, and treating its absence as an error would mean chasing a bug that is really a power cut. Read it the other way round: the open row is trustworthy, the close row is a bonus, and every unmatched open row is a session that ended badly and left you a note about it.

⚠️ Which means vl_Status = running is ambiguous forever unless something resolves it. A row saying running is either a session happening right now or a session that died in March.

⬜ The gap that closes it, and it does not exist yet: a UTIL · Sweep Abandoned Runs script, called from FILE · Open before anything else, that finds running rows whose SessionToken is not the current one and stamps them abandoned. Cheap, and it converts an ambiguous state into a countable one. Named here rather than written, because nobody asked for it and an unrequested script is a script nobody maintains.

docs.title: What must never be written here
docs.text:
🚫 No record data. Not a borrower, not a person, not a production title, not a payoff figure. A log is read by whoever is debugging, and a debugging surface is the last place anyone thinks to check before sharing a screenshot. json_Params is the loophole to watch: it captures the inbound parameter verbatim, so a script called with a name in its parameter puts that name in the log. Pass keys, never values.

🚫 No second log table. UTILITY_REPORTS is downstream of this one, per INDEX.tsv. It reads these rows; it does not keep its own.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text: • GLOBAL_USE|byLogPK — GLOBAL_USE::g_logPK = UTILITY_LOGS::PrimaryKey. ⬜ Not built. UTIL · Run End cannot work without it, and that is deliberate: with the relationship, Run End edits the log row through a global key from an anchor and never runs a find. Without it, every run-close is an Enter Find Mode, which the house rules forbid inline for good reason.

docs.title: calc_Duration
docs.text:
Unstored Number, from ts_Start and ts_End. Seconds a run took.

Case (
  IsEmpty ( ts_End ) or IsEmpty ( ts_Start ) ; "" ;
  GetAsNumber ( ts_End ) - GetAsNumber ( ts_Start )
)
  • Unstored because half of these rows have no end yet, and a stored calc on an empty operand stores the wrong answer rather than no answer.
  • Empty is a real result here and means still running, or never finished. Do not default it to zero; zero is a run that took no time, which is a different and much less alarming fact.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text: MAW Prose · Fall 2026

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
What the graph SHOULD be. The DDR is what it IS. The value is the diff.

Grain

One row per table occurrence. Grouped by the ANCHOR that owns it.

🔴 This file holds INTENT, never inventory. What should exist, why, which anchor owns it, whether creation is allowed through it. The DDR already generates what DOES exist — its overview line counts and lists every relationship on every export. Keeping a second hand-written list of the same fact is a second claimant, and the hand-written one always loses.

So: this is the plan, the DDR is the audit, and the useful artifact is the DIFF between them.

⚠️ It only survives if a row is written BEFORE the relationship is built. Written after, it is transcription, and transcription gets skipped on the first busy afternoon. Written before, it is the design step — decide the predicates and the create flag here, then go tick the boxes. The same reason the layouts TSV works.

🚫 Never write a relationship count on this page. The rows are the count.

docs.title: Why these columns
docs.text:
Most of them are self-evident. Two are not, and they are the reason the file exists:

  • Allow_Create — the transaction pattern depends on this checkbox and it is invisible on the graph. A relationship that silently lost it breaks a rebuild script with no error.
  • Used_By — which layout or script depends on the occurrence. This is what makes deleting one safe, and no DDR can tell you.

Sorted_By earns its place too: the sorted-relationship mechanism is load-bearing three separate times here — value lists, emphasis resolution, and span portals — and a sort living on the wrong side of a relationship has already cost an afternoon.

docs.title: Anchor and buoy
docs.text:
One anchor occurrence per table a layout is built on, with buoys hanging off it for everything that anchor must reach. Never one interconnected web.

Why: in a web-shaped graph, adding a relationship for a new report silently changes what existing layouts can see, and the symptom arrives on a printed page weeks later. In anchor and buoy, a change to one anchor's buoys cannot affect another anchor. Ever.

Cost, stated honestly: the graph gets wide. LOCATIONS may appear under several anchors. You will scroll — and you will never debug a cross-anchor side effect, because there cannot be one.

⚠️ A view | TABLE occurrence is used by its OWN layout and nothing else. The moment a portal on another anchor points at one, they become shared buoys and the web is back.

⚠️ Naming, corrected 2026-08-16: this page specified <ANCHOR>_<PATH>; the file uses <TABLE>_for_<ANCHOR> (STYLES_for_WORKDAYS, THEMES_X_STYLES_for_EVENTS). The file's version wins — it reads as a sentence and sorts by target table, which is how you actually hunt an occurrence. Documented convention updated to match the build.

docs.title: 🪦 Retired vocabulary · "HOUSE"
docs.text:
🚫 The word HOUSE is retired from this app's theme vocabulary as of 2026-08-16. The word is DEFAULT.

It came from the 08-09 config design, where the fallback theme was a record: ORGANIZATION.fkDefaultTheme was called the house theme because ORGANIZATION represented the company that owns the copy of the app, cascading PRODUCERS.fkTheme → house → magenta. In that model "house" carried real meaning: it named a level of ownership, distinct from a producer.

🔴 That cascade is not what got built. The file resolves the floor from GLOBAL_USE::g_pkDefaultTheme, true Global storage, set at startup. There is no ORGANIZATION hop and no producer hop in the styling chain — two globals, g_pkCurrentTheme and g_pkDefaultTheme, and that is the whole cascade.

⭐ So "house" now names a level that does not exist, which is worse than a merely unfamiliar word: it implies a hop a reader will go looking for. The theme named default is a row in THEMES; the global is g_pkDefaultTheme; the branch is the DEFAULT branch. One word, three surfaces, no translation.

⚠️ Historical note kept deliberately, because the ORGANIZATION cascade may still return for logos and brand, which is what that level was genuinely for. If it does, it will be a producer/organization cascade feeding the theme choice — not a fourth fallback rung inside the styling resolve.

docs.title: ✅ RESOLVED 2026-08-16 · the global-in-predicate fork
docs.text:
This page previously carried an open three-way fork: a relationship matches two occurrences only, so it "cannot reach GLOBAL_USE::g_currentCalendar from the WORKDAYS side." The three drafted options were (1) put the global field on WORKDAYS, (2) portal filter, (3) re-anchor the grid on GLOBAL_USE. It was flagged as also hitting STYLES_ACTIVE and STYLES_HOUSE, with decide once, apply to all three.

🔴 The premise was wrong, and that is why none of the three options was satisfying.

⭐ OPTION 4 — A GLOBAL FIELD IS READABLE FROM ANY CONTEXT IN A CALCULATION, WITH NO RELATIONSHIP AT ALL. That is what global storage is: one value, file-wide, not reached through the graph. So the source table does not need the global; it needs a calculation that references it.

STYLES::calc_ActiveThemeKey  =  GLOBAL_USE::g_pkCurrentTheme & ">" & PrimaryKey

Unstored (it must be — it references a global), and unstored is fine because it is the LEFT side of the relationship. Only the right side needs a stored, indexed field.

Why it beats all three drafted options:

Option Verdict 1 · global field on the source table 🚫 Second claimant on the session value. Two fields named for one truth, and nothing keeps them equal. 2 · portal filter 🚫 Display only. No effect on a found set, a report, or a PDF — and this app's whole purpose is print. 3 · re-anchor on GLOBAL_USE ⚠️ Works, and is right for a Home/dashboard layout that is about session state. Wrong for a data grid, whose anchor should be its own records. 4 · unstored calc reading the global ✅ One origin, no restructuring, works for found sets and print.

⚠️ The cost, stated: an unstored calc referencing a global cannot be indexed, so it may never be the right side of a relationship and never a stored match target. In this pattern it never is.

⚠️ Apply to all three as the original fork instructed: STYLES_ACTIVE, STYLES_DEFAULT (drafted as STYLES_HOUSE), and the WORKDAYS_EVENTS calendar predicate.

docs.title: 🎨 The theme resolution chain (the shape to build)
docs.text:
Full reasoning: [Theme Resolution] · observed state: [Theme State].

⭐ The two key calcs live on the STYLES BASE TABLE, so every occurrence of STYLES inherits them for free — STYLES_for_WORKDAYS, STYLES_for_EVENTS, and any future consumer. Fields are shared across occurrences; TOs are not. That is why extending this to a second anchor costs predicates and buoys, never fields.

ANCHOR: WORKDAYS  (the print grid)
  |
  +-- STYLES_for_WORKDAYS            StyleJoin_auto = calc_Key
  |     |                             (built 08-16)
  |     |
  |     +-- TXS_ACTIVE_for_WORKDAYS   calc_ActiveThemeKey  = calc_ThemeStyleKey
  |     |     |                        g_pkCurrentTheme & ">" & PrimaryKey
  |     |     +-- COLOR_ACTIVE_for_WORKDAYS    fkColor_Text = PrimaryKey
  |     |     +-- TYPE_ACTIVE_for_WORKDAYS     fkTypography = PrimaryKey
  |     |
  |     +-- TXS_DEFAULT_for_WORKDAYS  calc_DefaultThemeKey = calc_ThemeStyleKey
  |           |                        g_pkDefaultTheme & ">" & PrimaryKey
  |           +-- COLOR_DEFAULT_for_WORKDAYS   fkColor_Text = PrimaryKey
  |           +-- TYPE_DEFAULT_for_WORKDAYS    fkTypography = PrimaryKey

🔴 TWO parallel appearance branches, not one. Active and default. The per-vector coalesce needs both sides simultaneously, so it cannot be done by re-pointing one relationship.

🔴 A single composite predicate per hop, never two separate predicates. fkTheme + fkStyle as two predicates would need two match fields on the STYLES side; one composite key needs one. Same argument that produced calc_Key, one level down.

🔴 THEMES_x_STYLES needs a new stored key: calc_ThemeStyleKey = fkTheme & ">" & fkStyle, stored and indexed, and backfilled across all 18 existing rows — auto-enter does not populate rows that already exist.

⚠️ Verify what fkTheme and fkStyle actually STORE before writing that key. The table view displays default and monthLabel>january, which is either the stored value or a value-list display of a UUID. A composite built from a display label is not a key. If they store UUIDs, the composite is UUID-based and correct; if they store the readable strings, that is a separate finding.

⚠️ The four leaf occurrences are unavoidable. Text colour and typography are different tables, and active and default are different rows, so it is 2 × 2. Anchor–buoy forbids sharing them with the EVENTS chain — that duplication is the pattern working, not a cost of it.

docs.title: 🔴 The EVENTS branch has the same defect, and a flip-order trap
docs.text:
THEMES_X_STYLES_for_EVENTS matches on fkStyle alone — no theme predicate. It works today only because default is the only theme with rows, so one style matches exactly one record. Repoint it to calc_ActiveThemeKey = calc_ThemeStyleKey and mirror the default branch, exactly as WORKDAYS.

🔴 THE TRAP: g_pkCurrentTheme is set to URITP, which has zero appearance rows. The instant that predicate is repointed, every event style on every layout goes blank, because URITP>... matches nothing and the default branch does not exist yet to catch it. ⚠️ It looks like the change broke the relationship, when it actually started telling the truth — the old match was hiding an unset theme.

✅ Safe orders: set g_pkCurrentTheme to default FIRST, then repoint · or build both branches and the resolve calc in one sitting, then flip the global. 🚫 Never repoint and then go build the default branch afterwards — that leaves the file visibly broken between two edits, which is exactly when a session gets interrupted.

docs.title: The floor
docs.text:
✅ GLOBAL_USE already holds both halves as true Global storage: g_pkCurrentTheme and g_pkDefaultTheme. 🔴 So the default-theme floor is a GLOBAL, not ORGANIZATION.fkDefaultTheme — the 08-09 plan put it on a record and the file put it in session state. The 08-09 open item is satisfied differently than written, and every doc claiming the floor is missing is stale.

⚠️ But a global is volatile: something must SET it at startup, and an empty g_pkDefaultTheme prints the whole file magenta. OnFirstWindowOpen owns that, and the completeness report must check it. This is the one real advantage the record-based design had, and it is now a startup obligation instead of a stored fact.

docs.text: Written before a single relationship exists, it surfaced: two blocked anchors (no PEOPLE table, no STANDARD_DOCS) · two joins that cannot work until an index is added (the crosswalk, the upsert) · one grain mismatch in the layouts plan (highlights hanging off an export set rather than a calendar) · and three misspelled keys that must be fixed before a relationship binds them.

docs.title: Custom Functions
docs.text:
What this app installs, what it authors, and the one test that decides which.

Grain

One page per function this app AUTHORS. Installed-from-canonical functions are listed, never copied.

docs.title: 🔴 The rule: canonical is INSTALLED, app-level is AUTHORED, and the test is one question
docs.text:
Does this need to be true in every solution, or only in this one?

Everything in the first bucket lives in maw-prose and is pulled, never restated here — a copy is a second claimant that goes stale the first time the original moves, and three retired manifests in brain-config are the evidence. Everything in the second is a house convention that would tax other files for nothing.

docs.title: Installed from canonical — pointers only
docs.text:
The JSON script-parameter family, nine functions, at maw-prose → standards/filemaker/custom-functions/json-params/.

PText · PNum · PBool · PJSON · Param · ParamHas · ParamGetText · ParamGetNumber · ParamGetBoolean

⬜ Not installed in this file yet Not recorded, and everything in 70-scripts/ assumes them. ⚠️ Param uses While ( ), so FileMaker 19.6 or later — the file's options currently declare a minimum of 12, and in an older file the family does not partially work, it does not compile.

🔴 Install order is not optional: four builders → Param → ParamHas → the three readers. Each reader calls ParamHas.

⚠️ Verify by BEHAVIOUR, never by a version note. FileMaker cannot read its own function bodies at runtime, so a version stamp is a label a human sets and a human forgets — it reports health it no longer has. The canonical folder ships conformance.json, twelve calculations and the exact text each must return. Run it after installing and again whenever the utility reports run. When a vector fails, the canonical definition wins and the installed copy is what is wrong.

docs.title: Authored here
docs.text: • ErrJSON — the failure payload every script returns. Read its page before adding a second function to this list; it carries the whole canonical-versus-app-level argument, including the reason it is not in the shared family and the trigger that would promote it.

docs.title: ⚠️ Adding one
docs.text:
Check the canonical folder FIRST. ErrJSON was specced into four script pages before anyone read the family contract that names its exact shape as forbidden — the rule was one day old and nobody looked.

Then ask the one question at the top. If the answer is "every solution," it does not belong here at all, and the right move is a proposal against maw-prose, not a file in this folder. 🚫 And never merge a new idea into an existing canonical family — a family stays the size it declared; a new idea gets its own folder beside it.

docs.title: Not here
docs.text:
🚫 Scripts are not custom functions, however small. A function returns a value and does nothing; a script does something. Conflating the two is the same family-discipline failure this folder exists to refuse — see the scripts index for the parallel one-taxonomy ruling.

docs.title: ErrJSON
docs.text: MAW Prose · Fall 2026

docs.title: ErrJSON
docs.text:
The failure payload every script returns. App-level on purpose - the canonical family refuses this shape.

Grain

One call per failure. Builds the JSON a script returns when it did not do its job.

/* ErrJSON ( code ; where ; comment )
   The failure payload. Composes the canonical family; adds no syntax.
   Requires: Param, PBool, PNum, PText installed first. */

Param (
    List (
        PBool ( "ok"      ; 0 ) ;
        PNum  ( "error"   ; code ) ;
        PText ( "where"   ; where ) ;
        PText ( "comment" ; comment )
    )
)

Called by FIND · All Or None, UTIL · Value Index Move, FIND · Values and FILE · Save Backup. Replaces the retired exit w/ errors, which could never work.

docs.title: 🔴 The canonical family REFUSES this function, and the refusal is correct
docs.text:
maw-prose → standards/filemaker/custom-functions/json-params/ is the canonical nine, and its contract says, in a section headed Keep the family at nine:

No array builders, no object-graph helpers beyond PJSON, no required-key validator framework, and no result-builder wrappers… a tenth function is a claim that the layer became a language.

ErrJSON is a result-builder wrapper. It is the named example.

⚠️ I specced it into four script pages on 2026-08-09 without reading that file. The rule is one day old, it is well argued, and it stands. This page exists because the function was already load-bearing before anyone checked whether it was allowed.

docs.title: So why does it exist at all
docs.text:
The ban is scoped to the FAMILY, and the family's own reasoning says why. Those nine are installed in every solution, so a tenth taxes every file forever and has to be held in every head. An app-level function taxes one file. Different cost, different answer.

⭐ The test that decides it, and it is the one to reuse: does this need to be true in every solution, or only in this one? A parameter-building vocabulary is the first. What our error payload looks like is the second — it is a house convention, not a language feature.

docs.title: 🔴 The promotion trigger, written now so it is not improvised later
docs.text:
The moment a SECOND app wants an error payload, it does NOT write its own. Two apps with two error shapes is the divergence that makes ok mean different things in different files, and it is the failure this whole family was consolidated to prevent.

It gets promoted to a SIBLING canonical folder — standards/filemaker/custom-functions/error-payload/ — 🚫 never merged into json-params/. That folder's rule survives promotion: a family stays at nine and a new idea gets its own folder.

docs.title: ⚠️ It must not grow, and the pressure to grow it is obvious
docs.text:
A fifth argument. An ErrJSONFrom ( ) that reads Get ( LastError ) itself. A success twin. Every one of those is the family-becomes-a-language failure, one level down, in a file with no contract to refuse it.

If a caller needs more than these four keys, it builds the payload inline with Param. That is not a workaround — it is the reason the canonical family exists, and inline is where an unusual shape belongs.

docs.title: 🔴 error: 0 is a REFUSAL, not a success, and this is the trap
docs.text:
Four call sites pass 0:

ErrJSON ( 0 ; "FIND · All Or None" ; "mode is required" )

0 is FileMaker's code for "no error," so the payload reads ok: 0, error: 0 — which looks self-contradictory and is not.

⭐ It means WE refused, FileMaker did not fail. A missing mandatory parameter is a rejection by the script, and there is no FileMaker error code for the caller wrote the wrong thing. Inventing a private code would put a number in the log that no Claris reference explains.

So the contract is: read ok FIRST, always. error is diagnostic detail, never the test. A caller branching on error ≠ 0 treats every validation refusal as a success.

⬜ Named, not chosen: a distinct reason key ("validation" against "filemaker") would make it self-describing at the cost of a fifth argument this page just argued against. Michael's, if the ambiguity ever bites. To be confirmed

docs.title: 🚫 PII: where and comment are LOGGED
docs.text:
Both land in UTILITY_LOGS::Comment through UTIL · Run End. Same rule as json_Params: pass keys, ids and step names, never values.

⚠️ And the tempting call is the wrong one. ErrJSON ( err ; "Perform Find" ; $searchTerm ) is exactly what you want while debugging and exactly what puts a person's name in a permanent log. Pass the FIELD you searched, never what you searched for.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
After the canonical nine — it calls four of them, so entering it first fails validation. It is not in conformance.json and should not be added to it: that fixture audits the shared family against its canonical definition, and an app-level function in it would make the file's conformance check depend on this app's private conventions.

docs.title: 🔴 The ruling: ONE taxonomy, and the name prefix is it
docs.text:
The file currently has two filing systems running at once. Six folders (00_APP, File OPERATIONS, 80-GOTO, 90-UTILITY, LOGS, SHOW & HIDE) and, separately, name prefixes that do not match them.

The prefix wins, and folders mirror it 1:1. The prefix is what survives into a DDR, a Perform Script picker, an export and a version of FileMaker with no folders; a folder is a view. Two filing systems means one of them is always the stale one, and nothing tells you which.

The consequence is small and worth stating: LOGS, SHOW & HIDE and File OPERATIONS go away. They are topic folders, and topics cut across prefixes — SHOW & HIDE holds a FIND ·, LOGS holds a UTIL ·, File OPERATIONS holds a FILE ·. Each one is a third axis that will eventually disagree with both of the others.

00 FILE      FILE · Open · FILE · Close · FILE · Save Backup
10 GOTO      GOTO · Utility Logs · GOTO · Values
20 FIND      FIND · Values · FIND · All Or None
30 SHOW      (empty)
40 BUILD     (empty)
50 EXPORT    (empty)
90 UTIL      UTIL · Run Start · UTIL · Run End · UTIL · Value Index Move
_TEMPLATE    _TEMPLATE · New Script

⚠️ Empty folders are deliberate. They are the build order, visible every time the script workspace is opened. A folder created the day it is first needed gets named on the fly and is how the second taxonomy started.

docs.title: House rule for anything written here
docs.text: 🔴 Set Error Capture [On] plus a Get(LastError) check after every write — branching on the code, not on ≠ 0, because 401 after a find is an answer and not a failure. A swallowed error means the caller believes a write landed; an invented one means an empty list reads as a crash. Legacy had scripts that failed silently and one that shipped with a live debug dialog.

docs.title: _TEMPLATE · New Script
docs.text: MAW Prose · Fall 2026

docs.title: _TEMPLATE · New Script
docs.text:
Duplicate this to start every script. The house rules live in the header on purpose.

Grain

One starting point for every script in the file. Duplicate, rename, delete what does not apply.

The rules are written inside the script rather than in this page, because a rule you have to go and look up is a rule that gets skipped. They are meant to get shorter over time as the instincts form — strike a line when it is genuinely automatic, do not delete the file.

docs.title: The template
docs.text:
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# <SCRIPT NAME>
# Purpose:
# Params (JSON):
# Returns (JSON):
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# HOUSE RULES - delete a line only when it truly does not apply
#  1. Error capture is LINE ONE. A subscript cannot set it.
#  2. Check Get(LastError) after EVERY risky step. Capture
#     hides the dialog, it does not handle the error.
#     Branch on the CODE: 401 after a find is an answer.
#  3. No inline Enter Find Mode. Call FIND-Entity.
#  4. No inline Go to Layout. Call GOTO-Destination.
#  5. Params in and out are JSON, even for one value.
#     Default ONLY where a wrong guess cannot go unnoticed.
#  6. No domain strings typed in calcs. Custom function.
#  7. Inside a transaction, nothing that implicitly commits
#     (Go to Layout / Go to Record / New Record / Show All).
#  8. Land on util_TABLE, never a user-facing layout.
#  9. Run Start and Run End wrap the work. Always both,
#     and the failure paths pass their OWN status.
# 10. ONE exit shape, on the LAST line. Falling off the end
#     returns the last SUBSCRIPT's result, not nothing.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════

Set Error Capture [ On ]
Allow User Abort [ Off ]

Set Variable [ $p     ; Get ( ScriptParameter ) ]
Perform Script [ UTIL · Run Start ]
Set Variable [ $ctx   ; Get ( ScriptResult ) ]
Set Variable [ $logPK ; JSONGetElement ( $ctx ; "logPK" ) ]

#  -- work ------------------------------------------


#  -- close -----------------------------------------
Perform Script [ UTIL · Run End ; JSON: logPK, status, comment ]
Exit Script [ JSONSetElement ( "{}" ; "ok" ; 1 ; JSONNumber ) ]

docs.title: Why each rule is there
docs.text:
1 · Error capture is line one. FileMaker restores the error-capture state when a subscript returns, so a UTIL · Set Up script that turns it on gives the caller nothing. The centralised version everyone writes first is a silent no-op. This one line cannot be delegated.

2 · Capture without a check is worse than no capture. Set Error Capture suppresses the dialog; it does not handle the error. Turn it on and skip the check and the script sails past a failed find, a failed commit or a failed write and reports success. Capture, act, check, branch.

⚠️ And it goes wrong in both directions, which is why the rule now says branch on the CODE. If [ Get ( LastError ) ≠ 0 ] after Perform Find fires on 401, "no records match" — a normal, correct outcome — and turns an empty list into a crash. Same for 101 at the end of a found set. (Live instance: status_index_move, 2026-08-09.)

3 and 4 · Chokepoints. Every search for an entity goes through one FIND · script; every navigation through one GOTO ·. FileMaker has no grep — a DDR lists fields, not the fifty places Enter Find Mode was typed. In a searchable codebase inline is recoverable; here it is not. It is also what makes a later change (an org predicate, a renamed layout) one edit instead of a hunt.

5 · JSON parameters. A positional parameter list cannot gain an argument without breaking every caller. JSON can.

docs.title: 🔴 5a · The default test, and it is the rule this file got wrong most often
docs.text:
Four defaults in this folder were written the same way and only two of them were defensible. The test that separates them, arrived at 2026-08-10:

Default ONLY where a wrong guess cannot go unnoticed.

Not how likely is the caller to omit it — how visible is the damage when they do.

Live case Default Verdict UTIL · Run End status → ok a run succeeded 🔴 KILLED. You only read the log because something broke, and it says nothing did. Invisible by construction new_UTILITY_LOG kind → script read from the wrong variable 🔴 RETIRED. Fired on EVERY row. A default that fires when nobody omitted anything is not a default, it is a constant UTIL · Run Start kind → script the caller is a script ✅ KEPT. One obviously-wrong row per day, one exception, and it passes explicitly FIND · All Or None mode → abort nothing 🔴 KILLED. abort was also a legal input, so forgot and meant-it were the same branch

⭐ Three ways to be safe, in order of preference: no default and treat empty as an error · a CONSPICUOUS default that nothing legitimately produces · a plain default whose wrongness is visible on sight. The conspicuous one is the magenta pattern borrowed straight from the theme cascade — a value nothing real generates, so hitting it is proof of a break rather than a guess that might be right. Run End's unreported is the live example.

🚫 Never a default that is also a plausible real value. The fallback firing and the system working then look identical, forever, with nothing to tell them apart.

6 · No domain strings in calcs. A vl_Domain comparison against "event-status" typed into a calculation returns FALSE forever if it is misspelled, silently, with nothing to highlight it. Custom function, one definition, autocompletes.

7 · Implicit commits break transactions. FileMaker's only rollback is: edit everything through relationships from one anchor record, then a single Commit Records, with Revert Record on error. Go to Layout, Go to Record, New Record and Show All Records all commit — which is why this discipline has to be adopted before the habits form.

8 · Script-only layouts. A script needs a layout for context. If it borrows a user-facing one, redesigning that layout breaks the script and the breakage is silent. It also destroys whatever the user was looking at.

9 · Run Start / Run End. UTIL · Run Start writes the UTILITY_LOGS row and returns the entry context. UTIL · Run End writes the outcome and puts the user back where they were. An unlogged run is indistinguishable from one that never happened.

🔴 Every failure path passes its OWN status. Run End cannot see what happened upstream. Forget it and the row now reads unreported rather than ok — visible, but still a hole in the record. This is the single easiest thing in the whole pattern to forget.

🔴 10 · One exit shape, on the last line. Added 2026-08-09 after it nearly locked the file open. Omitting Exit Script does not return nothing — FileMaker persists the last subscript's result up to the caller (Claris Community). So a script that falls off the end hands back a value produced by something else entirely, and the caller cannot tell.

Two live instances the same day: Show ALL or NONE{ .dr-mark-link .dr-mark--cls-alias .dr-mark--box .dr-gloss data-gloss="A RETIRED NAME. Point it at the live one so paperwork quoting the old name still lands: fkCal. For an old VALUE rather than an old name, use was." data-role-print="A RETIRED NAME. Point it at the live one so paperwork quoting the old name still lands: fkCal. For an old VALUE rather than an old name, use was." }, whose success branches return the previous subscript's result to anyone checking; and FILE · Close, where the inherited result is the close veto and declining a backup prompt stopped the file from shutting. A trailing Exit Script is not tidiness. It is the only way a script controls its own answer.

⚠️ Allow User Abort [ Off ] is in the template because Escape mid-transaction leaves records half-written and uncommitted. It also disables the debugger's abort — turn it back On while developing.

docs.title: Script naming
docs.text:
Older FileMaker has no script folders and sorts alphabetically, so the prefix is the folder:

  • _TEMPLATE · — this file
  • FILE · — the file's own lifecycle: Open, Close, Save Backup. Fired from File Options, not by a person
  • FIND · — one per entity, returns a found set
  • GOTO · — one per destination. The whole body is Go to Layout. Nothing else, ever
  • SHOW · — sets state, then calls GOTO ·. The door a human or a button uses
  • UTIL · — Run Start, Run End, registry refreshers
  • BUILD · — generators (workdays, projections, theme rows)
  • EXPORT · — the print/export chain

⚠️ FILE · was missing from this list until 2026-08-09 while two specced scripts already used it. A naming standard that does not list a prefix in live use is how a file ends up with two conventions — which is exactly what happened in the script workspace. Add the prefix here in the same pass as the first script that uses it.

🔴 GOTO · and SHOW · are two scripts on purpose. A utility script needs to land somewhere without disturbing state; a person needs to arrive somewhere meaningful. Collapse them and every internal jump silently rewrites the user's current calendar.

Folders mirror the prefixes 1:1 and hold nothing else. See the scripts index for the one-taxonomy ruling — a folder that does not correspond to a prefix is a second filing system, and one of the two always goes stale.

docs.title: 🔴 DOCUMENTING a script — the page has rules too, and they were broken first
docs.text:
The rules above govern the script. This section governs its PAGE, and it exists because the first eleven pages in this folder were written without it.

Every FileMaker object named in prose gets its marker. [UTIL · Run Start](@script:script-util-run-start) · [fkCalendar](@rel:table-events) · [dateFormat]{.calc} · [$$SESSION.token]{.global} · [OnFirstWindowOpen]{.trigger} · [vl_Kind]{.vl} · [util_VALUES]{.layout}.

Every claim you did not verify gets {.tbc} or {.verify}. Every thing that should exist and does not gets {.gap}. Every retired name gets {.alias}, pointed at the live one.

⭐ The reason is not tidiness, and it is the thing that was missed: a callout and an emoji are read by a HUMAN ON THAT PAGE. A marker is amassed at build time into the report, across the whole site. So ⬜ not verified in prose and {.tbc} look equally serious to the person writing them, and only one of them can answer what is unconfirmed across this whole app. Writing the first and skipping the second produces a build report that says the tree is clean.

🔴 Prefer the LINK form for script, rel, calc, vl, layout and alias. A span records a MENTION; a link records an EDGE, and the edges are what turn this folder into a call graph instead of a list of names. A dead reference never degrades into a span — it renders as a visible broken marker — so only link to an id that exists.

🚫 Never put a marker inside a verbatim code block. A marker inside evidence is an edit to the evidence, and it would not render anyway.

⚠️ status: is REQUIRED in the frontmatter. A page without one is reported as NOT BUILT, its id never registers, and every link pointing at it breaks silently. Six pages in this folder shipped without it on 2026-08-09.

docs.title: FILE · Close
docs.text: MAW Prose · Fall 2026

docs.title: FILE · Close
docs.text:
Closes the session row. The one script in the file that must not return JSON.

Grain

One run per clean file close. Set in File Options → When closing → Perform script.

Retired name: 00App__onLastWindowClose{ .dr-mark-link .dr-mark--cls-alias .dr-mark--box .dr-gloss data-gloss="A RETIRED NAME. Point it at the live one so paperwork quoting the old name still lands: fkCal. For an old VALUE rather than an old name, use was." data-role-print="A RETIRED NAME. Point it at the live one so paperwork quoting the old name still lands: fkCal. For an old VALUE rather than an old name, use was." }. Fires from: OnLastWindowClose.

docs.title: 🔴 This script is the documented exception to house rule 5
docs.text:
House rule 5 says params in and out are JSON, always. This script returns True instead, and it has to.

FileMaker treats the close handler's result as a veto: return false and the file does not close. Our template ends every script with Exit Script [ JSONSetElement ( ... ) ], a text result, and a text result evaluated as a boolean is not something to gamble a file's closability on. A file that will not shut is a worse bug than an unlogged close, and it is the kind you discover at the wrong moment.

So the JSON contract stops at the door. Rule 5 governs scripts talking to other scripts; this one talks to FileMaker.

docs.title: 🔴 The veto trap, found live 2026-08-09
docs.text:
The first close handler entered into the file was fkCal. For an old VALUE rather than an old name, use was.">00App__onLastWindowClose, and it had no Exit Script at all. It ended on a Perform Script call to FILE · Save Backup, which exits with a text result when the user declines the prompt.

That combination locks the file open. FileMaker persists a subscript's result up to its caller when the caller does not set one of its own (Claris Community), so the close handler's result became the backup script's result, and the close handler's result is a veto. Decline the backup → the file refuses to close. Reproduced by reasoning from first-party docs, not yet reproduced in the file

⭐ Omitting Exit Script is not neutral here, and that is the part that catches people. It does not mean no result; it means whatever the last subscript happened to return. The handler inherits a decision made by a script that knows nothing about closing files.

🔴 So Exit Script [ True ] is unconditional and it is the last step, always, on every path. Not inside a branch. Not skipped when there is nothing to log. A close handler with a conditional exit is a file with a conditional ability to close.

docs.title: 🚫 Do not call the backup from here
docs.text: It was built that way. Move it. FILE · Save Backup carries the full argument; the short version is that a close-triggered backup misses every session that ended badly — a crash fires no OnLastWindowClose — which is the only kind of session anyone has ever wanted a backup for. It runs from FILE · Open instead, where it copies the last known-good state before the day's edits start.

docs.title: The script
docs.text:
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# FILE · Close
# Purpose: close the session's log row
# Params (JSON): none
# Returns: True. NOT JSON - the result is a close veto
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════

Set Error Capture [ On ]
Allow User Abort [ Off ]

If [ not IsEmpty ( $$SESSION.logPK ) ]
    Perform Script [ UTIL · Run End ; Parameter:
    Param (
        List (
            PText ( "logPK"   ; $$SESSION.logPK ) ;
            PText ( "status"  ; "ok" ) ;
            PText ( "comment" ; "file closed cleanly" )
        )
    ) ]
End If

Exit Script [ True ]

Calls UTIL · Run End. Reads $$SESSION.logPK.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
The If is load-bearing. If FILE · Open failed to log, $$SESSION.logPK is empty and Run End would be called with nothing to close. Guarding here keeps the failure in one place instead of producing a second error at the exact moment the file is trying to shut.

Everything here is best-effort and the design assumes it. A crash, a force quit, a lost server connection or a killed process fires no close trigger at all. That is not a hole to plug — see utility logs, where an open row with no close is read as the crash log rather than as a missing write.

⚠️ Do not add work to this script. Every step is a step between the user clicking close and the file closing, and it runs at the moment they have already decided to leave. Log the close and get out of the way. The backup was the first thing to try to move in here; it will not be the last.

⚠️ Show Custom Dialog is banned in this script and in everything it calls. A dialog on the close path is a prompt the user answers after deciding to leave, and its answer feeds the veto. If a close-time question is ever genuinely needed, ask it somewhere the answer is not also a vote on whether the file may shut.

docs.title: Naming
docs.text: The live script is fkCal. For an old VALUE rather than an old name, use was.">00App__onLastWindowClose — double underscore, against three single-underscore siblings, and a second naming convention alongside the FILE · prefix this folder committed to. Rename to FILE · Close. See the scripts index for the one-taxonomy ruling.

docs.text: MAW Prose · Fall 2026

docs.title: FILE · Open
docs.text:
The session starts here. Mints the token, logs the open, then does the file's setup work.

Grain

One run per file session. Set in File Options → When opening → Perform script, not on a layout trigger.

This is the only place a session token is created. Everything else in the file inherits it.

🔴 BLOCKED. Do not enter this script yet. APP_SESSIONS is a second claimant on UTILITY_LOGS and nothing has ruled which table holds the session row — so this script does not know where to write. Full argument on trigger_App_Open. Not recorded

Three scripts claim this handler: 00App_onFirstWindowOpen To be confirmed, trigger_App_Open, App_Startup. Only one can be set in File Options, and nothing in the file records which one won Verify on site.

docs.title: The script
docs.text:
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# FILE · Open
# Purpose: start the session, log it, run file setup
# Params (JSON): none
# Returns: nothing meaningful. Fires from File Options
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════

Set Error Capture [ On ]
Allow User Abort [ Off ]

Set Variable [ $$SESSION.token ; Get ( UUID ) ]

Perform Script [ UTIL · Run Start ; Parameter:
Param (
    List (
        PText ( "sessionToken" ; $$SESSION.token ) ;
        PText ( "kind"         ; "session" ) ;
        PText ( "scriptName"   ; "FILE · Open" ) ;
        PText ( "comment"      ; "file opened" )
    )
) ]
Set Variable [ $$SESSION.logPK ; ParamGetText ( Get ( ScriptResult ) ; "logPK" ; "" ) ]

#  -- file setup ------------------------------------
Perform Script [ FILE · Save Backup ]
#  auto_LAYOUTS refresh (upsert, never rebuild)
#  g_ defaults, including g_currentOrg
#  landing layout via SHOW ·

Exit Script [ True ]

Mints $$SESSION.token and $$SESSION.logPK. Calls UTIL · Run Start and FILE · Save Backup. Fires from OnFirstWindowOpen.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
$$SESSION.token and $$SESSION.logPK are global variables and that is deliberate. They have to outlive this script and be readable from every other one. A $ variable dies at the last Exit Script and a field would mean a write on every read; a global is the only lifetime that fits a session.

Get ( UUID ) is line one of the body and cannot fail, so nothing can happen between minting the token and using it. That is the fix for trigger_App_Open's defect, where the token was set three lines after the row was written and an error in between orphaned the session.

⚠️ This handler already had a second job before logging existed. INDEX.tsv describes auto_LAYOUTS as generated on file open for front lazy menu loading, so the open script is an orchestrator that happens to log first, not a logging script. Keep the log call at the top: if the setup work fails, the session row already exists to record that it did.

🔴 The backup runs from HERE, not from the close handler — added 2026-08-09. FILE · Save Backup carries the argument: a close-triggered backup misses every session that crashed, and those are the only sessions anyone ever wanted a backup for. It is placed after the log call on purpose, so a backup that fails is recorded in a session row that already exists.

⚠️ It is also the slowest thing in the open path. A multi-MB file copy runs before the user sees a layout. If that becomes intolerable, the answer is a button rather than a faster copy — and the log row is what will tell you how long it actually takes Verify on site.

⚠️ g_currentOrg must be set here. Empty at startup means every token resolves to magenta and the whole file prints unstyled. The theme cascade has no other entry point.

⚠️ Allow User Abort [ Off ] disables the debugger's abort. Turn it back on while developing this script specifically — a file-open script you cannot escape is a file you cannot get into.

⬜ The abandoned-run sweep belongs here and is not written Not recorded. See utility logs: a running row carrying a stale token is a crashed session, and nothing currently resolves it.

docs.text:
Timestamped copy of the file into ./zBACKUPS/. Fires on OPEN, not on close.

Grain

One copy of the whole .fmp12 per run. Called by FILE · Open, and by a Back up now.

docs.title: 🔴 The ruling: this fires on OPEN, not on close
docs.text:
It was built on OnLastWindowClose. Move it. Three reasons, and the third one is the one that matters.

1 · The close handler is a veto surface. Anything called from it can stop the file from closing — see FILE · Close. A backup that can wedge the file shut is a worse problem than the one it solves.

2 · A backup on close misses every session you actually want backed up. No close trigger fires on a crash, a force quit, a lost connection or a killed process. The sessions that end badly are exactly the sessions that produce nothing — and those are the only ones where you would ever reach for a backup.

3 · ⭐ On open you are copying a file nobody has touched yet. Same argument the projection layer already runs on: back up the last known-good state, before today's edits, not the state produced by a session that may have gone wrong. On close you preserve the damage. On open you preserve the last version that was fine.

⚠️ The cost, stated honestly: you lose the final session's work if you never reopen the file. That is the trade, and it is the right side of it — a session's work is also sitting in the live file, which is not gone; a backup exists for when the live file is.

docs.title: The script
docs.text:
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# FILE · Save Backup
# Purpose: timestamped copy of this file into ./zBACKUPS/
# Params (JSON): prompt (bool, default 0)
# Returns (JSON): ok, skipped, reason, path
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════

Set Error Capture [ On ]
Allow User Abort [ Off ]

Set Variable [ $p ; Get ( ScriptParameter ) ]

#  -- 1. platform gate ------------------------------
#  Save a Copy as does not exist on FileMaker Go.
If [ PatternCount ( Get ( ApplicationVersion ) ; "Go" ) ]
    Exit Script [ Param ( List (
        PBool ( "ok"      ; 1 ) ;
        PBool ( "skipped" ; 1 ) ;
        PText ( "reason"  ; "FileMaker Go cannot save a copy" ) ) ) ]
End If

#  -- 2. hosted gate --------------------------------
#  A hosted file is backed up by the server, not by us.
If [ not IsEmpty ( Get ( HostName ) ) ]
    Exit Script [ Param ( List (
        PBool ( "ok"      ; 1 ) ;
        PBool ( "skipped" ; 1 ) ;
        PText ( "reason"  ; "file is hosted" ) ) ) ]
End If

#  -- 3. optional prompt ----------------------------
If [ ParamGetBoolean ( $p ; "prompt" ; 0 ) ]
    Show Custom Dialog [ "Save a backup?" ]
    If [ Get ( LastMessageChoice ) = 2 ]
        Exit Script [ Param ( List (
            PBool ( "ok"      ; 1 ) ;
            PBool ( "skipped" ; 1 ) ;
            PText ( "reason"  ; "declined" ) ) ) ]
    End If
End If

#  -- 4. build the destination ----------------------
#  Read the path live. Never trust a stored one.
Set Variable [ $path ; Get ( FilePath ) ]
Set Variable [ $dir  ; Left ( $path ;
    Position ( $path ; "/" ; Length ( $path ) ; -1 ) ) ]

Set Variable [ $ts ;
    Year ( Get ( CurrentDate ) )
    & Right ( "0" & Month  ( Get ( CurrentDate ) ) ; 2 )
    & Right ( "0" & Day    ( Get ( CurrentDate ) ) ; 2 )
    & "-"
    & Right ( "0" & Hour   ( Get ( CurrentTime ) ) ; 2 )
    & Right ( "0" & Minute ( Get ( CurrentTime ) ) ; 2 ) ]

Set Variable [ $file ; $dir & "zBACKUPS/"
    & Get ( FileName ) & " " & $ts & ".fmp12" ]

#  -- 5. write --------------------------------------
Save a Copy as [ "$file" ; copy of current file ; Create folders: On ]
If [ Get ( LastError ) ≠ 0 ]
    Exit Script [ ErrJSON ( Get ( LastError ) ; "Save a Copy as" ; $file ) ]
End If

Exit Script [ Param ( List (
    PBool ( "ok"      ; 1 ) ;
    PBool ( "skipped" ; 0 ) ;
    PText ( "path"    ; $file ) ) ) ]

Calls ErrJSON and the canonical JSON parameter family — see custom functions.

🚫 The $file passed to ErrJSON is a FILE PATH, and that is deliberate. A path is a location, not a person; it is the one thing worth having in the log when a backup fails. Never widen it — that function's page carries the rule, and the tempting call is the one that logs a value instead of a key.

docs.title: Why each piece
docs.text:
⭐ Reading Get ( FilePath ) live is right and it was right in the original. It carries the platform prefix (file: / filemac:) already correct, so slicing the directory off the front of it means the destination inherits the prefix for free. Hand-building a path is how you get a script that works on one machine.

Position ( … ; Length ( $path ) ; -1 ) walks backwards to the last separator. The negative occurrence is a real feature and the tidiest way to get a parent directory in FileMaker.

🔴 The timestamp is zero-padded on purpose. Month ( … ) returns 8, not 08, so an unpadded stamp sorts 20260810 after 2026810 and the folder is scrambled permanently. It is also built from the component functions rather than formatted from the date, because Get ( CurrentDate ) renders per the system locale — a backup set that changes its own filename shape when the machine's region setting moves is a genuinely nasty thing to debug.

🔴 Get ( LastError ) after Save a Copy as is not optional. Disk full, a read-only volume, a locked folder, an insufficient privilege set: with capture on, every one of those returns cleanly and writes nothing. A backup routine that silently does not back up is strictly worse than not having one, because you stop thinking about it.

The prompt defaults OFF. A dialog on every run gets clicked through inside a week and then it is furniture. ⭐ The log row is the confirmation — UTILITY_LOGS records that the backup ran, where it went, and how long it took, and that is a record you can actually check later. Pass prompt: 1 from a manual Back up now if a human wants the choice.

The hosted gate exists for the version of this file that lives on a server. Save a Copy as is not permitted on a hosted file, and skipping deliberately is better than erroring — the server's own backup schedule is doing this job properly by then.

docs.title: ⚠️ Two things this script does not solve
docs.text:
1 · The file lives in a synced folder. Backups written beside it get pushed to iCloud or Dropbox on every run — a multi-MB upload each time, forever. Exclude zBACKUPS/ in the sync client, or point the destination outside the synced tree. This is a setup step, not a code change, and it is the kind that gets skipped and then blamed on the script.

2 · Nothing prunes. A daily copy of a file that only grows means the folder only grows. ⬜ Named as a gap and deliberately not built Not recorded — nobody asked for it, and a delete-files routine written speculatively is a delete-files routine nobody reviewed. The obvious shape when it is wanted: keep the last N, plus the first of each month.

docs.title: Unverified
docs.text:
• Get ( HostName ) as the hosted test. To be confirmed Believed empty for a local file and set for a hosted one. Confirm before relying on the gate rather than on the error.
  • PatternCount ( Get ( ApplicationVersion ) ; "Go" ) is the documented idiom for detecting FileMaker Go. To be confirmed Get ( SystemPlatform ) would be tidier, but its numeric codes are not written here from memory — look them up and swap if you want the cleaner test.
  • Whether Create folders: On creates zBACKUPS/ on first run in every supported version, or only where the parent already exists. Verify on site Test the very first run into an empty directory, which is the one case nobody ever tests twice.

docs.text: MAW Prose · Fall 2026

docs.title: FIND · All Or None
docs.text:
Sets the current layout's found set to everything, or to nothing. The one entity-agnostic FIND.

Grain

One run per found-set reset.

Retired name: Show ALL or NONE{ .dr-mark-link .dr-mark--cls-alias .dr-mark--box .dr-gloss data-gloss="A RETIRED NAME. Point it at the live one so paperwork quoting the old name still lands: fkCal. For an old VALUE rather than an old name, use was." data-role-print="A RETIRED NAME. Point it at the live one so paperwork quoting the old name still lands: fkCal. For an old VALUE rather than an old name, use was." }.

docs.title: Why it is a FIND · and not a SHOW ·
docs.text:
It returns a found set and touches nothing else, which is the FIND · contract. SHOW · sets state and then sends a person somewhere; nobody arrives anywhere here.

🔴 It is the one FIND that is not bound to an entity, and that is a hazard, not a feature. It operates on whatever table the current layout happens to sit on, so its behaviour is decided by the caller's context rather than by its parameter. Always call a GOTO · immediately before it. A caller that assumes it knows where it is standing is the bug this script will eventually cause.

docs.title: The script
docs.text:
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# FIND · All Or None
# Purpose: found set = every record, or no records
# Params (JSON): mode = "all" | "none"   MANDATORY
# Returns (JSON): ok, mode, count
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════

Set Error Capture [ On ]
Allow User Abort [ Off ]

Set Variable [ $p    ; Get ( ScriptParameter ) ]
Set Variable [ $mode ; ParamGetText ( $p ; "mode" ; "" ) ]

If [ IsEmpty ( $mode ) ]
    Exit Script [ ErrJSON ( 0 ; "FIND · All Or None" ; "mode is required" ) ]
End If

If [ $mode = "all" ]
    Show All Records

Else If [ $mode = "none" ]
    Show All Records
    Show Omitted Only

Else
    Exit Script [ ErrJSON ( 0 ; "FIND · All Or None" ;
        "unknown mode: " & $mode ) ]
End If

Exit Script [ Param ( List (
    PBool ( "ok"    ; 1 ) ;
    PText ( "mode"  ; $mode ) ;
    PNum  ( "count" ; Get ( FoundCount ) ) ) ) ]

Calls ErrJSON.

🔴 Both failure calls pass 0 as the error code, and that is correct rather than a placeholder. 0 is FileMaker's code for no error — because FileMaker did not fail, this script refused. A missing or unknown mode is a rejection by the script, and there is no Claris code for the caller wrote the wrong thing. The consequence for every caller: read ok first, never error. Full argument on ErrJSON's own page.

docs.title: 🔴 1 · Every path now exits with a result
docs.text:
The original's two success branches fall out of the If block and off the end of the script with no Exit Script. That does not return nothing — FileMaker persists the previous subscript's result, so a caller checking Get ( ScriptResult ) after a successful "all" reads whatever the last script that bothered to set one returned (Claris Community).

⭐ This is the same mechanism that nearly locked the file open through FILE · Close on the same day. One defect, two scripts, and in one of them it was fatal. The rule that closes it everywhere: a script has exactly one exit shape, and it is on the last line.

docs.title: 🔴 2 · The "abort" default is removed everywhere
docs.text:
The original reads ParamGetText ( $param ; "mode" ; "abort" ) and then branches on $mode = "abort". A caller who forgot the parameter and a caller who deliberately passed "abort" land in the same branch and cannot be told apart. A default exists to describe absence; the moment it is also a legal input, absence stops being detectable.

Empty is the missing marker. Missing is an error. Same rule applies to the other three scripts in this pass — all four used "abort" this way.

docs.title: 3 · The three spellings of NONE collapse to one
docs.text:
$mode = "NONE" or $mode = "none" or … — FileMaker's = on text is case-insensitive. All three tests are the same test. Exact ( ) is the case-sensitive one, and it is not wanted here.

⚠️ The redundancy is worth naming rather than just deleting: it is a written record of an assumption nobody checked, and it appears in three of the four scripts. Tidying it away without saying so loses the signal.

docs.title: 4 · The commented-out dialog is deleted, not commented
docs.text: // Show Custom Dialog [ "None" ] sits in the live script. Legacy shipped with a live debug dialog in a running file; this is that, one step earlier. A commented step is uncommented by the next person in a hurry. Delete it — git has it now.

docs.title: 5 · Failure is a payload, not a dialog
docs.text: ErrJSON replaces the call to exit w/ errors. That script could never work — a subscript cannot exit its caller — so the caller checks ok and exits itself.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
Show All Records → Show Omitted Only is the correct "find nothing" idiom and it was right in the original. Showing everything empties the omitted set; showing the omitted set then leaves you on zero records. It beats a find that cannot match, because it cannot accidentally match.

🔴 Both steps implicitly commit (house rule 7). This script can never be called from inside a transaction. Worth a comment in the script body itself, since the caller is where the damage happens.

⚠️ Show All Records on a large table fetches the whole found set. Harmless on VALUES, not harmless on EVENTS once real seasons are loaded. If a caller only needs a count, it wants a relationship or an ExecuteSQL, not this.

docs.text:

  • Who calls this today. Not recorded trigger_App_Open did, and it is retired.

docs.title: GOTO · (the family)
docs.text: MAW Prose · Fall 2026

docs.title: GOTO · (the family)
docs.text:
One script per destination, one step each. Documented as a family because four stub pages would say the same thing four times.

Grain

One script per destination. The whole body is Go to Layout. Nothing else, ever.

They are documented together on purpose. A page per one-line script is four copies of the same paragraph that then rot at different rates; the family has one contract, so it gets one page. Deviations get their own page — and a GOTO · that needs its own page has stopped being a GOTO ·.

docs.title: The shape
docs.text:
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# GOTO · <Destination>
# Purpose: land on util_<TABLE>
# Params (JSON): none
# Returns: nothing
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════

Go to Layout [ "util_<TABLE>" (<TABLE>) ]

No error capture, no parameter, no result. A one-step script that grows a second step is a SHOW ·, not a GOTO · — see the split rule in the template.

docs.title: 🔴 There are two scripts named goto_view_UTILITY_LOGS
docs.text:
Both sit in the same folder. FileMaker does not require script names to be unique — it identifies scripts internally, so Perform Script [ Specified: From list ] binds to a specific body and both callers appear to work.

The damage is threefold:

  1. You cannot tell which one you are editing. Fix a bug in one twin and the caller bound to the other keeps the bug.
  2. Perform Script by name is a coin flip, and so is anything that resolves a script from a stored string.
  3. 🔴 Deleting the wrong twin silently breaks every caller bound to it. They become Perform Script [ <unknown> ], which throws error 4 at runtime and is swallowed whole by the Set Error Capture [ On ] that every script in this file opens with.

⚠️ That third one is not hypothetical here. App_Startup already carries a live <unknown> on line 12. The file has an example of the failure before it has an example of the fix.

Order of operations, and it matters: open both, find which is referenced (a DDR script-reference list is the only reliable way), repoint the callers to the keeper, then delete. Never delete first and hunt after.

docs.title: 🔴 view_ is the wrong destination for a script
docs.text:
House rule 8: a script lands on util_<TABLE>, never a user-facing layout.

The live scripts target view_UTILITY_LOGS and view_VALUES. If those layouts are in the layout menu — and the view_ prefix says they are meant to be looked at — then every internal jump destroys whatever the user was doing: their found set, their record, their scroll position, their sort. It also welds the script to a layout that exists to be redesigned, so a cosmetic change breaks a utility and nothing says so.

⚠️ This is the second sighting of the unpicked table-occurrence naming fork (view_PRODUCTIONS vs bare), already flagged in the relationships pass. The first sighting was a schema opinion; this one is a script that goes to the wrong place. Pick the convention before the relationship graph binds it — it is nearly free now and it is thirty edits later.

docs.title: Why no error check
docs.text:
Go to Layout on a hardcoded, existing layout fails only if the layout was deleted or the privilege set forbids it. Adding a check would put a second step in a script whose entire value is that it has one — the reason the family exists is that every destination in the file is greppable from the script list, and that only holds while the bodies are trivial.

The trade, stated plainly: a deleted layout is caught by a DDR pass, not at runtime. That is acceptable while layouts are being built and reviewed in the same sitting. Revisit it when the file has users who are not Michael.

  • Whether view_UTILITY_LOGS and view_VALUES are actually in the layout menu. Verify on site If they are not, rule 8 is already satisfied and only the prefix is misleading. Cheap to check, and it changes the fix from a rebuild to a rename.

docs.title: UTIL · Run End
docs.text: MAW Prose · Fall 2026

docs.title: UTIL · Run End
docs.text:
Closes the log row through a relationship. No find, ever. A missing status is never success.

Grain

One call per run. Writes the outcome onto the row UTIL · Run Start opened.

The second half of house rule 9. It stamps the end time, the status and the error, and puts itself back where it came from.

🔴 It reaches the log row through a relationship, not a find. Rule 3 forbids inline Enter Find Mode, and this is exactly the case that tempts people to break it — the row is known by key, so finding it would be searching for something you already have the address of. Setting a global and editing through the relationship is fewer steps, cannot disturb a found set, and is the rule 7 transaction pattern applied to a one-record edit.

⚠️ That makes a relationship a hard dependency. g_logPK = UTILITY_LOGS::PrimaryKey, table occurrence named UTILITY_LOGS|byLogPK Not recorded. It does not exist. This script does nothing until it does, and "does nothing" here means every log row stays running forever — the exact end state that retired new_UTILITY_LOG, reached from the other direction.

docs.title: The script
docs.text:
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# UTIL · Run End
# Purpose: close the UTILITY_LOGS row this run opened
# Params (JSON): logPK (required), status, comment, errorCode
# Returns (JSON): ok, error
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Never call inside a transaction. It commits.
# Requires TO UTILITY_LOGS|byLogPK off GLOBAL_USE.
# A MISSING status is logged as unreported, never as ok.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════

Set Error Capture [ On ]

Set Variable [ $p     ; Get ( ScriptParameter ) ]
Set Variable [ $logPK ; ParamGetText ( $p ; "logPK" ; "" ) ]

If [ IsEmpty ( $logPK ) ]
    Exit Script [ Param (
        List (
            PBool ( "ok" ; 0 ) ;
            PText ( "error" ; "missing logPK" )
        )
    ) ]
End If

#  The caller did not say how it went. Say THAT, not "fine".
Set Variable [ $status ; ParamGetText ( $p ; "status" ; "unreported" ) ]

Go to Layout [ util_GLOBAL_USE ]
Set Field [ GLOBAL_USE::g_logPK ; $logPK ]

If [ IsEmpty ( UTILITY_LOGS|byLogPK::PrimaryKey ) ]
    Go to Layout [ original layout ]
    Exit Script [ Param (
        List (
            PBool ( "ok" ; 0 ) ;
            PText ( "error" ; "log row not found" ) ;
            PText ( "logPK" ; $logPK )
        )
    ) ]
End If

Set Field [ UTILITY_LOGS|byLogPK::ts_End    ; Get ( CurrentTimestamp ) ]
Set Field [ UTILITY_LOGS|byLogPK::vl_Status ; $status ]
Set Field [ UTILITY_LOGS|byLogPK::Comment   ; ParamGetText   ( $p ; "comment"   ; "" ) ]
Set Field [ UTILITY_LOGS|byLogPK::ErrorCode ; ParamGetNumber ( $p ; "errorCode" ; 0 ) ]

Commit Records/Requests [ No dialog ]
Set Variable [ $err ; Get ( LastError ) ]
If [ $err ≠ 0 ]
    Revert Record/Request [ No dialog ]
End If

Go to Layout [ original layout ]

Exit Script [ Param (
    List (
        PBool ( "ok" ; $err = 0 ) ;
        PNum  ( "error" ; $err )
    )
) ]

Lands on util_GLOBAL_USE To be confirmed. Sets g_logPK, edits through UTILITY_LOGS|byLogPK Not recorded. Writes ts_End, vl_Status, Comment, ErrorCode.

docs.title: 🔴 vl_Status defaults to unreported. Changed 2026-08-10, and this is the important part of the page.
docs.text:
It used to default to ok. That meant a script which failed and then called Run End without passing a status logged a success — and Run End cannot know better, because it cannot see what happened upstream.

⭐ A default is safe only when the case it assumes is the one that CANNOT go unnoticed if it is wrong. That is the sharpened rule, and it is what separates this from the other two defaults in the logging spine. A mislabelled kind on a session row is one obviously-wrong row a day, visible on sight. A mislabelled outcome on a failure is invisible by construction — you only read the log because something went wrong, and the log is telling you nothing did.

unreported is the magenta pattern one runtime over: a value nothing legitimately produces, so seeing it is proof of a break rather than a guess that might be right. Group by vl_Status and every caller that forgot shows up in its own bucket.

⚠️ It is a real value list entry, not a blank Not recorded. unreported has to be added to the vl_Status value list or it fails validation on write, which turns a soft signal into a hard error at the worst moment.

The rule this leaves for callers is unchanged and still the easiest thing to forget: every failure path passes its own status. What changed is that forgetting now produces a visible wrong answer instead of an invisible right-looking one.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
A missing logPK exits quietly rather than loudly. The caller has already finished its work by the time Run End is reached, so failing hard here would turn a bookkeeping problem into a user-visible one. The ok: 0 is there for a caller that wants to care.

"Log row not found" is a different failure from "could not write" and is reported as such. The first means the key is wrong or the row was deleted; the second means the write was refused. Collapsing them would make the one debuggable case indistinguishable from the one that is not.

$status is resolved BEFORE the navigation, so the one line that carries the outcome is read while the parameter is still the only thing in scope. Cosmetic, and it keeps the substantive decision out of the middle of a block that is all plumbing.
