docs.title: UTIL · Run Start
docs.text: MAW Prose · Fall 2026

docs.title: UTIL · Run Start
docs.text:
Opens the log row and hands back the key everything else reports against.

Grain

One call per run. Writes one UTILITY_LOGS row and returns its key.

House rule 9 says every script is wrapped by Run Start and UTIL · Run End. This is the first half. It captures where the caller was standing, creates the log row, commits it, and puts itself back — the caller never notices it moved.

🔴 It navigates and it commits, so it can never be called from inside a transaction. Rule 7 forbids implicit commits mid-transaction, and Go to Layout plus New Record are two of them. Call it at the top of a script, before the transaction opens. That ordering is not a style preference: a Run Start in the middle of a transaction silently commits half of it.

docs.title: The script
docs.text:
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# UTIL · Run Start
# Purpose: open a UTILITY_LOGS row for this run
# Params (JSON): sessionToken, kind, scriptName, params
# Returns (JSON): ok, logPK, sessionToken, entryLayout
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Never call inside a transaction. It commits.
# kind defaults to "script" ON PURPOSE. See the page.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════

Set Error Capture [ On ]

Set Variable [ $p ; Get ( ScriptParameter ) ]

#  -- entry context, captured BEFORE we move ---------
Set Variable [ $entryLayout ; Get ( LayoutName ) ]
Set Variable [ $entryFound  ; Get ( FoundCount ) ]
Set Variable [ $token       ; ParamGetText ( $p ; "sessionToken" ; $$SESSION.token ) ]

Go to Layout [ util_UTILITY_LOGS ]
New Record/Request
If [ Get ( LastError ) ≠ 0 ]
    Set Variable [ $err ; Get ( LastError ) ]
    Go to Layout [ original layout ]
    Exit Script [ Param ( List ( PBool ( "ok" ; 0 ) ; PNum ( "error" ; $err ) ) ) ]
End If

Set Field [ UTILITY_LOGS::SessionToken ; $token ]
Set Field [ UTILITY_LOGS::vl_Kind      ; ParamGetText ( $p ; "kind" ; "script" ) ]
Set Field [ UTILITY_LOGS::ScriptName   ; ParamGetText ( $p ; "scriptName" ; "" ) ]
Set Field [ UTILITY_LOGS::vl_Status    ; "running" ]
Set Field [ UTILITY_LOGS::ts_Start     ; Get ( CurrentTimestamp ) ]
Set Field [ UTILITY_LOGS::json_Params  ; ParamGetText ( $p ; "params" ; "" ) ]
Set Field [ UTILITY_LOGS::AccountName  ; Get ( AccountName ) ]
Set Field [ UTILITY_LOGS::UserName     ; Get ( UserName ) ]
Set Field [ UTILITY_LOGS::HostName     ; Get ( HostName ) ]
Set Field [ UTILITY_LOGS::AppVersion   ; Get ( ApplicationVersion ) ]
Set Field [ UTILITY_LOGS::json_Context ; Param (
    List (
        PText ( "entryLayout" ; $entryLayout ) ;
        PNum  ( "entryFound"  ; $entryFound )
    )
) ]

Set Variable [ $pk ; UTILITY_LOGS::PrimaryKey ]

Commit Records/Requests [ No dialog ]
If [ Get ( LastError ) ≠ 0 ]
    Set Variable [ $err ; Get ( LastError ) ]
    Revert Record/Request [ No dialog ]
    Go to Layout [ original layout ]
    Exit Script [ Param ( List ( PBool ( "ok" ; 0 ) ; PNum ( "error" ; $err ) ) ) ]
End If

Go to Layout [ original layout ]

Exit Script [ Param (
    List (
        PBool ( "ok" ; 1 ) ;
        PText ( "logPK" ; $pk ) ;
        PText ( "sessionToken" ; $token ) ;
        PText ( "entryLayout" ; $entryLayout )
    )
) ]

Lands on util_UTILITY_LOGS To be confirmed. Reads $$SESSION.token. Writes SessionToken, vl_Kind, ScriptName, vl_Status, ts_Start, json_Params, json_Context.

docs.title: ⭐ The vl_Kind default STAYS, and writing down why is the point of this section
docs.text:
UTIL · Run End lost its ok default on 2026-08-10 because a forgotten status logged a success. The obvious next move is to strip this default too, and it is wrong. Left unwritten, someone tidies it out in a month on the strength of the sibling's commit message.

A default is safe only when the case it assumes is the one that CANNOT go unnoticed if it is wrong. Apply it to the two:

assumes if wrong vl_Kind → script the caller is a script one obviously-wrong row per day. The session row is the first of its day, FILE · Open is its only producer, and it is mislabelled in a way you see at a glance vl_Status → ok the run succeeded invisible by construction. You only open the log because something broke, and it says nothing did

🔴 And the default is what makes the template's bare Perform Script [ UTIL · Run Start ] legal. Every templated script is a script; requiring the parameter would put one line of ceremony into every script in the file to describe the only thing they all have in common. The exception passes explicitly, and there is exactly one exception.

⚠️ The condition that ends this argument, so it is falsifiable rather than a preference: the moment a THIRD kind exists — an import run, a scheduled run, a server-side run — the caller population stops being 99% one thing, and the default becomes a lie told quietly. Strip it then.

⚠️ Not the same as new_UTILITY_LOG's version, which looked identical and was not: there the parameter was read from the wrong variable, so the default fired on every row rather than on the ones that omitted it. A default that fires when nobody omitted anything is not a default, it is a constant.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
Go to Layout [ original layout ] is why the caller never has to restore anything. FileMaker remembers the entry layout for the duration of one script, so the utility cleans up after itself rather than making every caller do it. Every exit path uses it, including the two failure paths — a utility that leaves you standing on a util layout after an error has turned a logging failure into a navigation bug.

The caller's found set survives because util_UTILITY_LOGS sits on its own table occurrence. That is the real argument for house rule 8, and it is stronger than the one the rule states: borrowing a user-facing layout would not just risk a redesign breaking the script, it would move the user's record pointer inside their own found set.

⚠️ Returning fires OnLayoutEnter on the entry layout. If that trigger ever does real work, a run-logged script fires it twice. Nothing has such a trigger today Verify on site; write one and this is where it bites.

⚠️ $entryLayout is returned and nothing consumes it. Run End restores itself the same way, so the value is diagnostic only, and it is also written into json_Context where it is genuinely useful. Kept deliberately: if a caller ever needs to know where it stood before a chain of utilities ran, this is the only record of it.

🚫 Do not pass values in params. The field stores what it is handed, verbatim, and a log is the last surface anyone sanitises. Keys, ids and modes — never a name, never an amount.

docs.title: UTIL · Value Index Move (+ FIND · Values)
docs.text: MAW Prose · Fall 2026

docs.title: UTIL · Value Index Move
docs.text:
Steps to first, last, next or previous within one value list's sort order. Rewrite of status_index_move, split in two.

Grain

One step per call, within one list.

Retired name: status_index_move{ .dr-mark-link .dr-mark--cls-alias .dr-mark--box .dr-gloss data-gloss="A RETIRED NAME. Point it at the live one so paperwork quoting the old name still lands: fkCal. For an old VALUE rather than an old name, use was." data-role-print="A RETIRED NAME. Point it at the live one so paperwork quoting the old name still lands: fkCal. For an old VALUE rather than an old name, use was." }. Both scripts call ErrJSON.

docs.title: Why it is two scripts
docs.text: The original does a find and the stepping logic. House rule 3 says the find moves out — but the real argument is not the rule, it is that the find is reusable and the stepping is not. Anything that needs the values of one list wants FIND · Values; only a stepper wants the arithmetic. Fused, the find is unreachable from anywhere else and gets typed inline a second time.

docs.title: FIND · Values
docs.text:
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# FIND · Values
# Purpose: the VALUES rows for one list, in sort order
# Params (JSON): fkList   MANDATORY
# Returns (JSON): ok, count
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════

Set Error Capture [ On ]
Allow User Abort [ Off ]

Set Variable [ $p      ; Get ( ScriptParameter ) ]
Set Variable [ $fkList ; ParamGetText ( $p ; "fkList" ; "" ) ]

If [ IsEmpty ( $fkList ) ]
    Exit Script [ ErrJSON ( 0 ; "FIND · Values" ; "fkList is required" ) ]
End If

Perform Script [ GOTO · Values ]

Enter Find Mode [ Pause: Off ]
Set Field [ util_VALUES::fkList ; $fkList ]
Perform Find [ ]

#  401 = no records match. That is an ANSWER, not a failure.
Set Variable [ $err ; Get ( LastError ) ]
If [ $err = 401 ]
    Exit Script [ Param ( List (
        PBool ( "ok"    ; 1 ) ;
        PNum  ( "count" ; 0 ) ) ) ]
Else If [ $err ≠ 0 ]
    Exit Script [ ErrJSON ( $err ; "FIND · Values / Perform Find" ; $fkList ) ]
End If

Sort Records [ By field: util_VALUES::Sort ; ascending ; With dialog: Off ]
If [ Get ( LastError ) ≠ 0 ]
    Exit Script [ ErrJSON ( Get ( LastError ) ; "FIND · Values / Sort" ; "" ) ]
End If

Exit Script [ Param ( List (
    PBool ( "ok"    ; 1 ) ;
    PNum  ( "count" ; Get ( FoundCount ) ) ) ) ]

Calls GOTO · Values and ErrJSON. Lands on util_VALUES To be confirmed, finds on fkList, sorts on VALUES::Sort Not recorded.

🚫 $fkList goes into the log through ErrJSON, and it is a KEY, which is why it is allowed. A UUID identifies a row; it is not a person's name or a value someone typed. Never widen this to the search TERM — that is the exact call that puts real data in a permanent log, and it is the tempting one while debugging.

docs.title: 🔴 Error 401 is not an error
docs.text:
The live script does If [ Get ( LastError ) ≠ 0 ] straight after Perform Find and treats the result as failure. 401 means "no records match", which is the correct and expected outcome of a find against an empty list. Treated as a hard error, an empty list becomes a crash instead of a zero.

⭐ This is the mirror of the swallowed-error problem, and it is the reason house rule 2 is easy to get wrong in both directions. Not checking means missing real failures; checking bluntly means inventing failures that are not there. Branch on the code, never on ≠ 0 alone, after any step whose "nothing found" case is legitimate. Finds are the main one; Go to Record [Next] at the end of a found set (error 101) is the other one this file will hit.

docs.title: 🔴 Sort Records [ Restore ] is replaced by a sort on a real field
docs.text:
The live script uses Restore, which stores the sort specification inside the script. Change the intended order and the script keeps silently sorting by the old spec — no error, no symptom, just a "next" that goes to the wrong place.

⭐ Same shape as everything else settled this week: a value that looks authored and is actually a stale copy. The fix is the same one used on themes and on standard events — make the order DATA. A Sort field is visible, editable and diffable. A stored sort spec is none of those.

⚠️ VALUES was renamed to VALUE_ITEMS in the open fix queue (SQL reserved word). If that rename lands, this script and its GOTO · change with it — noted here so the pair is not discovered separately. The old name will need an fkCal. For an old VALUE rather than an old name, use was.">VALUES row.

docs.title: UTIL · Value Index Move
docs.text:
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# UTIL · Value Index Move
# Purpose: step within one list's sort order
# Params (JSON): fkList    MANDATORY
#                mode      MANDATORY  first|last|next|previous
#                curIndex  required when mode is next|previous
# Returns (JSON): ok, index, count, atEnd
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════

Set Error Capture [ On ]
Allow User Abort [ Off ]

Set Variable [ $p      ; Get ( ScriptParameter ) ]
Set Variable [ $fkList ; ParamGetText ( $p ; "fkList" ; "" ) ]
Set Variable [ $mode   ; ParamGetText ( $p ; "mode"   ; "" ) ]

If [ IsEmpty ( $fkList ) or IsEmpty ( $mode ) ]
    Exit Script [ ErrJSON ( 0 ; "UTIL · Value Index Move" ;
        "fkList and mode are both required" ) ]
End If

If [ $mode = "next" or $mode = "previous" ]
    Set Variable [ $cur ; ParamGetNumber ( $p ; "curIndex" ; "" ) ]
    If [ IsEmpty ( $cur ) ]
        Exit Script [ ErrJSON ( 0 ; "UTIL · Value Index Move" ;
            "curIndex is required for mode " & $mode ) ]
    End If
End If

Perform Script [ FIND · Values ; Param ( PText ( "fkList" ; $fkList ) ) ]
Set Variable [ $r ; Get ( ScriptResult ) ]
If [ not ParamGetBoolean ( $r ; "ok" ; 0 ) ]
    Exit Script [ $r ]
End If

Set Variable [ $count ; ParamGetNumber ( $r ; "count" ; 0 ) ]
If [ $count = 0 ]
    Exit Script [ Param ( List (
        PBool ( "ok"    ; 1 ) ;
        PNum  ( "count" ; 0 ) ;
        PBool ( "atEnd" ; 1 ) ) ) ]
End If

#  -- resolve the target index, clamped ---------------
Set Variable [ $i ; Case (
    $mode = "first"    ; 1 ;
    $mode = "last"     ; $count ;
    $mode = "next"     ; Min ( $cur + 1 ; $count ) ;
    $mode = "previous" ; Max ( $cur - 1 ; 1 ) ;
    0 ) ]

If [ $i = 0 ]
    Exit Script [ ErrJSON ( 0 ; "UTIL · Value Index Move" ;
        "unknown mode: " & $mode ) ]
End If

Go to Record/Request [ $i ]
If [ Get ( LastError ) ≠ 0 ]
    Exit Script [ ErrJSON ( Get ( LastError ) ; "Go to Record" ; $i ) ]
End If

Exit Script [ Param ( List (
    PBool ( "ok"    ; 1 ) ;
    PNum  ( "index" ; $i ) ;
    PNum  ( "count" ; $count ) ;
    PBool ( "atEnd" ; $i = 1 or $i = $count ) ) ) ]

⭐ Exit Script [ $r ] passes the inner failure up UNMODIFIED, and that is deliberate. Re-wrapping it in a fresh ErrJSON here would overwrite where with this script's name and lose the fact that the find is what failed. A caller wants the site of the failure, not the site of the last handler that touched it.

docs.title: 🔴 The "last" default on a missing mode is removed
docs.text:
The live script reads ParamGetText ( $p ; "mode" ; "last" ). A caller that forgot to pass a mode silently jumps to the end of the list — a real action, taken confidently, on no instruction. Mode is mandatory now and absence is an error.

⭐ Same family as new_UTILITY_LOG defaulting its action type to "script": a default that is also a plausible real value cannot be distinguished from a working system. Both scripts in this pass had one.

docs.title: 🔴 The "abort" sentinel is gone
docs.text: ParamGetText ( $p ; "vl" ; "abort" ) then If [ $vl = "abort" ] cannot tell a missing parameter from a caller who deliberately sent "abort". Empty is the missing marker. Written up in full on FIND · All Or None.

docs.title: The empty If [ ] at line 35 is resolved
docs.text: The live script ends on an If with no condition and no body — the unfinished stepping logic. That is what the Case block above is for. ⚠️ An empty If is not inert: it is a decision someone was in the middle of making, and it is the single most useful thing in the original script because it marks exactly where the thinking stopped.

docs.title: Clamping instead of erroring at the ends
docs.text: Min / Max hold the index inside the found set, and atEnd tells the caller it did. A stepper that errors at the boundary makes every caller write the same guard; one that clamps and reports makes the boundary visible without making it fatal.

docs.title: Naming
docs.text: fkCal. For an old VALUE rather than an old name, use was.">status_index_move names neither what it does (steps within a list) nor what it operates on (VALUES), and the word status is a leftover from one caller. A script named after one of its callers gets copied the day a second caller appears.

  • Whether Go to Record/Request [ by calculation ] accepts a variable directly in the installed version. To be confirmed It does in every version this file will run on, but it has not been tested here.
  • Who actually calls this. Not recorded It is referenced in a stray comment inside new_UTILITY_LOG and nowhere else that has been read. A utility with no live caller is a utility whose contract nobody has pressure-tested.

docs.title: Retired Scripts
docs.text: MAW Prose · Fall 2026

docs.title: Retired Scripts
docs.text:
Scripts that were written, then ruled dead. Kept verbatim, never culled.

Grain

One page per script that was built in the file and then ruled dead. The body is pasted as it was, not as it should have been.

docs.title: Why this folder exists
docs.text: A deleted script leaves no trace of the thinking that produced it, and the same idea comes back three weeks later wearing a different name. The reasoning is the asset; the steps are disposable. Same never-cull rule the Decision Logs run on.

docs.title: How to read a page here
docs.text:
Every page carries three things and nothing else:

  1. VERBATIM — the script as it existed. Do not fix it. Do not reformat it. It is evidence, not code.
  2. WHY IT DIED — one paragraph. The defect, not a summary of the steps.
  3. WHAT REPLACES IT — a link, or an explicit "nothing."

⚠️ Transcription honesty. The 2026-08-09 set was read from screenshots of the FileMaker script workspace, so lines the screenshot clipped are marked Not recorded. A clipped line is never reconstructed from a guess — a plausible-looking body in an archive is worse than an obvious gap, because the gap gets checked and the guess gets quoted.

🚫 Marker spans stop at the code fence. The verbatim blocks carry no markup of any kind, deliberately: a marker inside evidence is an edit to the evidence. Everything on these pages that is tagged sits in the prose around the block.

docs.title: 🔴 Retiring a script does NOT delete it from the file
docs.text:
Archiving here and deleting in FileMaker are two separate actions, and the second one is Michael's.

Deleting a script breaks every Perform Script that referenced it, and FileMaker does not warn you — the caller silently becomes Perform Script [ <unknown> ]. That exact symptom is already live in this file on line 12 of App_Startup, which is how we know what a dead reference looks like here rather than in theory.

So the order is: archive → find the callers → repoint them → then delete. Never the other way round.

docs.title: The 2026-08-09 set
docs.text:
Four scripts from the file's first script-writing pass. All four were written before the template existed, and each one is a genuinely useful mistake.

Script Died because Replaced by trigger_App_Open Third claimant on the open handler, and it writes the session row to the wrong table FILE · Open App_Startup A fragment. Tests a variable it never sets, and calls a script that no longer exists FILE · Open new_UTILITY_LOG Second claimant on run logging, and three of its own variables never get a value UTIL · Run Start exit w/ errors 🔴 Cannot do what its name says. A subscript cannot exit its caller a custom function, not a script

⭐ The pattern across all four is one thing: a script that reads as finished because it has a header, a parameter and a shape. Three of them silently do nothing. None of them would look wrong on a layout, and none of them would fail loudly. That is the same comments-are-the-spec, fields-are-the-build defect already documented against the schema, arriving one layer up in the scripts.

It is the file's only worked example of what a deleted script reference looks like, and it will happen again the first time someone tidies the GOTO folder.

docs.title: VERBATIM
docs.text:
Transcribed from the FileMaker script workspace, 2026-08-09 ~21:45 ET. Clipped lines are marked; nothing is reconstructed.

# ---

# EXPECTING: sessionToken
# ---
Set Error Capture [ On ]
Allow User Abort [ Off ]


Set Variable [ $p ; Value: Get(ScriptParameter) ]
Set Variable [ $session ; Value: ParamGetText ( $p ;…[clipped] ]

Perform Script [ Specified: From list ; <unknown> ; Parameter:   ]

If [ $mode = "ALL" ]
    Show All Records
Else If [ $mode = "NONE" or $mode = "none" or $mode…[clipped] ]

End If

Two lines are truncated in the source screenshot Not recorded.

docs.title: WHY IT DIED
docs.text: Three separate reasons, and the third is the one that decides it.

docs.title: 1 · 🔴 $mode is never set in this script
docs.text:
Lines 14–16 branch on $mode. Nothing in the script assigns it. A $ variable is script-local, so it is empty here no matter what the caller did, both branches evaluate false, and the If block does nothing at all — silently, with no error and no symptom.

⭐ The block is a paste of Show ALL or NONE with the one line that made it work left behind. That is worth more than the bug: a copied block carries its conditions but not its setup, and FileMaker will not tell you which half you took. The rewrite's answer is that no script branches on a variable it did not read from its own parameter, on its own first few lines, where the omission is visible.

docs.title: 2 · 🔴 Perform Script [ <unknown> ] on line 12
docs.text:
<unknown> is FileMaker's rendering of a reference to a script that has been deleted. It is not a placeholder someone left; it is a broken pointer, and it throws error 4 (unknown command) at runtime — which, with Set Error Capture [ On ] two lines above and no Get ( LastError ) check anywhere, is swallowed whole.

⚠️ This is the exact failure that makes the duplicate goto_view_UTILITY_LOGS pair dangerous. Delete the wrong twin and every caller that bound to it becomes this. See the GOTO family.

⬜ Which script it used to point at has never been established Not recorded — the reference is dead, so the name is gone with it.

docs.title: 3 · It is the third claimant on the file-open handler
docs.text:
00App_onFirstWindowOpen To be confirmed, trigger_App_Open and this script all want to be what runs on OnFirstWindowOpen. Only one thing can be set in File Options, so two of the three are dead code that reads as live — and there is nothing in the file that says which one won.

⭐ Same second-claimant shape that killed THEMES::bool_isDefault, EXPORT_SETS::bool_DefaultRecord and GLOBAL_EXPORT_VARIABLES::g_pkDefault_EXPORT_SET earlier the same day. Three N-designating-one defects in the schema, then immediately a fourth in the scripts. The mechanism does not care which layer it is in.

docs.title: WHAT REPLACES IT
docs.text:
FILE · Open — already specced, and it holds the pieces this script was reaching for: it mints $$SESSION.token, calls UTIL · Run Start, and keeps its setup work in one clearly marked block.

⚠️ Before deleting this script, check whether File Options points at it Verify on site. If it does, repoint to FILE · Open first. A file whose open handler is a deleted script opens with an error dialog every single time, and it is a fiddly thing to fix from the inside.

docs.title: VERBATIM
docs.text:
Transcribed from the FileMaker script workspace, 2026-08-09 ~21:45 ET. Clipped lines are marked; nothing is reconstructed.

# ---

# REQUIRED: VALUE LIST
# EXPECTING: "next, previous, first, or last, in VALUE LIST sort"
# ---
Set Error Capture [ On ]
Allow User Abort [ Off ]


Set Variable [ $p ; Value: Get(ScriptParameter) ]
Set Variable [ $comment ; Value: ParamGetText ( $p ; "comment" ; "" ) ]
If [ $comment ≠ "" ]
    Show Custom Dialog [ $comment ; "Exiting…" ]
End If







Exit Script [ Text Result: Param ( List ( Pbool ( "o…[clipped] ]

The final line is truncated in the source screenshot Not recorded — the boolean key and everything after it were never read.

docs.title: WHY IT DIED
docs.text:
🔴 Exit Script ends the script it is written in. It has no reach into the caller.

Call this from a script that has just hit a failed find and the sequence is: this script runs, shows its dialog, exits — and the caller resumes on its very next step, error unhandled, as if nothing happened. The name promises an abort. The mechanism cannot deliver one. There is no version of this script that works, because the thing it is trying to do is not a thing a subscript can do in FileMaker.

⭐ And the failure is invisible in exactly the situation it was written for. You only reach for it on an error path, error paths are the least-tested code in any file, and the symptom of it not working is the script keeps going — which looks identical to no error having occurred.

⚠️ The step that DOES stop everything is Halt Script, and it is wrong here for a different reason: it kills the entire call stack including the caller's cleanup, so UTIL · Run End never runs and the log row stays open forever. A logged crash is worth more than a clean abort.

docs.title: Two smaller defects, worth naming because they generalize
docs.text:
The header belongs to a different script. # REQUIRED: VALUE LIST and # EXPECTING: "next, previous, first, or last…" are status_index_move's header, pasted in and never edited. This is the comments-are-the-spec, fields-are-the-build pattern that the DDR pass has now found in field definitions, in table comments, and here in scripts. Three surfaces, one habit: the description is written in the same sitting as the thing and never reconciled with it.

Show Custom Dialog is not suppressed by Set Error Capture. A dialog inside an error handler stops an unattended run dead and waits for a human who is not there. Any error path that can fire during an import, an export or a scheduled run must be able to complete silently.

docs.title: WHAT REPLACES IT
docs.text:
Nothing, as a script. The payload builder is ErrJSON, a custom function, and the caller does its own exiting:

// ErrJSON ( code ; where ; comment )
Param (
    List (
        PBool ( "ok"      ; 0 ) ;
        PNum  ( "error"   ; code ) ;
        PText ( "where"   ; where ) ;
        PText ( "comment" ; comment )
    )
)

Then, in the script that actually failed:

If [ Get ( LastError ) ≠ 0 ]
    Perform Script [ UTIL · Run End ; logPK, status "error", comment ]
    Exit Script [ ErrJSON ( Get ( LastError ) ; "Perform Find" ; "" ) ]
End If

⭐ The rewrite is smaller than the script it replaces and it works, which is the tell that the original was a script-shaped answer to a function-shaped problem. House rule 6 already says domain strings belong in custom functions; this widens it: anything a script returns but does not DO is a custom function.

⚠️ It also gets the reporting right by accident. The dialog is gone, so an unattended run completes, and the failure lands in UTILITY_LOGS where it can be found later — instead of on a screen nobody was watching.

⚠️ The block above is a QUOTE of the definition, not a second copy of it. ErrJSON's own page is canonical; if the two ever disagree, that page wins and this one is wrong. It is reproduced here because the argument for retiring this script is unreadable without seeing what replaced it.

docs.title: Callers
docs.text:
Known to have called it: FIND · All Or None and status_index_move in their live forms. A full caller list has never been read Not recorded — it needs a DDR script-reference pass, and it is required before the script is deleted rather than merely retired.

Point it at the live one so paperwork quoting the old name still lands: fkCal. For an old VALUE rather than an old name, use was." data-role-print="A RETIRED NAME. Point it at the live one so paperwork quoting the old name still lands: fkCal. For an old VALUE rather than an old name, use was." }. Writes UTILITY_LOGS::fkSessionToken and UTILITY_LOGS::vl_ActionType.

docs.title: 1 · 🔴 Three variables are read and never written
docs.text:
This is the whole story, and none of it throws an error.

Read on line Written on line Result at runtime $token (33) never fkSessionToken is always empty $p (37) never — the parameter went into $param (8) ParamGetText gets nothing, returns the default "script" every time $fkReport (11) declared with no value the field the header calls MANDATORY is never written

🔴 vl_ActionType is the worst of the three, because it is confidently wrong rather than blank. An empty field reads as not filled in and someone eventually asks why. "script" on every single row reads as the answer, and it is the fallback firing on a typo — one character between $p and $param.

⭐ The generalizable rule: a default that is also a plausible real value cannot be distinguished from a working system. Same defect the theme resolve cascade already solved by falling back to magenta — a colour nothing legitimately uses, so hitting it is proof of a break rather than a guess that might be right. A default should be conspicuous or it should be an error. "script" is neither.

docs.title: 2 · 🔴 It never returns the key it created
docs.text:
No Exit Script on the success path. The log row is opened and the caller is never told which row it is, so nothing can ever close it. Every row this script writes is permanently running.

That is precisely the ambiguity J13 accepted as unavoidable for crashes — and this manufactures it for normal, successful runs, which destroys the one signal the open-with-no-close row was supposed to carry.

docs.title: 3 · Second claimant on run logging
docs.text: UTIL · Run Start was specced the same day for this exact job, and returns logPK because UTIL · Run End needs it. Two scripts, one responsibility.

docs.title: 4 · Someone else's comments, again
docs.text: Lines 15–16 — "perform script to: find next, previous, first, or last, in VALUE LIST sort" — belong to status_index_move and describe nothing this script does. Third instance in four scripts. ⚠️ The dangling Set Variable [ ] on line 17 is the shell of whatever that note was meant to become.

docs.title: 5 · No Get ( LastError ) after the two Set Field steps
docs.text: Only New Record is checked. A Set Field fails on a validation rule, a lock or a missing field, and with capture on it fails quietly.

docs.title: WHAT REPLACES IT
docs.text:
UTIL · Run Start — same job, returns logPK, and half of house rule 9.

⚠️ Run Start is not yet enterable either: its sibling UTIL · Run End is blocked on the UTILITY_LOGS|byLogPK table occurrence Not recorded, which does not exist. Log rows that cannot be closed is the same end state as this script, arrived at from the other direction — so build the relationship before entering either.

docs.title: 1 · 🔴 APP_SESSIONS is a second claimant on UTILITY_LOGS
docs.text:
This is the real reason, and it is a schema question wearing a script.

J13 ruled one table with two grains, separated by vl_Kind and bound by SessionToken: a file session and a script run both start, both end, both succeed or do not, and both want the same nine columns. The ruling was explicit that splitting them "would duplicate every field to gain a distinction one indexed value already makes, and would turn what happened during this session into a join instead of a sort."

APP_SESSIONS is that split, built anyway. Two tables now claim the session row, and UTILITY_LOGS::fkSessionToken — the field that binds every script run to its session — points at whichever one wins.

⬜ Michael's call, and it is not mine to make Not recorded. Either APP_SESSIONS dies and vl_Kind carries it, or J13 is reversed in writing and UTILITY_LOGS sheds its session grain. Both are defensible. Having both tables is not. Until it is settled, FILE · Open cannot be entered, because it does not know which table to write to.

docs.title: 2 · 🔴 The session token is minted after the row is written
docs.text:
Set Variable [ $$SESSION.token ] is the last step, three lines after the record is created. So the row exists without its token, and if anything between them errors, the session row is orphaned — present, timestamped, and unjoinable to any of the script runs that follow it.

Mint the token first, then write the row. In FILE · Open Get ( UUID ) is line one of the body for exactly this reason: it cannot fail, so nothing can happen between minting and using it.

docs.title: 3 · New Record/Request with no Get ( LastError ) check
docs.text: House rule 2. Set Error Capture [ On ] is on line 4, so a failed create is silent, and the two Set Field steps that follow then write into whatever record the user happened to be on. ⚠️ That is worse than a failure: it is a silent edit to real data.

docs.title: 4 · Show ALL or NONE{ .dr-mark-link .dr-mark--cls-alias .dr-mark--box .dr-gloss data-gloss="A RETIRED NAME. Point it at the live one so paperwork quoting the old name still lands: fkCal. For an old VALUE rather than an old name, use was." data-role-print="A RETIRED NAME. Point it at the live one so paperwork quoting the old name still lands: fkCal. For an old VALUE rather than an old name, use was." } on the way in does nothing useful
docs.text: Showing every session row before creating a new one has no effect on the create and costs a full found-set fetch at open, which grows forever. ⚠️ And Show All Records implicitly commits (house rule 7), so it can never sit inside a transaction later.

docs.title: 5 · Third claimant on the open handler
docs.text: With 00App_onFirstWindowOpen To be confirmed and App_Startup. See that page — the same defect is written up there.

docs.title: WHAT REPLACES IT
docs.text:
FILE · Open, once the APP_SESSIONS fork above is settled.

⭐ What this script got right, and the rewrite keeps: it calls a GOTO · rather than typing Go to Layout inline, and it uses a JSON parameter on a script that only needed one value. Both were house rules before the house rules were written down.

What to port, transform, and kill.

docs.title: ✅ PORT the bones
docs.text: Script Why CREATE PRODUCTION WORKDAYS The generator. Two loops: production days forward from first rehearsal, pre-pro backward. Then sort by DATE → stamp sequential SORT → re-sort by SORT. This is the WEEKS → WORKDAYS pattern. ⚠️ Kill the magic $daysNeeded + 10 on the pre-pro exit. showRelevantDates + showNecessaryRecords Find HideDateFromCalendar = 1 → Show Omitted Only → constrain to DATE > Calendar_START - 1. The found-set trick that makes hide-as-existence work. Proof the stamped-hide call was right. EXPORT Calendar Set Filename builder (YYMMDD, long/short title prompt) + four-output run (8.5x11 landscape, 8.5x11 portrait, 11x17 expanded, agenda). The whole script becomes PRINT_PRESETS rows. Workday Sort INPUT Sequential SORT stamp after a date sort. Keeps print order independent of date. PRINT_SETUP pair Parameter 1 = landscape, else portrait. Clean. Becomes OutputSize + orientation on the preset.

docs.title: 🔄 TRANSFORM
docs.text: Script Problem New home REMOVE ShortName Strips [BL] by looping and mutating Event Name in place Raw stays in Raw_Payload; cleaned name is a separate field. Never mutate. remove notes Strips <...> the same way Same CREATE_multipleDays A multi-day event is DUPLICATED into one record per day, flagged autoGenerated=1 🔴 Needs a decision — EVENTS grain is currently one row per event. Either keep a span as one row and render across days, or adopt duplicate-per-day explicitly. Events Agenda View SORT Hides a business rule in a sort: finds Event Name == "Rehearsal" then Show Omitted Only, so the agenda deliberately excludes plain rehearsals That is a preset FILTER, not a sort → PRINT_PRESETS 6x stored production INFO Each hardcodes title / short / first-rehearsal / last-needed / director / semester / course + all six range fields into the ONE SETUP record, then regenerates ⭐ These scripts ARE the PRODUCTIONS table, written as code. All six delete outright once records exist.

docs.title: 🪦 KILL
docs.text:
• import Records — Show All → Delete All Records → Import. REPLACE THE SET deletes again before calling it. Double delete, and the reason history is impossible → UPSERT on TaskID + fkProduction.
  • Delete ClickUp Rows — finds Event Name = "Task Name" and deletes it. That is the CSV header row landing as a record. Pure CSV artifact; an API pull has no headers.
  • AUTO_WorkdayID — assigns dates via NumberOfRecordsPerPortal / NumberAvailablePreProRecords math. Portal geometry driving data placement.
  • updatePreproCounter / updateUnscheduledCounter — counters existing only to feed that geometry.
  • checkHIGHlight / checkLOWlight → CALENDAR_EMPHASIS relationship. checkHideWorkday survives.
  • refreshFilePath — deletes and recreates the SETUP_EXPORT record to refresh a path. Get ( FilePath ) replaces it.
  • removeTextFormatting — strips styling off a field that should never have held styling.
  • ColorMONTHStyle / ColorSTATUSStyle / updateEventSTYLE / updateWORKDAYcolor / TextColorHex / color_Text — six scripts writing RGB into stored text. STYLES resolves colour at render.
  • FCCalendar addon (~25 scripts) — third-party widget. FCCalendar Import Sample Data calls https://fakermaker.geist.ws/api/generate from inside a production file.

docs.title: 🔴 Live bugs found
docs.text:
1. RGB ( $R ; $G ; $R ) in BOTH ColorSTATUSStyle and updateWORKDAYcolor. Blue takes red's value. Every status and month colour in that file is wrong and nobody noticed — the argument for one resolution path.
  2. Three flag scripts, no priority. checkHideWorkday / checkHIGHlight / checkLOWlight each set their own flag to 1 with no resolution between them. A day in two ranges gets two flags and the layout picks. The overlap bug was always there, it just never fired on single-range use.
  3. updateWORKDAYcolor ships a live Show Custom Dialog debug popup, uncommented.
  4. One Acts INFO has Course Numbers: "THTR TIME course" — copy-pasted from TIME.
  5. import Records references two <Missing Field> entries in its import mapping.

docs.title: ⬜ Device handoff — the open-log
docs.text:
One person, three devices, one file. The file is never open in two places — but nothing in the file says so. This closes that gap. Logged 2026-08-08; fleet-wide concern, implemented here first because this app is being built now.

The existing workflow is already a checkout protocol: download to device = checkout, share-sheet the file back out = check-in, sequential-only = the lease. It runs in Michael's head. This writes it down. Nothing here changes the discipline; it instruments it.

docs.title: Tier 0 — three fields + one trigger. No relationships, no dependencies. BUILD THIS FIRST.
docs.text:
On 00_APP (or wherever the single-record app-state row lives):

Field Type Written by LastOpenedAt Timestamp OnFirstWindowOpen LastOpenedDevice Text OnFirstWindowOpen LastOpenedPlatform Text OnFirstWindowOpen 
Set Field [ 00_APP::LastOpenedAt       ; Get ( CurrentTimeStamp ) ]
Set Field [ 00_APP::LastOpenedDevice   ; Get ( SystemNVLTargetName ) ]
Set Field [ 00_APP::LastOpenedPlatform ; Get ( Device ) ]

Surface it as merge text, top-right of the home layout: home-mbp · Aug 8 7:20 PM.

Why it earns its place before anything else: open any copy on any device and it tells you where that copy last lived. A copy on the work laptop last opened on the iPad two hours ago is visibly the stale one. That is the whole "what's open elsewhere" problem solved for three fields.

Rule Failure mode if broken Stamp on OPEN, not on close A crash or a force-quit never writes a close. Open always fires. Never trust the stamp as a LOCK It is a sign, not a gate. It reports; it does not prevent. Verify Get ( Device ) return values against current docs Return integers are quoted from memory constantly and are wrong about as often.

⚠️ Get ( SystemNVLTargetName ) is unverified on FileMaker Go — it may return something useless there. If so, fall back to a one-time manual device picker written to a global on first open per device.

docs.title: Tier 1 — transport
docs.text:
Mobile leg moves to Dropbox; laptop↔laptop stays on iCloud. Dropbox earns the mobile leg for exactly one reason: it has an HTTP API Insert from URL can call, which makes pull scriptable. iCloud has none.

🚫 Push is never scriptable. FileMaker Go cannot export to FMP12 at all, so moving a file back off an iPad is an iOS share-sheet operation FileMaker cannot see or trigger. Design the return trip out of existence rather than trying to automate it.

docs.title: Tier 2 — the launcher (gated on a device test)
docs.text:
A small permanent MAW_Launch.fmp12 per device: lists the apps, shows each build stamp, one Pull newest button each. Splits a tiny always-current control plane from the fat on-demand data plane.

Insert from URL [ target: container ; Dropbox download endpoint ]

# VALIDATE — never skip. Insert from URL succeeds at storing whatever came back.
# A 404 page and a wrong MIME type both land in the container looking fine.
Set Variable [ $size ; GetContainerAttribute ( container ; "fileSize" ) ]
Set Variable [ $md5  ; GetContainerAttribute ( container ; "MD5" ) ]
If [ $size < 100000 or $md5 ≠ expected ]  →  fail loudly, exit

Export Field Contents [ container ; Get ( DocumentsPath ) & filename ]
Open URL [ "fmp://~/" & filename ]

⚠️ Two unverified claims block Tier 2. Test on a real device before designing further:

  1. the launch token — fmp://~/ vs fmp://$/ on current FileMaker Go. No first-party dated source found for either.
  2. whether Export Field Contents can write where Go actually browses. A 2024 report has AirDropped .fmp12 files landing in an iOS Downloads folder Go cannot see at all.

If either fails, Tier 2 does not exist. Tiers 0 and 1 stand alone regardless.

docs.title: Tier 3 — the registry. PARKED.
docs.text:
APPS · APP_BUILDS · APP_CHECKOUTS · DEVICES · SYNC_EVENTS. Full shape and reasoning on the session task. Build only if Tier 0 proves insufficient in practice. Notes: APPS duplicates two existing inventories (repo VERSIONS.md, the URITP fmp Solutions list) so it folds in rather than starting fresh; and the registry can never live inside the app it tracks, or you must open the stale copy to learn it is stale.

Open-state should be a relationship, not a stored flag — constant calc cOutFlag = "out" matched against APP_CHECKOUTS::State on a second TO, then not IsEmpty ( ... ) unstored. Derived state cannot go stale. Same law as the [Projection Law].

docs.title: 🚫 What is NOT on the table
docs.text: Not doing Why Merge / conflict resolution .fmp12 is opaque binary. No diff, no merge, not ever. Two edited copies = pick one, retype the other. A pull-request UI It would be a merge surface that can never merge. Hosting / serving Ruled out of scope. Automated push from mobile Platform impossibility, see Tier 1.

docs.title: ⬜ Open — UI/DATA separation
docs.text:
Splitting a solution into a records-free UI file + a DATA file, joined by an external data source reference (the mechanism URITP GLOBAL Setup already uses fleet-wide). Makes version push idempotent: a UI file holds no records, so overwriting it can never lose work.

Editing... Lives in Separation helps? tables, fields, relationships DATA no layouts, scripts, value lists, TOs UI yes — overwrite is lossless entering / reviewing records DATA no

The tension, stated honestly: it pays off least during the current schema-build phase and most once the work becomes layouts and reports — but it is cheap only while there are no layouts to re-point, which is now. Cheapest now, most useful later. Michael's call; posed as Q10 on the FMP Apps — Shared Build & Behaviour Decision Log (ClickUp).

⚠️ Also unverified: two local separated files referencing each other via external data source on FileMaker Go. Separation normally pairs with hosting. Same device test as Tier 2.

docs.text: Naming conventions for this app. Names lock before any calc queries them by name.

docs.title: Naming
docs.text:
Convention Pattern Example Primary keys PrimaryKey, UUID, never serial ⚠️ Diverges from house pk_ prefix (open governance item) Foreign keys fk<Parent> fkProduction, fkCalendar, fkStandardEvent Dates date_ prefix date_FirstRehearsal, date_NeededLast Booleans bool_ prefix bool_AddPreProWeek, bool_IsScratch Calculations calc_ prefix calc_TotalOutstanding Overrides ovr_ prefix ovr_OutputSize — empty means INHERIT from the parent Integration keys cu prefix, camel, no underscore cuProductionToken, cuProductionID Globals g_ prefix; gLIST_ for value-list globals g_currentProduction, gLIST_PropertyNames Audit fields PrimaryKey, CreationTimestamp, CreatedBy, ModificationTimestamp, ModifiedBy Every table, including a singleton No leading underscores Active core tables only Legacy GLOBAL_, XXval_, old... gets stripped Value list vs table Metadata beyond display value → table Location type = value list until it earns SortOrder; event type (carries skin + report role) = STANDARD_EVENTS

⚠️ date_, bool_, ovr_ and cu were added 2026-08-08 from live practice. This page had documented only calc_, g_ and fk while the build was already using the others — the doc lost to the diff.

docs.title: Why names lock before SQL
docs.text: ExecuteSQL embeds table and field names as text. Rename a table and the calc returns empty, not error.

docs.title: Field-menu conventions (the .tsv side)
docs.text:
• The first column is a confirmation state ({.conf} / {.tbc}), not a sort ordinal. A field menu is a build tracker, not a static list.
  • Columns mirror FileMaker's own field dialog: Field_Name · Type · Options · Notes.
  • Sections are bare singular rows: NORMALIZED FIELDS · INTEGRATION KEYS · RELATIONSHIP · CHILDREN · AUDIT FIELDS, closed by - EOF -.
  • Audit fields are spelled out, not pointed at — you cannot check off a pointer while sitting in the field dialog.
  • TABLE.tsv is uppercase (it is the FMP table name); table.md is lowercase (it is a document).

docs.title: The pipe
docs.text:
• CSV first, API second. Same fields serve both — no migration.
  • The VIEW is the contract. A saved ClickUp view is a stable, human-editable integration surface: change what gets published without touching a script.
  • One session = one production (see [import_SESSIONS]).

docs.title: Views are per-LIST
docs.text:
• A view lives on one list and carries its own filter. So "Big Love events" is a saved view built once.
  • Cost: one saved view per production. Manual upkeep at 7+ shows, and a new show means a new view before the first import.

docs.title: ⬜ TO-DO — one view, production passed as a PARAMETER at pull time
docs.text:
Wanted. Replaces N per-production views with ONE view plus a runtime filter argument.

  • API only. A CSV export is a static file; there is no parameter to pass.
  • So the per-production views are the CSV-era stopgap, and this is what retires them.
  • Blocks nothing today: cuProductionID is already on [PRODUCTIONS] waiting for it.

docs.title: Join keys
docs.text:
Key Transport Note cuProductionToken CSV + API Exact label string. A rename in ClickUp breaks it SILENTLY cuProductionID API only Rename-proof. Empty until the pull exists
  • Operator declares the production at import. Non-resolving rows get flagged, never silently filed.

docs.title: ⬜ Open
docs.text:
• ⬜ Multi-label exposure. URITP Productions is multi-select, so one event task can carry two shows. Handled by per-production views + a compound upsert key — verify against a live CSV.
  • ⬜ Do CSV multi-value labels come back comma-separated inside one quoted cell, and do any show titles contain commas?
  • ⬜ Event classification: a CU-side canonical-type dropdown was declined, so a crosswalk (raw name → fkStandardEvent) with an unmatched queue carries it. Learns instead of guessing.
  • ⬜ ClickUp does not emit a LOCATION on an event task today. Ruled 2026-08-08: not going there yet, but [LOCATIONS] is built so it can.
  • ⬜ Crew calls — third document, or a view of the calendar? A call carries person, role, call time, report location.

docs.title: Projection Law
docs.text: MAW Prose · Fall 2026

docs.title: Projection law
docs.text:
LOCKED 2026-08-08 — there are NO manual edits to the projection layer, ever. The engine covers it.

"let's just not plan to do ManualEdits and have a formatting engine that is robust enough to get what I need done." — Michael, 2026-08-08

docs.title: The rule
docs.text:
[WEEKS] · [WORKDAYS] · [EVENTS_workday]To be confirmed are 100% derived. Delete-and-rebuild, always, on any trigger. No flags, no preservation pass, no reconciliation, no verify-before-commit step. Nothing is ever lost because nothing is ever authored there.

The ManualEdit flag is killed before it shipped — and killing it removes the whole machine it needed: a preservation pass on rebuild, a divergence report, an accept/discard decision per row. That machinery existed only to protect edits that now cannot happen.

⭐ Why this is the right call and not just the simpler one: a disposable table with edits in it is not disposable, it is a second source of truth wearing a temporary costume. Same species as the autoGenerated flag killed on the legacy duplicates, the convenience-copy dates, and the second-claimant highlight fields. Fourth instance in one session.

docs.title: What this OBLIGATES the engine to do
docs.text:
The pressure that creates spot-edits is real. Refusing the edits means the engine has to cover the cases, so they are named here rather than discovered under deadline:

Pressure Must be solved by "this one event needs different styling on this one page" a [STYLES] row or a [CALENDAR_EMPHASIS] row — a rule, not a keystroke "this week needs a page break here" PAGE_BREAK is generated; the RULE that sets it belongs on the preset "this day is too crowded to fit" overflow behaviour in the layout, not a hand-trimmed cell "the name is too long for the cell" UseShortTitle + a length-aware display calc "drop this event from this one printout" a [PRINT_PRESETS] FILTER (the legacy agenda already did exactly this to hide rehearsals) "a typo in an event name" fix it in ClickUp, reimport. ClickUp authors.

🔴 The last row is the load-bearing one. Every "just let me fix it on the page" is really a request to author data in the render layer, which is the architecture locked on 2026-08-07: ClickUp authors, FileMaker renders.

docs.title: Consequences, stated plainly
docs.text:
• ✅ Rebuild is dumb and safe: delete in scope, regenerate. No branching.
  • ✅ Reprinting an old [PRINT_SESSIONS] row is honest: it renders today's truth, and the paper was never authoritative.
  • ✅ No verify-before-commit pass to build or maintain.
  • ⚠️ A formatting need with no rule behind it becomes a BUILD task, not a workaround. That is the trade: slower on the one-off, and the app never accumulates untracked hand-fixes.
  • ⚠️ If a genuinely unrulable one-off ever appears, the answer is export the PDF and edit the PDF — outside the system, where it cannot pretend to be data.

docs.title: Build & Use Workflow
docs.text: MAW Prose · Fall 2026

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: Manual first, import skins on top.

docs.title: 🔴 Manual input comes FIRST, and it has to
docs.text:
First rehearsal cannot be derived from imported events. The dependency runs one way:

date_FirstRehearsal  →  calendar start  →  WEEKS  →  WORKDAYS  →  events land on days

Derive the date from events and you have a circle: events need workdays to land on, workdays need weeks, weeks need a start, the start needs the date. So it is typed, and it is typed before any import runs.

docs.title: Order of operations
docs.text:
# Step Where Typed or generated 1 Create the production. Type date_FirstRehearsal + date_Opening. Set cuProductionToken. [PRODUCTIONS] typed 2 Create the calendar. Type the page bounds, set bool_AddPreProWeek. [PRODUCTION_CALENDARS] typed 3 Generate the grid. [WEEKS] → [WORKDAYS] generated, never typed 4 Add callouts. Tech week, breaks, residencies. [CALENDAR_EMPHASIS] typed 5 Import. Events land on days that already exist. [import_SESSIONS] → [import_EVENTS] → [EVENTS] imported 6 Print. [PRINT_PRESETS] → [PRINT_SESSIONS] generated

Steps 1–4 are a working app with zero imports. That is deliberate: a calendar with a grid and no events is still printable, and it is how you find a wrong start date before 121 event records are sitting on it.

⚠️ The grid is rebuilt per print, not built once. WeekStartDay lives on the preset, so a Tue-start and a Sun-start render different week rows from the same calendar. See [Projection Law].

docs.title: Import SKINS, it never AUTHORS
docs.text:
The import layer may only:

  • create/update [EVENTS] (upsert on TaskID + fkProduction)
  • resolve fkStyle from the raw ClickUp status token
  • resolve fkStandardEvent via the crosswalk
  • rebuild [EVENTS_workday]To be confirmed as the last step

It may never write first rehearsal, opening, page bounds, or emphasis rows. Those are human decisions.

docs.title: The one thing it does check
docs.text:
⭐ If the earliest event of canonical type "First Rehearsal" does not match the typed date_FirstRehearsal, FLAG it. Never correct it.

Same guard shape as the production token: the import surfaces a disagreement instead of silently resolving one. This is what stops a date typed in June from quietly contradicting a schedule that moved in August — the failure mode being defended against is a printed page that is a week off with no symptom.

docs.title: Anchored emphasis needs events
docs.text:
event-mode [CALENDAR_EMPHASIS] rows resolve through events, so they render as nothing until the first import lands. MatchCount = 0 is the tell. That is correct behaviour, not a bug — and it is why range mode exists for anything that must print pre-import.

docs.title: CALENDAR_EMPHASIS
docs.text:
N typed callouts per calendar. Replaces the fixed highlight/lowlight pairs.

Grain

One callout on one calendar. A new KIND of emphasis is a ROW, never a schema change.

Replaces HIGHLIGHT_Start/End + LOWLIGHT_Start/End on PRODUCTION_CALENDARS. "Highlight" and "lowlight" were never concepts, just the first two rows Michael happened to need.

docs.title: Two anchor modes
docs.text:
AnchorMode Range comes from Use range typed DateStart / DateEnd spring break, a residency, dark days event matched EVENTS rows via fkStandardEvent Designer Run, Q2Q, load-in

⭐ event mode is the one that survives a reschedule. "Highlight Designer Run" resolves through EVENTS at render time, so when the run moves, the emphasis moves. A typed range would silently point at the old date.

  • event mode matches every event of that type in the production, so "all designer runs" is ONE row, not one per instance. This is the honest answer to recurrence: it works when the recurrence is a real event type, not when it is "every Monday."
  • Cost, stated plainly: two resolution predicates, one priority ladder. range resolves date-between; event resolves through the workday's events. Same sort, same winner rule, two relationships.
  • PadBefore / PadAfter extend an anchored emphasis outward in days (tech week = Q2Q anchored, padded back 3).

docs.title: Resolution rule (the load-bearing part)
docs.text:
Overlap is the NORMAL state, not an edge case — tech week sits inside the rehearsal block, opening weekend sits inside tech.

  1. Highest Priority wins.
  2. Tie → narrowest range wins. The specific thing is almost always the thing you meant to call out.
  3. Resolved LIVE through a sorted relationship from WORKDAYS (sorted Priority, then span). Not stamped: stamping would mean regenerating 68+ workday records to change one colour.

Convention that makes Priority easy: the academic calendar always loses to the production calendar visually. Spring break greyed under tech week red, never the reverse. Set academic rows low (10) and stop thinking about it. Increment by 10.

⚠️ A day with two claims prints ONE colour. MatchCount exists so the layout can mark a contested day instead of silently dropping the loser.

docs.title: Not supported in v1
docs.text:
• Half-day emphasis. Grain is the day. Ruled out by Michael.
  • Calendar-shape recurrence ("every Monday is dark"). Hand-enter the rows; accept that a one-week shift invalidates all of them. event mode covers the cases that are really event types.
  • Derived cross-production emphasis (greying another show's load-in on a shared stage). Type the range for now. This is the most likely v2 ask.

docs.title: Guards
docs.text:
• DateEnd ≥ DateStart. An inverted row matches nothing and reads as a broken feature.
  • Range must fall inside the calendar's bounds (Calendar_START → last week's end). Wrong-year entry is the boring failure that costs twenty minutes.

docs.title: Seams
docs.text:
• fkStyle → STYLES, domain emphasis. Emphasis never hardcodes a colour.
  • Label is not decoration: it is what makes a printed legend possible. The legacy file had no legend, so every colour on the 11x17 was tribal knowledge.
  • HIDE deliberately did NOT move here. Hide changes which records EXIST in the found set; emphasis only styles records that are already there. Different verb, so hide stays a stamped flag on WORKDAYS driven by a range pair on the calendar. ⚠️ The names "hide" and "lowlight" sound like one idea at two strengths and are built differently on purpose.
  • ⚠️ Lineage tradeoff: live resolution means reprinting an old PRINT_SESSIONS row renders with TODAY's emphasis rows, not the ones in effect at print time. Accepted; the paper was never authoritative.
  • 🪦 Legacy scripts checkHIGHlight / checkLOWlight are replaced by this relationship. checkHideWorkday survives.

docs.title: Events
docs.text: MAW Prose · Fall 2026

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
The current, printable event set. One row per event.

Grain

ONE row per event per production. A multi-day event is ONE row. Always the latest known state.

  • Built by UPSERT from the newest import session. Never deleted and re-created.
  • 🔴 Upsert key = TaskID + fkProduction. A CU event task can carry two shows; each calendar prints its own copy.
  • fkStandardEvent is the reporting spine: per-production churn on TaskID, season-wide "we never move these" on the standard event.
  • Unscheduled (no date) events collect at the top of week one, legacy parity.

docs.title: 🔴 SPANS STAY WHOLE (ruled by Fiona, 2026-08-08)
docs.text:
The legacy file DUPLICATED a multi-day event into one record per day (CREATE_multipleDays, flagged autoGenerated = 1) so that a day-portal could find it. That is killed.

Why it cannot survive:

  1. It breaks the upsert key. Three rows with an identical TaskID + fkProduction means the second import cannot tell an update from a duplicate. Either the key grows a date and stops being an identity, or re-import returns to delete-and-replace — and the whole history model goes with it.
  2. It destroys the change count. A span moving Mon–Wed → Tue–Thu is ONE change. Duplicated, it reads as three deletions and three creations, so WatchHash counts noise on exactly the events that move most.
  3. ⭐ autoGenerated is the tell. A flag meaning this row is not real is the schema saying the row should not exist. Same species as a convenience-copy date or a second-claimant field.
  4. The agenda gets correct for free. A span appears ONCE with a date range. Under duplication it could not — hence the autoGenerated descending sort buried in Events Agenda View SORT.

docs.title: How a day-portal finds a span
docs.text:
Not an equality on a stamped key. A multi-predicate RANGE relationship:

WORKDAYS::DATE      >=  EVENTS|span::Start_DATE
WORKDAYS::DATE      <=  EVENTS|span::End_DATE
WORKDAYS::fkCalendar =   EVENTS|span::fkCalendar

Every day inside the span sees the event, from ONE stored row. Same pattern as CALENDAR_EMPHASIS — one range-resolution mechanism used twice, not two different tricks.

  • 🔴 End_DATE must never be empty. A single-day event needs End_DATE = Start_DATE; empty means DATE <= "" and the event vanishes from every portal. Auto-enter it.
  • ⚠️ Inequality predicates cannot use a stored index like equality can, so a span portal is slower. On a 68-day grid with ~120 events this is a non-issue.
  • 🚪 Escape hatch, NOT built: if performance ever bites, generate an EVENT_DAYS join (one row per event-day, rebuilt at import, never edited, never the source of truth). That buys duplication's SPEED without its IDENTITY problem. Named here so nobody re-invents autoGenerated under pressure.

docs.title: Open, from Beckett
docs.text:
• ⬜ A span crossing a HIDDEN day renders on both sides of a gap and reads as continuous. Duplication handled this by accident (no row was made for a hidden day). Range joins have no opinion. Decide what the page should show.
  • ⬜ A span running past the calendar bounds truncates silently — the page understates duration with no marker.
  • ⬜ Visual continuation. A five-day load-in prints its name in five cells with no "continues" affordance. Legacy had the same problem, so not a regression, but nobody has specified it.

docs.title: EVENTS_workday
docs.text: MAW Prose · Fall 2026

docs.title: EVENTS_workday
docs.text:
One row per event per day. A projection, rebuilt at import, never edited.

Grain

One event on one workday. A five-day load-in is five rows.

docs.title: Why it exists — and it is NOT a performance hedge
docs.text:
It was first offered as an escape hatch in case the range join proved slow. Michael found the real reason: a list view repeats per RECORD, so a one-row span cannot produce three agenda lines, and a WORKDAYS portal is fixed-height. The agenda REQUIRES this table.

The split that keeps it safe:

Table Holds Layer [EVENTS] IDENTITY — the upsert key, history, change counts canonical EVENTS_workday a PROJECTION for reports disposable

Both agenda shapes then come free: base a report HERE for one line per day, base it on EVENTS for one line with a date range.

docs.title: When it is built
docs.text:
At import, as the LAST step. Never at print.

  • Printing must not be a write. A read-only report that mutates data cannot run on a locked file, cannot run twice safely, and turns "reprint that PDF" into a schema operation.
  • Rebuild triggers: an import lands · the grid regenerates (page bounds or WeekStartDay moved) · on demand.
  • Full delete-and-rebuild for the calendar in scope. Safe precisely because it holds no identity, nothing points at it, and nothing is lost. See [Projection Law].

docs.title: ⭐ It SKIPS hidden days
docs.text:
A span crossing a hidden range (spring break) gets no rows for those days. Two things fall out of that:

  • Beckett's continuous-span problem solves itself on the agenda — the gap is real because the rows are absent, rather than a span silently reading as unbroken.
  • DayIndex / DayCount count working days, so "day 2 of 3" reads the way a person would say it.

docs.title: GLOBAL_USE
docs.text:
Session state only. The hub lens.

Grain

Singleton. One record, all global-storage fields.

  • Split globals by LIFETIME, not by topic. This holds only what is true for THIS user in THIS session: which production is selected, which semester.
  • Globals are per-user per-session in a hosted file, which is exactly what a lens is.
  • 🚫 No GLOBAL_EXPORT_SETTINGS. Highlight/lowlight/hide ranges are facts about a specific show's calendar, so they live on PRODUCTION_CALENDARS. As globals they get retyped every reprint.
  • 🚫 FilePathName needs no storage. It is Get ( FilePath ).
  • 🚫 SETUP is killed. Once production config became real records and print config moved to the calendar, nothing was left in it. The legacy SETUP was 20 fields / 1 record / almost all global — which is why the old file could only ever hold ONE production at a time.

One physical place we can point at. Todd Theatre, the scene shop, Rehearsal 2.

docs.title: 🔒 RULED 2026-08-08 — VENUES is dead, it lives here
docs.text:
Michael: "venues is my elevation of locations — for when we get into assigning events to rooms."

⭐ LOCATIONS is not a rename of VENUES, it is the LEVEL BELOW it. A venue is the building you produce in; a room is where a call actually happens. One table holds both, distinguished by fkLocationType.

  • PRODUCTIONS.fkVenue → LOCATIONS. The field name stays — it states which ROLE the location plays for this production, which is real information the join needs.
  • 🚫 Do not create a separate VENUES table. Two tables for one concept is the second-claimant problem; this session killed four instances of that shape.

docs.title: Why the table exists at all: events in rooms
docs.text:
⬜ EVENTS.fkLocation is the stated destination, not a nice-to-have. "Assigning events to rooms" is Michael's own reason for elevating this.

  • The legacy calendar had no location on an event, which is why the printed grid cannot answer "where is this call."
  • ⚠️ Unverified: whether ClickUp emits a location on an event task. If it does not, this is a manual field and cannot be part of the import. Check a live export before promising it.
  • Crew calls need a report location (Milo's open question). If crew calls ever land, they resolve here.
  • Room assignment implies conflict detection eventually — two events, one room, one time. Not v1, but it is the reason a room is an entity rather than a text field.

docs.title: ⚠️ This is currently a value list wearing a table
docs.text:
As shipped it holds Name + the five audit fields and nothing else. Your own rule (data-standards.md): metadata beyond display value → table; otherwise value list.

By that test this should be a value list today. Keep it as a table only if it earns metadata, and there are real candidates:

  • SortOrder — so a picker groups by kind instead of alphabetically
  • IsBookable / RequiresReservation — a venue needs scheduling, a storage closet does not
  • DefaultCapacity
  • IsOnCampus

If none of those ever arrive, this is six fields doing a value list's job. Not a reason to delete it now — it is a reason to add the one field that justifies it, which is SortOrder.

docs.title: Where it sits in the print hub
docs.text:
Table Is Lifetime PRINT_PRESETS HOW to output reused forever [PRINT_SETS] WHAT to output, batched reused; one is scratch [PRINT_SET_ITEMS] one output + its overrides per line [PRINT_SESSIONS] WHAT HAPPENED one per produced PDF

🔴 A preset is NOT created per print. That was considered and refused 2026-08-08: minting one on entry would produce hundreds of near-identical rows and destroy the only thing that makes it a preset — being reusable across shows. The per-entry record is a scratch PRINT_SET instead.

docs.title: DocumentType (added 2026-08-08)
docs.text: A preset is scoped to a KIND of document. A calendar preset has no ShowVacancies; a contact-sheet preset has no WeekStartDay. Without this field, one flat option list serves every document and the table becomes legacy SETUP again.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
• Presets are reusable across productions. fkCalendar is NULLABLE: null = a house preset ("11x17 Full Company"), set = a one-off saved for this calendar.
  • This is what makes department filtering (the legacy next-step: "only light lab tasks") a preset row rather than a code change.
  • Legacy parity: the two PRINT_SET...Rlandscape scripts and exportORprint are what this table replaces as DATA.
  • ⬜ Department filtering needs a department field on EVENTS that does not exist yet — Corey's Production Note labels field is the candidate, unresolved (see [ClickUp Integration]).

docs.title: PRINT_SESSIONS
docs.text:
One export. Where editions live.

Grain

One exported calendar. Edition lives HERE, never on an import.

  • Michael's rule: import sessions are inherently the snapshot; an edition is a published artifact plus live awareness of where we are in the process. That is the export side.
  • Consequence: watermark stops being a field you flip on the calendar and becomes a value on the run. FIRST / REVISED / UPDATED styled via STYLES, domain watermark.
  • Gives print-to-print diffing two stable endpoints, so "what moved since last print" no longer depends on a ClickUp automation firing.
  • Reissue is ROUTINE, not rare — zOLD/ holds 9 dated versions for Thought Crime, 8 for The Christians. Each reissue is a staffing milestone, not a formatting pass.

docs.title: PRINT_SETS
docs.text: MAW Prose · Fall 2026

docs.title: PRINT_SETS
docs.text:
A batch of documents to produce together. The print hub.

Grain

One named batch of documents produced together. A HEADER; the actual doc x preset pairs are [PRINT_SET_ITEMS].

Build your print set from the available docs, editions, presets, overrides and formats. One run, N PDFs.

docs.title: 🔴 The legacy file already had this, written as CODE
docs.text: EXPORT Calendar Set prints four outputs in a hardcoded sequence — 8.5x11 landscape, 8.5x11 portrait, 11x17 expanded, agenda. That IS a print set with no table. Same discovery as the six stored production INFO scripts being the PRODUCTIONS table written as code. Adding a row is now how you add an output.

docs.title: Header / line split, and why overrides live on the LINE
docs.text:
A set legitimately contains the same document at two presets, or two documents sharing one preset. If overrides sat on the header, every line would inherit the same ones and a set could only ever mean one thing. So:

Table Holds PRINT_SETS the name, the scratch/template flags, the calendar it belongs to PRINT_SET_ITEMS one row per output: doc type, preset, edition, sort, its own overrides

docs.title: ⭐ SCRATCH: one reserved set, reset from a TEMPLATE set
docs.text:
bool_IsScratch marks the single working set the print hub lands on. It is never saved and always overwritten, so it needs no naming and produces no clutter.

bool_IsDefaultTemplate marks the set the scratch RESETS FROM. Reset = delete the scratch's items, duplicate the template's items onto it. One reserved template, one reserved scratch, per calendar.

🔴 RESET ON ENTRY, not on close. Reset-at-close looks tidier and fails the first time the app quits unexpectedly, leaving yesterday's staging as today's starting point — a stale-state bug with no symptom. Entry-time reset is idempotent and self-healing: whatever happened last time, opening the hub gives you the template. Resetting at close as well is harmless but redundant.

⚠️ This retires GLOBAL_EXPORT_VARIABLES (considered and dropped 2026-08-08). Staging is a RECORD you can see, sort and re-run, so GLOBAL_USE keeps one field — g_fkPrintSet — and no per-field global staging exists.

  • Globals were per-user and collision-free, which was their one real advantage. Single-operator year, so a shared scratch record is acceptable — two people staging at once would fight over it. Noted, not solved.

docs.title: Running a set
docs.text: N items produce N [PRINT_SESSIONS] rows, sharing one run stamp. Receipt granularity stays per-PDF (each has its own path and edition) while the SET is the thing you re-run.

docs.title: PRINT_SET_ITEMS
docs.text:
One output in a print set. Where overrides live.

Grain

ONE produced document. doc type x preset x edition, plus this run's overrides.

docs.title: Overrides live here, and empty means INHERIT
docs.text:
The resolution rule, and it is the whole contract:

If ( IsEmpty ( item::override_x ) ; preset::x ; item::override_x )

🔴 Do NOT copy every preset field down onto the line. If every field is always populated you can never tell an OVERRIDE from an INHERITANCE, the preset stops mattering, and you have built a shadow PRINT_PRESETS that drifts. Only fields a human actually flips at print time get an override column.

Three categories, and the third is why staging needs a home at all:

Category Example Where preset-only, never overridden ExportFolder, IsDefault PRINT_PRESETS only genuinely overridable per run output size, week start, legend override column here session-only, no preset to inherit from edition, note here only

docs.title: 🔒 The PII fields are not conveniences
docs.text: Once contacts land, bool_IncludeContactInfo and bool_Anonymize decide whether a PDF full of student phone numbers leaves the building. They snapshot onto PRINT_SESSIONS so there is a record of what was actually on the page you handed out.

docs.title: DocumentType is what keeps the override list small
docs.text: A calendar has no ShowVacancies; a contact sheet has no WeekStartDay. The preset carries the type-specific defaults, so the override set exposed here is whatever the CURRENT document type actually uses. Without DocumentType this table drifts into one flat list of every option for every document — which is legacy SETUP rebuilt one table over.

docs.title: PRODUCTION_CALENDARS
docs.text: MAW Prose · Fall 2026

docs.title: PRODUCTION_CALENDARS
docs.text:
Joining entity to output.

Grain

One calendar per production per semester. Exceptions: the same production in two different time blocks.

  • Entity vs output. PRODUCTIONS is the entity, so nothing about how a page looks goes there.
  • date_NeededFirst / date_NeededLast are page bounds, not schedule facts — nothing happens on "last date needed." Legacy fed it into CalendarDaysNeeded, which sized the grid.
  • First rehearsal + opening are read through fkProduction. Never copied down — a copy diverges silently and the symptom is a printed page quietly a week off.
  • fkSemester is a property of the CALENDAR. Two calendars for one show means two semesters.

docs.title: HIDE is real, and it stays
docs.text:
HIDE_Start / HIDE_End grey a range out entirely — the flag stamps onto WORKDAYS and those days do not print. Legacy evidence: Secretary INFO sets 3/7/27 → 3/13/27, which is spring break.

Hide is existence, not styling: it changes which records are in the found set. CALENDAR_EMPHASIS only styles records already there.

docs.title: 🔴 The grid moved to the PRINT layer (2026-08-08, Michael)
docs.text:
Week start is a PRINT spec, not a calendar fact. date_CalendarStart and bool_StartOnMonday are gone from this table.

  • WeekStartDay (1–7) lives on PRINT_PRESETS, snapshotted onto PRINT_SESSIONS.
  • 🪦 The boolean is dead. It cannot express Tuesday, which is the actual answer — a theatre week runs Tue→Mon because Monday is the dark day. Sunday-or-Monday was never the real domain, and the legacy startOnMon (a TEXT field compared against = 1) was wrong twice over.
  • date_CalendarStart is derived: the WeekStartDay falling on or before PRODUCTIONS::DateFirstRehearsal.

⚠️ The consequence is structural: WEEKS and WORKDAYS are DISPOSABLE. The same calendar rendered Tue-start vs Sun-start produces different week rows, so the grid cannot be generated once and reused. It is rebuilt per print, exactly like EVENTS_workday.

Three layers:

Layer Tables Rule Canonical PRODUCTIONS · PRODUCTION_CALENDARS · EVENTS · CALENDAR_EMPHASIS · ROLES · ASSIGNMENTS · LOCATIONS · PRODUCERS typed, edited, holds identity Projection WEEKS · WORKDAYS · EVENTS_workday generated, disposable, rebuilt, NEVER edited Archive import_EVENTS · import_SESSIONS · PRINT_SESSIONS append-only, never trashed

🔒 The projection is never hand-edited — see projection-law.md. Rebuild is therefore a dumb delete-and-regenerate with no preservation pass.

docs.text:
• Highlight / lowlight ranges → CALENDAR_EMPHASIS
  • Watermark → PRINT_SESSIONS (it belongs to a run)
  • Export settings + week start → PRINT_PRESETS

docs.title: STANDARD_EVENTS
docs.text: MAW Prose · Fall 2026

docs.title: STANDARD_EVENTS
docs.text:
Canonical cross-season event types. The reporting spine and the skin layer.

Grain

One kind of event that recurs across productions and seasons. Load In, Q2Q, Designer Run, Photo Call.

docs.title: Nothing breaks if this table is empty
docs.text:
Michael's rule, and it is the important one: every imported event is handled elegantly whether or not it matches a standard event. fkStandardEvent is nullable on both [EVENTS] and [import_EVENTS]. An unmatched event still prints.

What a match BUYS:

  • The season-report axis. Per-production churn counts on TaskID; season-wide "we never move these" counts on fkStandardEvent. ⭐ The second is impossible to retrofit, which is why the link goes in from day one rather than when the report is wanted.
  • Skinning beyond the raw ClickUp status token.
  • Anchored emphasis. An event-mode [CALENDAR_EMPHASIS] row points HERE, so "highlight Designer Run" resolves through events at render time and moves when the run moves.
  • Workflow notes attached to a canonical definition rather than to one instance.

docs.title: How an import matches
docs.text:
🚫 Not by fuzzy name matching — that mis-buckets silently and nobody notices.

Michael declined a ClickUp-side canonical-type dropdown, so matching is a CROSSWALK: raw event name → fkStandardEvent, with unmatched rows landing in a queue that gets resolved once by hand. It learns instead of guessing.

docs.title: import_EVENTS
docs.text: MAW Prose · Fall 2026

docs.title: import_EVENTS
docs.text:
Raw ClickUp pulls, append-only.

Grain

One event, as it appeared in ONE import session. Not one event. Re-importing the same task appends a NEW row; it never edits the old one.

docs.title: Append-only
docs.text: Nothing in the app edits or deletes a row here. This table IS the revision history — order by session and the timeline reads itself. That is why there is no separate EVENT_TRACKING / revisions table.

docs.title: 🔴 Upsert key = TaskID + fkProduction, never TaskID alone
docs.text:
URITP Productions in ClickUp is a labels (multi-select) field, so one event task can legitimately carry two shows. Each production's calendar prints its own copy, so the same TaskID must be able to exist twice — once per show.

Keying the upsert into EVENTS on TaskID alone means show two silently overwrites show one. Compound the key.

Mitigation on the ClickUp side: make the export view per-production, so one import session = one show. A cross-listed event then arrives in both sessions, which is correct.

docs.title: WatchHash
docs.text:
Auto-enter calculation, "Do not replace existing value" CHECKED. A plain calculation field recomputes, which rewrites history the first time the formula is touched.

Let ( ~d = "|" ;
  GetAsText ( Start_TIMESTAMP ) & ~d &
  GetAsText ( End_TIMESTAMP )   & ~d &
  Event_Name
)

The delimiter is load-bearing: without it "12" & "3" and "1" & "23" collide.

Watched set: start/end timestamps + event name. NOT modification stamps, style, or row order — otherwise "Q2Q moved 12 times" really means "you reimported 12 times." Same hash as the prior session for that TaskID = no real change. Counting distinct hashes = counting real changes.

docs.title: Timestamps are STORED, not unstored
docs.text: An unstored calculation re-evaluates on read, so fixing the parse formula later silently rewrites every historical row and moves every change count.

docs.title: Raw_Payload
docs.text: The whole original row/JSON, kept verbatim. An unmapped ClickUp field that turns out to matter in six months is already in the table instead of needing a re-import that can no longer be reproduced.

docs.title: What NOT to port from the old file
docs.text: The legacy ProductionCalendar Format table spent 8 of 23 fields parsing text dates (Start Date IMPORT / End Date IMPORT were TEXT, chewed by MiddleWords / LeftWords). That is CSV damage, not schema. The API pull deletes all of it — including the month-walk date-overflow trap, which lives in code that should not exist here.

docs.title: import_SESSIONS
docs.text:
One pull from ClickUp.

Grain

One pull. The session IS the snapshot — nothing here ever carries an edition.

  • Serves BOTH pipes: calendar events and contact-sheet assignments come down the same way. The two-projects framing is really one import layer with two renderers.
  • One session = one production. The export view is per-production, so a cross-listed event arrives in both sessions. That is correct, not duplication.
  • fkProduction is declared by the operator at import. Any row whose CU token does not resolve to it gets flagged, never silently filed — that is how a renamed label gets caught on day one.
  • RowCount is the reconciliation check. Rows in the file vs rows landed.
  • Editions belong to PRINT_SESSIONS, on the export side. Import never has one.
